adult-sexting-consent-risk-guide.en:
Imagine two 25-year-olds, one in Bengaluru and one in Lucknow, a year into a long-distance relationship. Photos are exchanged one night. Nobody has done anything wrong. A year later they have broken up, and an old phone has gone to a cousin with the gallery still signed in to the cloud.

Many leaks begin with an image that outlived the trust it was sent in, or an account that was never who it claimed to be. This guide is for adults. It will not tell you not to sext, or that it is safe. Its rules lower the risk; none removes it. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Adults only: what the law allows and forbids

POCSO defines a child as anyone under 18 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], and Section 67B of the IT Act punishes creating, collecting, browsing, downloading or exchanging sexually explicit material depicting a child with up to five years in prison and a fine of up to Rs 10 lakh on first conviction [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. There is no "we both agreed" exception, not even for two 17-year-olds. If either of you is under 18, nothing below applies.

For adults, the law draws its line at consent, in two places. Section 77 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) makes sharing a private image of a woman without her consent the offence of voyeurism, even if she agreed to the image being taken, with one to three years in prison on first conviction [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 66E of the IT Act protects any person: capturing, publishing or transmitting an image of someone's private area without consent carries up to three years, a fine of up to Rs 2 lakh, or both [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. For men, and for queer and transgender people whom Section 77's wording leaves out, 66E does the work.

Now the uncomfortable part. No Indian statute says that adults may sext. The IT Act's obscenity sections, 67 and 67A, punish transmitting obscene or sexually explicit material and do not mention consent at all [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. The law gives no written guarantee; its weight falls on whoever sends an image where it was never meant to go.

## Consent before you send, and before they keep

- **Ask first.** "Can I send you something?" is one line. An explicit image nobody asked for is not flirting; it is the transmission Section 67 punishes, with up to three years on first conviction [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].
- **A yes is narrow.** Yes to receiving is not yes to saving, screenshotting or showing a friend. Section 77's Explanation 2 separates consent to capture from consent to dissemination to "third persons", [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The provision speaks of third persons and sets no minimum audience, so do not assume that showing one friend is safe.
- **Pressure is not consent.** "If you trusted me, you would" is a demand. Nobody owes a partner an image, and a no needs no reason.
- **Consent runs out.** Last month's photo does not make the next request automatic, and "please delete it" is not an opening offer.

## Verify the person, secure the device

The first risk is that the person is not the person. In a 2023 Snap survey of more than 6,000 teens and young adults in six countries including India, 65% said they or their friends had been targeted in sextortion schemes through catfishing or hacking [[weprotect-snap-sextortion-research-2023]]. Read it with care: a platform commissioned it, it pools six countries, and "or their friends" pushes the figure up. It still says fake and stolen accounts are everyday tools.

So send nothing to anyone you have not seen live. A video call is a low bar, and a fake profile will keep finding reasons to avoid it.

The second risk is the device.

- **Cloud backup.** Photo apps copy the gallery to every device signed in to the same account, including a shared family tablet. Turn sync off for those images, or use the phone's locked folder.
- **Disappearing messages.** "View once" stops casual saving. It does not stop a second phone photographing the screen.
- **The frame.** Leave out your face, tattoos, birthmarks, jewellery and any recognisable room. An image that cannot be tied to you is a weaker weapon.
- **Handing the phone over.** Before a repair shop, a resale or a hand-me-down, erase the images and sign out of the cloud account.

## Storage, deletion and the breakup conversation

Agree on deletion while things are good: images go when either person asks, and when the relationship ends. Say it in a message, so it exists in writing.

Deleting means the chat, the gallery, the "recently deleted" bin, the cloud copy, the chat backup and the old phone in a drawer.

At a breakup, ask once, in writing: please delete the photos I sent you, including backups, and confirm. You cannot check the answer, which is why the frame rule matters more. But if the image ever surfaces, that message shows the other person knew they had no permission.

> Trust is a reason to send an image. It is not a place to store one.

And if you hold someone else's images after a breakup, delete them unasked. Keeping them "just in case" is keeping leverage.

## If trust breaks: StopNCII and the law

Sending an image to a partner who asked for it is not what the law goes after. Sharing it without consent is. If someone threatens to post, do not pay and do not send more.

1. **Block re-uploads.** StopNCII.org, run by the UK charity SWGfL, creates a digital fingerprint of the image and shares only that with partner platforms. By November 2025 it was protecting 2 million images and had supported more than 785,000 cases [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]]. It covers images taken at 18 or older, and only partner platforms act on it. For images taken before 18, NCMEC's Take It Down does the same job [[ncmec-take-it-down]].
2. **Report to the platform.** Since 20 February 2026, platforms must remove nude, sexual or morphed images of a person within two hours of that person's complaint [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].
3. **Report the crime.** Call 1930 or file on cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]], and take a written complaint naming Section 77 or Section 66E to a police station.

A leak or a threat can feel overwhelming; if it does, call the Tele-MANAS mental health helpline on 14416. Two adults who choose to share images have done nothing shameful. The law is written for the person who breaks that choice.
adult-sexting-consent-risk-guide.hg:
Socho, do log hain, dono 25 saal ke, ek Bengaluru mein aur ek Lucknow mein, aur unka long-distance relationship ek saal se chal raha hai. Ek raat photos exchange hoti hain. Kisi ne kuch galat nahi kiya. Ek saal baad breakup ho chuka hai, aur purana phone ek cousin ko de diya gaya hai, jisme gallery ab bhi cloud mein signed in hai.

Bahut se leaks aise hi shuru hote hain: ek image se jo us bharose se zyada chali jisme woh bheji gayi thi, ya ek account se jo kabhi woh tha hi nahi jo hone ka daava karta tha. Yeh guide adults ke liye hai. Yeh na tumhe sext karne se rokegi, na yeh kahegi ki yeh safe hai. Iske rules risk kam karte hain; koi bhi rule risk khatam nahi karta. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Sirf adults: law kya allow karta hai aur kya nahi

POCSO ke hisaab se 18 se kam ka har insaan child hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], aur IT Act ka Section 67B child ko dikhane wale sexually explicit material ko banane, collect karne, browse karne, download karne ya exchange karne pe first conviction mein paanch saal tak ki jail aur Rs 10 lakh tak ka fine lagata hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. "Hum dono raazi the" wala koi exception nahi hai, do 17 saal ke logon ke liye bhi nahi. Agar tum dono mein se koi bhi 18 se kam hai, toh neeche likha kuch bhi tum pe laagu nahi hota.

Adults ke liye law apni line consent pe kheenchta hai, do jagah. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 77 kisi aurat ki private image uski consent ke bina share karne ko voyeurism ka offence banata hai, chahe image lene ke liye usne haan kaha ho, aur first conviction pe ek se teen saal ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. IT Act ka Section 66E har insaan ko protect karta hai: kisi ke private area ki image bina consent capture, publish ya transmit karne pe teen saal tak ki jail, Rs 2 lakh tak ka fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Men ke liye, aur un queer aur transgender logon ke liye jinhe Section 77 ke shabd bahar chhod dete hain, kaam 66E hi karta hai.

Ab woh baat jo uncomfortable hai. Koi bhi Indian statute yeh nahi kehta ki adults sext kar sakte hain. IT Act ke obscenity sections, 67 aur 67A, obscene ya sexually explicit material bhejne ko punish karte hain aur consent ka zikr tak nahi karte [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Law koi likhit guarantee nahi deta; uska wazan us pe padta hai jo image ko wahan bhejta hai jahan use kabhi jaana hi nahi tha.

## Bhejne se pehle consent, aur unke rakhne se pehle bhi

- **Pehle poocho.** "Kya main tumhe kuch bhejun?" bas ek line hai. Bina maange bheji gayi explicit image flirting nahi hai; yeh wahi transmission hai jise Section 67 punish karta hai, first conviction pe teen saal tak ki jail ke saath [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].
- **Haan ka daayra chhota hota hai.** Receive karne ke liye haan ka matlab save karne, screenshot lene ya kisi dost ko dikhane ke liye haan nahi hai. Section 77 ka Explanation 2 capture ki consent ko "third persons" tak dissemination ki consent se alag karta hai, [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Provision third persons ki baat karta hai aur koi minimum audience tay nahi karta, isliye yeh mat maano ki ek dost ko dikhana safe hai.
- **Pressure consent nahi hai.** "Agar tumhe mujh pe bharosa hota, toh tum bhej dete" ek demand hai. Koi bhi apne partner ko image dene ka karzdaar nahi hai, aur na kehne ke liye koi wajah deni zaroori nahi.
- **Consent khatam bhi hoti hai.** Pichhle mahine ki photo agli request ko automatic nahi bana deti, aur "please delete kar do" koi mol-bhaav ki shuruaat nahi hai.

## Insaan ko verify karo, device ko secure karo

Pehla risk yeh hai ki saamne wala woh insaan hai hi nahi. 2023 ke ek Snap survey mein, jisme India samet chhe deshon ke 6,000 se zyada teens aur young adults the, 65% ne kaha ki unhe ya unke doston ko catfishing ya hacking ke zariye sextortion schemes mein target kiya gaya [[weprotect-snap-sextortion-research-2023]]. Ise dhyaan se padho: survey ek platform ne karwaya tha, isme chhe desh mile hue hain, aur "ya unke doston ko" number ko upar le jaata hai. Phir bhi yeh batata hai ki fake aur chori kiye hue accounts roz ke auzaar hain.

Toh jise live nahi dekha, use kuch mat bhejo. Video call ek chhoti si shart hai, aur fake profile usse bachne ke bahane dhoondhti rahegi.

Doosra risk device hai.

- **Cloud backup.** Photo apps gallery ko us har device pe copy kar dete hain jo usi account mein signed in hai, ghar ke shared tablet pe bhi. Un images ke liye sync band karo, ya phone ka locked folder use karo.
- **Disappearing messages.** "View once" casual saving ko rokta hai. Doosre phone se screen ki photo lene ko nahi rokta.
- **Frame.** Chehra, tattoos, birthmarks, jewellery aur pehchana jaane wala kamra bahar rakho. Jo image tumse jodi nahi ja sakti, woh kamzor hathiyaar hai.
- **Phone kisi aur ke haath mein dena.** Repair shop pe dene, bechne ya ghar mein kisi ko dene se pehle images erase karo aur cloud account se sign out karo.

## Storage, deletion aur breakup wali baat

Jab sab theek chal raha ho, tabhi deletion pe baat tay kar lo: dono mein se koi bhi kahe toh images jaayengi, aur relationship khatam ho tab bhi. Yeh ek message mein kaho, taaki yeh likhit mein rahe.

Delete karne ka matlab hai chat, gallery, "recently deleted" bin, cloud copy, chat backup aur drawer mein pada purana phone.

Breakup pe ek baar, likh kar kaho: jo photos maine bheji thi unhe delete kar do, backups samet, aur confirm karo. Jawab tum check nahi kar sakte, isiliye frame wala rule zyada kaam ka hai. Lekin agar image kabhi saamne aati hai, toh yahi message dikhata hai ki doosre insaan ko pata tha ki uske paas permission nahi thi.

> Bharosa image bhejne ki wajah ho sakta hai. Image rakhne ki jagah nahi.

Aur agar breakup ke baad kisi aur ki images tumhare paas hain, toh bina kahe delete kar do. Unhe "just in case" rakhna kisi pe leverage rakhna hai.

## Agar bharosa toot jaaye: StopNCII aur law

Jis partner ne maangi ho use image bhejna woh cheez nahi jiske peeche law jaata hai. Use bina consent share karna offence hai. Agar koi post karne ki dhamki de, toh paise mat do aur aur images mat bhejo.

1. **Re-uploads block karo.** StopNCII.org, jise UK ki charity SWGfL chalati hai, image ka digital fingerprint banata hai aur partner platforms ke saath sirf wahi share karta hai. November 2025 tak yeh 2 million images ko protect kar raha tha aur 785,000 se zyada cases mein support de chuka tha [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]]. Yeh un images ke liye hai jo 18 ya usse zyada ki umar mein li gayi, aur is pe sirf partner platforms action lete hain. 18 se pehle li gayi images ke liye yahi kaam NCMEC ka Take It Down karta hai [[ncmec-take-it-down]].
2. **Platform pe report karo.** 20 February 2026 se platforms ko kisi insaan ki nude, sexual ya morphed images us insaan ki complaint ke do ghante ke andar hatani hoti hain [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].
3. **Crime report karo.** 1930 pe call karo ya cybercrime.gov.in pe file karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]], aur Section 77 ya Section 66E ka naam lekar police station mein likhit complaint do.

Leak ya dhamki bahut bhaari lag sakti hai; agar aisa ho, toh Tele-MANAS mental health helpline 14416 pe call karo. Jo do adults apni marzi se images share karte hain, unhone koi sharm ki baat nahi ki. Law us insaan ke liye likha gaya hai jo us marzi ko todta hai.

after-you-call-1930-cybercrime-portal.en:
Imagine filing a complaint on cybercrime.gov.in late one night about a fake profile carrying your photos. You get an acknowledgement number. Then you wait. What happens next is the part nobody explains. In 2024 the national portal registered 22.68 lakh complaints [[ls-uq432-2025]]. Police across India registered 1,01,928 cyber crime FIRs [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Here is where a complaint goes. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Built for women and children: the portal's 2019 promise

The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal went live as a pilot on 30 August 2019. It was meant to take complaints about all cyber crimes "with specific focus on crimes against women, children", especially child sexual abuse material and online content showing rapes or gang rapes, and was dedicated to the nation with the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) on 10 January 2020 [[pib-mha-i4c-launch-2020]].

That focus produced numbers. About 1.94 lakh complaints about child sexual abuse material and rape or gang-rape content had been reported on the portal by 30 April 2024, the Women and Child Development Minister told the Rajya Sabha [[pib-wcd-ccpwc-2024]]. That count is cumulative since 2019, and it counts complaints, not FIRs. Today the portal sits alongside 1930, a toll-free helpline set up to help people lodge online cyber complaints [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

## 4.52 lakh to 22.68 lakh: the complaint flood

Here are the Home Ministry's figures for portal complaints [[ls-uq432-2025]] beside NCRB's count of cyber crime FIRs [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]] [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]:

| Year | Portal complaints | Cyber crime FIRs |
|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 4.52 lakh | 52,974 |
| 2022 | 10.29 lakh | 65,893 |
| 2023 | 15.96 lakh | 86,420 |
| 2024 | 22.68 lakh | 1,01,928 |

Complaints grew five-fold in three years, with a 42.08% rise in 2024 alone [[ls-uq432-2025]]. FIRs nearly doubled. The two series count different things, so the gap is not a tally of ignored crimes; NCRB itself warns that more registration is not the same as more crime [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. But the shape is plain: in 2024 the portal logged more than 20 complaints for every cyber crime FIR.

Money dominates what becomes a case. Of the 2024 FIRs, fraud was the motive in 73,987 (72.6%), sexual exploitation in 3,190 (3.1%) and extortion in 2,536 (2.5%) [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. If FIRs are a guide, the crimes the portal was built around are now a small share of the system's work.

## A complaint is not an FIR: where cases stall

The portal itself investigates nothing. A complaint filed there is handled by the police of the state or union territory concerned, and that force decides whether to register an FIR [[cybercrime-portal]]. It is also the step a complainant sees least of.

In principle, the law is clear. In Lalita Kumari (2013), a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court held that registering an FIR is mandatory when information discloses a cognizable offence, and that officers who refuse must face action [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]]. Since 1 July 2024, though, Section 173(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita lets police, with a Deputy Superintendent's permission, hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days before registering offences punishable with three to under seven years [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Offences such as stalking and voyeurism, online or offline, may fall inside that window.

After registration the funnel narrows again. In 2024 police filed chargesheets in 31.9% of the cyber crime cases they disposed of [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Courts had 99,693 cyber crime cases before them that year; they completed trials in 4,567 and convicted in 2,596, and 90.9% were still pending at year end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These are different cases at different stages, not one group followed through. Still, the shape is a funnel: lakhs of complaints at the top, a few thousand convictions at the bottom.

## The tracker survivors were promised

In Mrs X v. Union of India (26 April 2023), the Delhi High Court directed that the portal carry a status tracker for complaints about non-consensual intimate images, that a round-the-clock helpline for such complaints be set up, and that search engines use a token-based system so de-indexed images do not resurface [[delhihc-mrs-x-2023]].

A tracker answers the problem this investigation keeps meeting: silence after filing. A survivor needs to know whether a police station has the complaint, whether an FIR exists, and whether anyone asked the platform to act. A November 2025 procedure from the Ministry of Electronics and IT then required platforms to remove flagged images and I4C to keep a secure hash bank of them [[pib-meity-ncii-sop-2025]].

The court set the standard; hold the system to it. If you cannot see what has happened to your complaint, write to the police handling it, quote your acknowledgement number (and, for intimate images, the 2023 order), and ask in writing whether an FIR has been registered. Your firmest rights attach to an FIR, not a portal complaint: once there is an investigation, police must tell you how it is progressing within 90 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## How to file so your complaint counts

- **Collect first:** screenshots showing date and time, the links themselves, account names, phone numbers and payment IDs.
- **Do not handle child abuse images:** report the links instead. The IT Act punishes browsing, downloading or exchanging child sexual abuse material, not only publishing it [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].
- **Write it in order:** what happened, when, on which platform, by which account, and what you want: removal and a police case.
- **Ask for the FIR:** under Section 173 BNSS you can report at any police station, wherever the offence took place, or electronically, signing within three days, and you must get a free copy [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. If a station refuses, you can write to the Superintendent of Police and then go to a magistrate [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Run removal separately:** since 20 February 2026, platforms must take down intimate images within two hours of a complaint [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

A portal complaint tells the state that something happened. An FIR obliges it to act. Leave with both.
after-you-call-1930-cybercrime-portal.hg:
Socho tum raat ko cybercrime.gov.in pe ek fake profile ke baare mein complaint file karte ho, jis pe tumhari photos lagi hain. Tumhe ek acknowledgement number milta hai. Phir intezaar. Uske baad kya hota hai, yeh koi nahi samjhata. 2024 mein national portal pe 22.68 lakh complaints register hui [[ls-uq432-2025]]. Poore India mein police ne 1,01,928 cyber crime FIRs register ki [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Yahan dekho ki complaint kahan jaati hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Women aur bachchon ke liye bana: portal ka 2019 wala vaada

National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal 30 August 2019 ko pilot ke taur pe shuru hua. Iska kaam tha saare cyber crimes ki complaints lena, "with specific focus on crimes against women, children", yaani women aur bachchon ke khilaf crimes pe khaas focus ke saath, khaaskar child sexual abuse material aur rape ya gang rape dikhane wale online content pe. 10 January 2020 ko ise Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) ke saath desh ko dedicate kiya gaya [[pib-mha-i4c-launch-2020]].

Is focus ka asar numbers mein dikha. 30 April 2024 tak portal pe child sexual abuse material aur rape ya gang-rape content ke baare mein lagbhag 1.94 lakh complaints report ho chuki thi, Women and Child Development Minister ne Rajya Sabha ko bataya [[pib-wcd-ccpwc-2024]]. Yeh 2019 se ab tak ka total hai, aur yeh complaints hain, FIRs nahi. Aaj portal ke saath 1930 bhi hai, ek toll-free helpline jo online cyber complaints darj karwane mein madad ke liye bani hai [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

## 4.52 lakh se 22.68 lakh: complaints ki baadh

Yeh rahe portal complaints ke Home Ministry wale figures [[ls-uq432-2025]], NCRB ke cyber crime FIR count ke saath [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]] [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]:

| Saal | Portal complaints | Cyber crime FIRs |
|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 4.52 lakh | 52,974 |
| 2022 | 10.29 lakh | 65,893 |
| 2023 | 15.96 lakh | 86,420 |
| 2024 | 22.68 lakh | 1,01,928 |

Teen saal mein complaints paanch guna ho gayi, aur sirf 2024 mein 42.08% badhi [[ls-uq432-2025]]. FIRs lagbhag doguni hui. Dono series alag cheezein ginti hain, isliye yeh gap ignore kiye gaye crimes ki ginti nahi hai; NCRB khud warn karta hai ki zyada registration ka matlab zyada crime nahi hota [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Phir bhi tasveer saaf hai: 2024 mein portal pe har cyber crime FIR ke muqable 20 se zyada complaints aayi.

Case kya banta hai, is pe paisa haavi hai. 2024 ki FIRs mein 73,987 (72.6%) ka motive fraud tha, 3,190 (3.1%) ka sexual exploitation aur 2,536 (2.5%) ka extortion [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Agar FIRs ko guide maano, toh jin crimes ke liye portal bana tha, woh ab system ke kaam ka chhota sa hissa hain.

## Complaint FIR nahi hai: cases kahan atakte hain

Portal khud kuch investigate nahi karta. Wahan file hui complaint sambandhit state ya union territory ki police dekhti hai, aur wahi police tay karti hai ki FIR register karni hai ya nahi [[cybercrime-portal]]. Complaint karne wale ko yahi step sabse kam dikhta hai.

Principle mein law saaf hai. Lalita Kumari (2013) mein Supreme Court ki Constitution Bench ne kaha ki agar information se cognizable offence banta hai, toh FIR register karna zaroori hai, aur mana karne wale officers pe action hona chahiye [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]]. Lekin 1 July 2024 se Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita ka Section 173(3) police ko, Deputy Superintendent ki permission se, FIR se pehle 14 din tak ki preliminary enquiry karne deta hai, un offences mein jinki saza 3 saal ya usse zyada, par 7 saal se kam hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Stalking aur voyeurism jaise offences, online ho ya offline, is window mein aa sakte hain.

Registration ke baad funnel aur patla hota hai. 2024 mein police ne jin cyber crime cases ko nipataya, unmein se 31.9% mein chargesheet file ki [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Us saal courts ke saamne 99,693 cyber crime cases the; 4,567 mein trial poora hua aur 2,596 mein conviction hua, aur saal ke end tak 90.9% pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh alag-alag stages pe alag-alag cases hain, ek hi group ko shuru se end tak follow nahi kiya gaya. Phir bhi shape funnel ki hai: upar lakhon complaints, neeche kuch hazaar convictions.

## Survivors se kiya gaya tracker ka vaada

Mrs X v. Union of India (26 April 2023) mein Delhi High Court ne direct kiya ki portal pe non-consensual intimate images wali complaints ke liye status tracker ho, aisi complaints ke liye din-raat chalne wali helpline bane, aur search engines token-based system use karein taaki de-index ki gayi images wapas na aayein [[delhihc-mrs-x-2023]].

Tracker us problem ka jawab hai jo is investigation mein baar-baar saamne aati hai: file karne ke baad ki khamoshi. Survivor ko pata hona chahiye ki complaint kisi police station tak pahunchi ya nahi, FIR bani ya nahi, aur kisi ne platform ko action lene ko kaha ya nahi. Phir November 2025 mein Ministry of Electronics and IT ke ek procedure ne platforms ko flagged images hatane aur I4C ko unka secure hash bank rakhne ko kaha [[pib-meity-ncii-sop-2025]].

Court ne standard tay kar diya hai; system ko usi pe kaso. Agar tumhe nahi dikh raha ki tumhari complaint ka kya hua, toh jo police use dekh rahi hai unhe likho, apna acknowledgement number (aur intimate images ke case mein 2023 ka order) quote karo, aur likh ke poocho ki FIR register hui ya nahi. Tumhare sabse pakke rights FIR se jude hain, portal complaint se nahi: investigation shuru hone ke baad police ko 90 din ke andar tumhe batana hota hai ki woh kahan tak pahunchi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Aise file karo ki complaint case bane

- **Pehle collect karo:** date aur time dikhate screenshots, khud links, account names, phone numbers aur payment IDs.
- **Child abuse images ko haath mat lagao:** unki jagah links report karo. IT Act child sexual abuse material ko sirf publish karne pe nahi, browse, download ya exchange karne pe bhi saza deta hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].
- **Order mein likho:** kya hua, kab, kis platform pe, kis account se, aur tum kya chahte ho: content hatana aur police case.
- **FIR maango:** Section 173 BNSS ke under tum kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakte ho, chahe offence kahin bhi hua ho, ya electronically, 3 din ke andar sign karke, aur tumhe uski free copy milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Agar station mana kare, toh tum Superintendent of Police ko likh sakte ho aur phir magistrate ke paas ja sakte ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Removal alag se chalao:** 20 February 2026 se platforms ko intimate images complaint milne ke 2 ghante ke andar hatani hoti hain [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Portal complaint state ko batati hai ki kuch hua hai. FIR use action lene pe majboor karti hai. Dono lekar niklo.

ai-nudify-apps-fake-images-real-abuse.en:
Imagine a 16-year-old in Indore. A classmate copies her photo from the school's annual-day post, runs it through an app that promises to "undress" anyone, and drops the result into a group chat. By evening, people she has never met have seen a nude image with her face on it. Or imagine a 24-year-old in Gurugram whose colleague does the same with a photo from an office lunch. No camera was ever pointed at either of them. The image is fake. The faces, the names and the humiliation are real, and the same abuse can target a boy, a teacher or a trans student.

These "nudify" tools are one corner of a problem that child-protection agencies have only recently begun to count: sexual abuse made with generative AI.

## From 4,700 to more than 400,000: the AI curve

The clearest numbers come from the US National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC), which receives reports of child sexual exploitation from tech platforms. Reports with a generative-AI link rose from about 4,700 in 2023 to 67,000 in 2024, a 1,325% increase, and to more than 400,000 in 2025. More than 182,000 of the 2025 reports involved offenders possessing, generating or trying to generate AI-made child sexual abuse material [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]].

Read the curve with care: these are reports, not victims, and reports rise when platforms look harder as well as when abuse grows. Still, in two years AI-linked exploitation went from a marginal category to one counted in hundreds of thousands of reports.

India's crime statistics offer no comparable count. NCRB's table of cyber crimes against women has no column for AI-made images; the nearest, "defamation or morphing", recorded 293 cases in all of India in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That table counts FIRs registered by police, not complaints, and online sexual abuse is heavily under-reported. So 293 measures what reached a police register. It does not show that this abuse is rare in India.

## No camera, real victims

The most misleading word in this story is "fake". It suggests that nobody was there, so nobody was hurt.

NCMEC's own work says otherwise. Since it began tracking generative AI in 2023, it has identified more than 275 child victims of AI-generated sexual abuse material and categorised more than 158,000 images and videos as AI-made abuse material [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. Each identified victim is a child, not a pattern of pixels.

For the person in the image, the harm does not depend on whether a camera was involved. Classmates, colleagues and relatives may not be able to tell a convincing fake from a photo, and may not stop to ask. The image can be used to threaten, to extort or to shame, and every forward makes a new copy the target has to chase. "But it isn't really you" stops none of that.

## What Indian law already says about morphed images

This is general information, not legal advice. Indian rules did not wait for AI. Since 2021, Rule 3(2)(b) of the IT Rules has required platforms to take down content that shows a person in full or partial nudity or in a sexual act, or impersonates them, "including artificially morphed images", on a complaint by that person or someone on their behalf [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]]. The deadline was 24 hours; since 20 February 2026 it is two hours [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Sharing the image can be a crime in its own right. Depending on what it shows, publishing or sending it online can fall under Section 67 of the IT Act (obscene material, up to three years and a Rs 5 lakh fine on first conviction) or Section 67A (sexually explicit material, up to five years and Rs 10 lakh, and up to seven years on a repeat conviction) [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Both sections are written around the material that is published or sent, not around how it was made.

If the person shown is under 18, Section 67B applies. It covers anyone who "creates text or digital images" depicting children in a sexually explicit manner, as well as anyone who collects, browses, downloads or exchanges it, with up to five years on first conviction [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Those words turn on what the image depicts, not on the tool that produced it, and the 2026 rules name synthetic child sexual abuse material directly [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

## The 2026 duty on AI tools

The 2026 amendment puts a duty on the toolmakers themselves. Platforms that offer AI tools must use technical measures to block synthetic content that contains child sexual exploitative and abuse material or non-consensual intimate imagery, and must prominently label other synthetic content [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Our explainer on India's deepfake rules covers the labelling duties in detail.

For nudify tools the implication is blunt: a product whose selling point is undressing people without consent is built to do exactly what the rules order AI tools to block. But a rule binds only companies that follow it, and an app that ignores it does not vanish on its own. For a target, the fastest lever is still a complaint.

## If it happens to you or a friend

1. **Do not forward the image**, even to warn someone or to prove it is fake. If the person shown is under 18, do not download it either: Section 67B covers downloading as well as sharing.
2. **Collect the trail instead**: links, usernames, group names, dates and any threats. Keep a record of where it was posted and by which account.
3. **Complain to the platform** and call it an "artificially morphed image". The platform must remove it within two hours [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]], and a friend can complain on the target's behalf [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]].
4. **Report it as a cyber crime** on the helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. If the person is under 18, the Child Helpline 1098, which is linked to the 112 emergency system, can also step in [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].
5. **Say the right thing.** "This is not your fault" matters more than "how did they get your photo?" If the weight of it becomes too much, Tele-MANAS on 14416 is free and round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

A nudify app needs one photo and a few seconds. The response has to be as quick: report it, get it removed, and refuse to pass it on.
ai-nudify-apps-fake-images-real-abuse.hg:
Socho, Indore mein ek 16 saal ki ladki hai. Uska ek classmate school ke annual day wale post se uski photo utha leta hai, use ek aise app mein daalta hai jo kisi ko bhi "undress" karne ka daava karta hai, aur result ek group chat mein daal deta hai. Shaam tak woh log bhi uske chehre wali ek nude image dekh chuke hote hain jinse woh kabhi mili tak nahi. Ya Gurugram mein kisi 24 saal ke insaan ko socho, jiske colleague ne office lunch ki ek photo ke saath yahi kiya. Dono mein se kisi ki taraf kabhi koi camera nahi utha. Image fake hai. Par chehre, naam aur beizzati asli hain, aur yahi abuse kisi ladke, teacher ya trans student ke saath bhi ho sakta hai.

Yeh "nudify" tools us problem ka bas ek kona hain jise child-protection agencies ne abhi haal hi mein ginna shuru kiya hai: generative AI se bana sexual abuse.

## 4,700 se 400,000 ke paar: AI ka graph

Sabse saaf aankde US ke National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) se aate hain, jahan tech platforms bachchon ke sexual exploitation ki reports bhejte hain. Generative AI se judi reports 2023 mein lagbhag 4,700 thi, 2024 mein 67,000 ho gayi, yaani 1,325% ki badhotri, aur 2025 mein 400,000 se bhi zyada. 2025 ki inme se 182,000 se zyada reports mein offenders AI se bana child sexual abuse material rakh rahe the, bana rahe the ya banane ki koshish kar rahe the [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]].

Is graph ko dhyan se padho: yeh reports hain, victims nahi, aur reports tab bhi badhti hain jab platforms zyada dhyan se dhoondhte hain, sirf tab nahi jab abuse badhta hai. Phir bhi, sirf do saal mein AI se juda exploitation ek chhoti si category se badhkar aisi category ban gaya jiski reports lakhon mein gini jaati hain.

India ke crime statistics mein aisi koi ginti nahi hai. NCRB ki auraton ke khilaaf cyber crime wali table mein AI se bani images ka koi column hi nahi; sabse kareeb wali category, "defamation ya morphing", mein 2024 mein poore India mein 293 case darj hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh table police ki darj ki hui FIRs ginti hai, complaints nahi, aur online sexual abuse bahut kam report hota hai. Isliye 293 sirf yeh batata hai ki police register tak kitna pahuncha. Isse yeh saabit nahi hota ki India mein yeh abuse kam hota hai.

## Camera nahi, par victims asli

Is kahani ka sabse gumraah karne wala shabd hai "fake". Isse lagta hai ki wahan koi tha hi nahi, to kisi ko chot bhi nahi lagi.

NCMEC ka apna kaam kuch aur kehta hai. 2023 mein generative AI ko track karna shuru karne ke baad se woh AI se bane sexual abuse material ke 275 se zyada bachcha victims ko pehchaan chuka hai, aur 158,000 se zyada images aur videos ko AI se bana abuse material maan chuka hai [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. Pehchana gaya har victim ek bachcha hai, pixels ka koi pattern nahi.

Image mein dikhne wale insaan ke liye nuksaan is baat par depend nahi karta ki camera tha ya nahi. Ho sakta hai classmates, colleagues aur rishtedaar ek achhe fake aur asli photo mein farak na kar paayein, aur ruk kar poochhein bhi nahi. Image se dhamkaya ja sakta hai, paise ainthe ja sakte hain, sharminda kiya ja sakta hai, aur har forward ek nayi copy banata hai jiske peeche target ko bhaagna padta hai. "Par yeh asli mein tum nahi ho" kehne se inme se kuch nahi rukta.

## Morphed images par Indian law pehle se kya kehta hai

Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi. India ke rules ne AI ka intezaar nahi kiya. 2021 se IT Rules ka Rule 3(2)(b) platforms ko aisa content hatane ko kehta hai jo kisi insaan ko poori ya aadhi nudity mein ya sexual act mein dikhaye, ya uski nakal kare, "including artificially morphed images"; yeh us insaan ki, ya uski taraf se kisi aur ki, complaint par hota hai [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]]. Pehle deadline 24 ghante thi; 20 February 2026 se yeh 2 ghante hai [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Image share karna apne aap mein crime ho sakta hai. Image mein kya dikh raha hai, uske hisaab se use online publish karna ya bhejna IT Act ke Section 67 (obscene material: pehli conviction par 3 saal tak aur Rs 5 lakh tak fine) ya Section 67A (sexually explicit material: 5 saal tak aur Rs 10 lakh, aur dobara conviction par 7 saal tak) mein aa sakta hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Dono sections us material ke baare mein hain jo publish ya send hua, is baare mein nahi ki woh bana kaise.

Agar image mein dikhne wala 18 se chhota hai, to Section 67B lagta hai. Iske shabd hain "creates text or digital images": yaani jo bhi bachchon ko sexually explicit tareeke se dikhane wali digital images banata hai, us par yeh lagta hai, aur jo aisa material collect, browse, download ya exchange karta hai, us par bhi; pehli conviction par 5 saal tak ki saza [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Yeh shabd is par tikte hain ki image kya dikhati hai, is par nahi ki woh kis tool se bani, aur 2026 ke rules synthetic child sexual abuse material ka naam seedha lete hain [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

## AI tools par 2026 ki zimmedari

2026 ka amendment khud tool banane walon par zimmedari daalta hai. AI tools dene wale platforms ko technical measures se aisa synthetic content block karna hoga jisme child sexual exploitative and abuse material ya non-consensual intimate imagery ho, aur baaki synthetic content par prominent label lagana hoga [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. India ke deepfake rules par hamara explainer labelling ki zimmedariyon ko detail mein samjhata hai.

Nudify tools ke liye iska matlab saaf hai: jis product ki khaasiyat hi logon ko unki consent ke bina "undress" karna hai, woh theek wahi karne ke liye bana hai jise block karne ka order rules AI tools ko dete hain. Par rule sirf un companies ko baandhta hai jo use maanti hain, aur jo app use ignore karta hai, woh apne aap gaayab nahi hota. Target ke liye sabse tez rasta ab bhi complaint hi hai.

## Agar yeh tumhare ya kisi dost ke saath ho

1. **Image forward mat karo**, kisi ko warn karne ya use fake prove karne ke liye bhi nahi. Agar image mein dikhne wala 18 se chhota hai, to use download bhi mat karo: Section 67B share karne ke saath download karne par bhi lagta hai.
2. **Iske bajaye saboot ka trail jama karo**: links, usernames, group ke naam, dates aur koi bhi dhamki. Record rakho ki image kahan post hui aur kis account se.
3. **Platform par complaint karo** aur use "artificially morphed image" bolo. Platform ko use 2 ghante ke andar hatana hoga [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]], aur target ki taraf se koi dost bhi complaint kar sakta hai [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]].
4. **Ise cyber crime ke roop mein report karo**: helpline 1930 par ya cybercrime.gov.in par [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. Agar woh insaan 18 se chhota hai, to Child Helpline 1098, jo 112 emergency system se judi hai, bhi madad kar sakti hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].
5. **Sahi baat bolo.** "Isme tumhari koi galti nahi hai" kehna "unke paas tumhari photo aayi kaise?" poochhne se kahin zyada zaroori hai. Agar yeh bojh bahut bhaari lagne lage, to Tele-MANAS 14416 free hai aur din-raat chalta hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Nudify app ko bas ek photo aur kuch second chahiye. Jawab bhi utna hi tez hona chahiye: report karo, image hatwao, aur use aage bhejne se saaf mana karo.

bnss-14-day-enquiry-cyber-complaints.en:
Imagine a 23-year-old in Pune who finds that a fake Instagram account in her name is posting private photos from a relationship that ended last year. She takes screenshots, the account link and her ex's number to the police station. The officer scrolls through them and says: "We will do an enquiry first. Come back after two weeks."

Before July 2024 that answer had no footing in law. Today, for most online sexual offences, part of it can be lawful, and the rest of it cannot. Here is how the window works, what it does not allow, and what to do while it runs. This is general information, not legal advice.

## What did Lalita Kumari promise in 2013?

On 12 November 2013, a five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court held in *Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh* that registering an FIR is mandatory when the information discloses a cognizable offence, and that no preliminary inquiry is permissible in such a case. An officer cannot avoid that duty, the court said, and action must be taken against officers who refuse [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]].

The judgment did allow short preliminary inquiries, of up to seven days, in a few categories such as matrimonial and family disputes [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]]. Leaked images, fake profiles and explicit messages were not on that list. A complaint was supposed to become an FIR on the day it was made.

## What did Section 173(3) change in 2024?

The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure on 1 July 2024 [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]]. Its Section 173(3) says that for a cognizable offence punishable with three years or more but less than seven, the officer in charge of a police station may, with prior permission from an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police, hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. It is a check before registration, not a replacement for it.

Every word sets a limit. "May" means the officer can still register the FIR at once. The permission must come before the enquiry starts, not after you complain about the delay. And 14 days is a ceiling, not a target.

## Why do most online sexual offences fall inside the window?

Because of where their punishments were set. Capturing or sharing an image of a person's private area without consent (IT Act Section 66E) carries up to three years or a fine of up to Rs 2 lakh; transmitting obscene material (Section 67) up to three years; and transmitting sexually explicit material (Section 67A) up to five years on first conviction [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, voyeurism, which includes sharing a woman's private image without her consent even if she agreed to it being taken, carries one to three years on first conviction; stalking and sexual harassment carry up to three [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

| Offence | Maximum on first conviction | Inside the 14-day window? |
|---|---|---|
| Private image without consent (IT Act 66E) | 3 years | Yes |
| Obscene material (IT Act 67) | 3 years | Yes |
| Sexually explicit material (IT Act 67A) | 5 years | Yes |
| Voyeurism or stalking (BNS 77, 78) | 3 years | Yes |
| Rape (BNS 64) | Life (minimum 10 years) | No |

Rape sits outside: it carries at least ten years, so a rape complaint must be registered when it is made [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The cost of the window is invisible in the data. Police registered 2,197 cases under Section 67A and 436 under Section 66E in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Those tables count FIRs, not complaints, and NCRB itself warns that registered crime is not the same as crime [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A complaint that sits in an enquiry and never becomes an FIR leaves no trace in them.

> The enquiry is a pause the law allows, with a clock and a signature attached. Without either, it is just a refusal.

## What are my rights during the enquiry?

- **Any station, or online.** Section 173 lets you report a cognizable offence at any police station, wherever it happened, or electronically, provided you sign within three days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. When the abuser is in another city, that matters. An e-FIR also gives you a dated record of when you complained.
- **A woman officer.** A woman's complaint of sexual harassment, stalking or voyeurism must be recorded by a woman police officer or woman officer [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **A free copy and an update.** Once the FIR is registered you get a copy free of cost, and police must tell you how the investigation is progressing within 90 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Takedown does not wait.** Since 20 February 2026, platforms must remove nude, sexual or morphed images of a person within two hours of that person's complaint [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Report on the platform and on the 1930 helpline or cybercrime.gov.in the same day [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

## What if police still refuse?

Ask three questions and write down the answers: Is this a preliminary enquiry under Section 173(3)? Which officer of Deputy Superintendent rank approved it, and on what date? When do the 14 days end? If no such permission exists, there is no lawful enquiry, and the *Lalita Kumari* rule applies in full.

When the 14 days are over, go back or write to the station and ask for the FIR, or for the result of the enquiry in writing. If the station still will not act, Section 173(4) lets you send the complaint to the Superintendent of Police, and then approach a magistrate [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

One more sentence is worth knowing. Section 199 of the BNS makes it a crime, punishable with six months to two years of rigorous imprisonment, for a public servant to fail to record information about certain sexual offences, and voyeurism is on that list; stalking, sexual harassment and the IT Act offences are not [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 77's voyeurism offence protects women, so if you are a woman and your complaint is about a private image shared without consent, name voyeurism alongside Section 66E.

For someone whose images are on a stranger's screen, two weeks is a long time. The law now gives police a window. It also gives you the right to see the clock.
bnss-14-day-enquiry-cyber-complaints.hg:
Socho, Pune mein ek 23 saal ki ladki ko pata chalta hai ki uske naam se ek fake Instagram account bana hai, jis pe pichhle saal khatam hue relationship ki private photos post ho rahi hain. Woh screenshots, account ka link aur apne ex ka number lekar police station jaati hai. Officer sab scroll karta hai aur kehta hai: "Pehle hum enquiry karenge. Do hafte baad aana."

July 2024 se pehle is jawab ka law mein koi aadhaar nahi tha. Aaj, zyada tar online sexual offences ke liye, iska ek hissa legal ho sakta hai, aur baaki hissa nahi. Yeh window kaise kaam karti hai, kya allow nahi karti, aur jab tak chal rahi hai tab tak kya karna hai, yahan padho. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 2013 mein Lalita Kumari ne kya vaada kiya tha?

12 November 2013 ko Supreme Court ki paanch judges wali Constitution Bench ne *Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh* mein kaha ki agar information se cognizable offence saamne aata hai toh FIR register karna zaroori hai, aur aise case mein koi preliminary inquiry allowed nahi hai. Court ne kaha ki officer is duty se bach nahi sakta, aur jo officers mana karte hain unke khilaaf action hona chahiye [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]].

Judgment ne kuch categories mein, jaise matrimonial aur family disputes, saat din tak ki chhoti preliminary inquiry ki ijaazat di thi [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]]. Leaked images, fake profiles aur explicit messages us list mein nahi the. Complaint jis din di jaaye, usi din FIR banni thi.

## 2024 mein Section 173(3) ne kya badla?

Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ne 1 July 2024 ko Code of Criminal Procedure ki jagah le li [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]]. Uska Section 173(3) kehta hai ki agar cognizable offence ki saza teen saal ya usse zyada lekin saat saal se kam hai, toh police station ka officer in charge, Deputy Superintendent of Police se neeche rank ke na hone wale officer ki pehle se li gayi permission ke saath, 14 din tak ki preliminary enquiry kar sakta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh registration se pehle ki ek jaanch hai, FIR ki jagah nahi.

Har shabd ek limit lagata hai. "Kar sakta hai" ka matlab hai ki officer chahe toh FIR turant register kar sakta hai. Permission enquiry shuru hone se pehle aani chahiye, tumhare delay pe shikayat karne ke baad nahi. Aur 14 din ek upper limit hai, koi target nahi.

## Zyada tar online sexual offences window ke andar kyun aate hain?

Kyunki unki saza wahin set ki gayi hai. Kisi insaan ke private area ki image bina consent capture ya share karna (IT Act Section 66E) teen saal tak ki jail ya Rs 2 lakh tak ke fine wala offence hai; obscene material bhejna (Section 67) teen saal tak; aur sexually explicit material bhejna (Section 67A) first conviction pe paanch saal tak [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke under voyeurism, jismein kisi aurat ki private image uske consent ke bina share karna bhi aata hai, chahe usne photo khinchwane ke liye haan kaha ho, first conviction pe ek se teen saal ki saza rakhta hai; stalking aur sexual harassment teen saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

| Offence | First conviction pe maximum | 14 din ki window ke andar? |
|---|---|---|
| Bina consent private image (IT Act 66E) | 3 saal | Haan |
| Obscene material (IT Act 67) | 3 saal | Haan |
| Sexually explicit material (IT Act 67A) | 5 saal | Haan |
| Voyeurism ya stalking (BNS 77, 78) | 3 saal | Haan |
| Rape (BNS 64) | Umrqaid (kam se kam 10 saal) | Nahi |

Rape bahar hai: uski saza kam se kam das saal hai, isliye rape ki complaint jis waqt di jaaye usi waqt register honi chahiye [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Is window ki keemat data mein dikhti hi nahi. 2024 mein police ne Section 67A ke under 2,197 aur Section 66E ke under 436 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh tables FIRs ginti hain, complaints nahi, aur NCRB khud warning deta hai ki register hua crime aur asli crime ek cheez nahi hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo complaint enquiry mein padi reh jaaye aur kabhi FIR na bane, uska in tables mein koi nishaan nahi milta.

> Enquiry ek pause hai jo law allow karta hai, ek ghadi aur ek signature ke saath. Dono ke bina, woh bas ek inkaar hai.

## Enquiry ke dauraan mere kya rights hain?

- **Koi bhi station, ya online.** Section 173 ke under tum cognizable offence ki report kisi bhi police station mein kar sakte ho, offence chahe kahin bhi hua ho, ya electronically, bas teen din ke andar sign karna hoga [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jab abuser kisi aur shehar mein ho, tab yeh bahut kaam aata hai. e-FIR se tumhare paas yeh record bhi rehta hai ki complaint kis date ko di.
- **Mahila officer.** Kisi aurat ki sexual harassment, stalking ya voyeurism ki complaint mahila police officer ya mahila officer hi record karegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Free copy aur update.** FIR register hone ke baad uski copy tumhe free milti hai, aur police ko 90 din ke andar batana hota hai ki investigation kahan tak pahunchi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Takedown intezaar nahi karta.** 20 February 2026 se platforms ko kisi insaan ki nude, sexual ya morphed images uski complaint ke do ghante ke andar hatani hoti hain [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Usi din platform pe aur 1930 helpline ya cybercrime.gov.in pe report karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

## Agar police phir bhi mana kare toh?

Teen sawaal poocho aur jawab likh lo: Kya yeh Section 173(3) ke under preliminary enquiry hai? Deputy Superintendent rank ke kis officer ne ise approve kiya, aur kis date ko? 14 din kab khatam honge? Agar aisi koi permission hai hi nahi, toh koi legal enquiry nahi chal rahi, aur *Lalita Kumari* ka rule poori tarah lagu hota hai.

14 din khatam hone pe station wapas jao ya likh kar FIR maango, ya enquiry ka result likhit mein maango. Agar station phir bhi kuch na kare, toh Section 173(4) ke under tum complaint Superintendent of Police ko bhej sakte ho, aur uske baad magistrate ke paas ja sakte ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Ek aur baat jaanna kaam ki hai. BNS ka Section 199 kisi public servant ke liye kuch sexual offences ki information record na karna crime banata hai, jiski saza chhe mahine se do saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment hai, aur voyeurism us list mein hai; stalking, sexual harassment aur IT Act ke offences nahi hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 77 ka voyeurism offence aurton ko protect karta hai, isliye agar tum aurat ho aur tumhari complaint bina consent share ki gayi private image ke baare mein hai, toh Section 66E ke saath voyeurism ka naam bhi lo.

Jiski images kisi anjaan ki screen pe hain, uske liye do hafte bahut lamba waqt hai. Law ne ab police ko ek window di hai. Usne tumhe bhi yeh haq diya hai ki tum us ghadi ko dekh sako.

consent-to-capture-not-to-share.en:
Imagine a 20-year-old in Indore. Early in a relationship, she sends her boyfriend a photo meant only for him. Months after they break up, it turns up in his hostel group. Plenty of people would say she brought it on herself. Indian criminal law says the opposite, in one sentence. This explainer is general information, not legal advice.

## One sentence in the law that changes everything

Section 77 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) is the voyeurism offence. Its Explanation 2 reads:

> "Where the victim consents to the capture of the images or any act, but not to their dissemination to third persons and where such image or act is disseminated, such dissemination shall be considered an offence under this section."

In plain words: agreeing to a photo is not agreeing to its being shared, and sharing it anyway is voyeurism. The punishment is one to three years in prison on first conviction, and three to seven years on a repeat [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Voyeurism entered Indian law in 2013 as IPC Section 354C [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]] and became Section 77 when the BNS replaced the IPC on 1 July 2024 [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]]. Section 77 protects women, and the BNS defines a woman as a female of any age [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 66E of the IT Act covers everyone, men and transgender people included: capturing, publishing or transmitting an image of "a private area of any person without his or her consent" is punishable with up to three years, a fine of up to Rs 2 lakh, or both [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

## Capture, keep, share: three separate consents

Explanation 2 splits one image into two moments, capture and dissemination, and asks for consent at each. The law already thinks this way about sex: Section 63 of the BNS defines consent as an "unequivocal voluntary agreement" to "the specific sexual act" [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Consent is specific: one act, one person, one time.

Apply that to a phone and there are three moments, not one:

- **Capture.** A yes to one photo is not a yes to the next one, or to a video.
- **Keep.** A photo sent during a relationship was sent to a partner, not to an archive. If she asks you to delete it, delete it.
- **Share.** This is where the law bites hardest. A yes to you is not a yes to your friends, your group or the internet.

Consent can also change. Someone who said yes last month can say no today, and a break-up does not turn a private image into public property.

There is one hard legal line inside "keep". If the person in the image is under 18, it is child sexual abuse material, and the Supreme Court held in 2024 that even storing or possessing it, without deleting or reporting it, is an offence under the POCSO Act [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]]. Under POCSO, a person under 18 cannot give legal consent to sexual activity, so agreement between two teenagers does not change this.

## What 1,722 and 436 cases tell us

In 2024, police across India registered 1,722 cases of voyeurism, counting the old IPC section and the new BNS one together, and 436 cases under Section 66E [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The two counts come from different tables and cannot be added. Neither says how many involved a forwarded image.

Think of how many college, hostel and office groups exist in one city, and how often a private photo "goes around" one of them. A few hundred or a couple of thousand FIRs a year, nationwide, do not describe that reality. They count how often it reaches a police station and becomes an FIR, not how often it happens.

Several things keep the numbers low. NCRB counts FIRs, not complaints, and online sexual abuse is heavily under-reported. Each FIR is counted only under its most serious offence, so a voyeurism case filed with a heavier charge may be counted under that charge instead [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. And there is the question a complainant may face at the police station or at home: why did you send it at all?

The law answers it. A woman's complaint of voyeurism must be recorded by a woman officer [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. In a Section 77 prosecution, evidence of her character or previous sexual experience is not relevant to the question of consent [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. Section 77 does not ask why she trusted someone. It asks whether she agreed to the image being shared.

## Forwarding culture: groups, 'proof' and 'just showing a friend'

Most forwards come with an excuse. The law recognises none of them.

- **"She sent it to me."** That was consent to capture, and to you. Under Explanation 2, passing it on without her consent is an offence in itself.
- **"It's proof she cheated" or "people should know what she's like."** The law names no exception for revenge, proof or warnings.
- **"It was already in the group."** Section 66E punishes anyone who "publishes or transmits" such an image [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Each forward is a fresh transmission.
- **"I only showed a friend on my phone."** The law speaks of "dissemination to third persons" and names no exception for one friend or one glance.

The person in the picture chose none of these audiences. That is exactly the wrong the law punishes.

## Practising digital consent

Digital consent is a habit. Five rules cover most situations:

1. **Ask before you capture**, every time, and accept a no without an argument.
2. **Ask before you share**, about the specific share: this photo, to this person.
3. **Treat a sent image as on loan.** Delete it when asked, and after a break-up, without being asked.
4. **Break the chain.** If an image reaches you that you were not meant to see, do not forward, save or react. Report it on the platform.
5. **If it happens to you, it is not your fault.** Call 1930 or file at cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]], and report every copy to the platform: since 20 February 2026, platforms must remove nude, sexual or morphed images within two hours of your complaint [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

None of these rules asks anyone to stop taking photos, sending them, or falling in love. They ask for the one thing the law already demands: that the person in the picture decides where it goes.
consent-to-capture-not-to-share.hg:
Socho, Indore ki ek 20 saal ki ladki. Relationship ki shuruaat mein woh apne boyfriend ko ek photo bhejti hai, sirf uske liye. Break-up ke kuch mahine baad woh photo uske hostel group mein pahunch jaati hai. Bahut log kahenge ki galti uski hai, usne bheji hi kyun. Indian criminal law iska ulta kehta hai, aur woh bhi ek hi sentence mein. Yeh explainer general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Law ka ek sentence jo sab badal deta hai

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 77 voyeurism ka offence hai. Uska Explanation 2 kehta hai:

> "Where the victim consents to the capture of the images or any act, but not to their dissemination to third persons and where such image or act is disseminated, such dissemination shall be considered an offence under this section."

Simple shabdon mein: photo ke liye haan kehna use share karne ke liye haan kehna nahi hai, aur phir bhi share karna voyeurism hai. Saza pehli conviction pe ek se teen saal ki jail hai, aur dobara conviction pe teen se saat saal [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Voyeurism 2013 mein IPC Section 354C ke roop mein Indian law mein aaya [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]], aur 1 July 2024 ko jab BNS ne IPC ki jagah li, toh yeh Section 77 ban gaya [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]]. Section 77 women ko protect karta hai, aur BNS "woman" ko kisi bhi umar ki female ke roop mein define karta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. IT Act ka Section 66E sabko cover karta hai, men aur transgender logon ko bhi: "a private area of any person without his or her consent", yaani kisi bhi insaan ke private area ki image bina consent capture, publish ya transmit karne pe teen saal tak ki jail, Rs 2 lakh tak ka fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

## Capture, keep, share: teen alag consents

Explanation 2 ek image ko do moments mein baant deta hai, capture aur dissemination (yaani aage phailana), aur dono pe consent maangta hai. Sex ke baare mein law pehle se aise hi sochta hai: BNS ka Section 63 consent ko "unequivocal voluntary agreement" kehta hai, "the specific sexual act" ke liye [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Consent specific hota hai: ek kaam, ek insaan, ek waqt.

Ise phone pe apply karo, toh ek nahi, teen moments hain:

- **Capture.** Ek photo ke liye haan agli photo ya video ke liye haan nahi hai.
- **Keep.** Relationship ke dauraan bheji gayi photo partner ko bheji gayi thi, kisi archive ko nahi. Agar woh delete karne ko kahe, toh delete karo.
- **Share.** Yahan law sabse sakht hai. Tumhe diya gaya haan tumhare friends, tumhare group ya internet ke liye haan nahi hai.

Consent badal bhi sakta hai. Jisne pichhle mahine haan kaha tha, woh aaj na keh sakta hai, aur break-up kisi private image ko public property nahi bana deta.

"Keep" ke andar ek pakki legal line hai. Agar image wala insaan 18 se kam ka hai, toh woh child sexual abuse material hai, aur 2024 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki use bina delete ya report kiye store karna ya apne paas rakhna bhi POCSO Act ke under offence hai [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]]. POCSO ke under 18 se kam umar ka insaan sexual activity ke liye legal consent nahi de sakta, isliye do teenagers ki aapsi haan se bhi yeh nahi badalta.

## 1,722 aur 436 cases kya batate hain

2024 mein poore India mein police ne voyeurism ke 1,722 cases register kiye, purane IPC section aur naye BNS section ko milakar, aur Section 66E ke under 436 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh dono ginti alag-alag tables se aati hain aur inhe joda nahi ja sakta. Dono mein se koi yeh nahi batati ki kitne cases mein image forward hui thi.

Ab socho ki ek hi shehar mein kitne college, hostel aur office groups hain, aur kitni baar koi private photo unme "ghoom jaati" hai. Poore desh ke liye saal bhar mein kuch sau ya do-ek hazaar FIRs us reality ko describe nahi karti. Yeh sirf yeh ginti hain ki aisa kitni baar police station tak pahuncha aur FIR bana, yeh nahi ki asal mein kitni baar hota hai.

Kai cheezein in numbers ko kam rakhti hain. NCRB FIRs ginta hai, complaints nahi, aur online sexual abuse bahut kam report hota hai. Har FIR sirf uske sabse serious offence ke neeche gini jaati hai, isliye jis voyeurism case ke saath koi bhaari charge laga ho, woh shayad us charge ke neeche gina jaaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aur woh sawaal bhi hai jo complaint karne wali ko police station ya ghar pe sunna pad sakta hai: tumne bheji hi kyun?

Law iska jawab deta hai. Voyeurism ki complaint agar woman kar rahi hai, toh use woman officer hi record karegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Section 77 ke case mein uska character ya pichhla sexual experience consent ke sawaal pe relevant nahi hai [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. Section 77 yeh nahi poochta ki usne kisi pe bharosa kyun kiya. Woh yeh poochta hai ki kya usne image share hone ke liye haan kaha tha.

## Forwarding culture: groups, 'proof' aur 'bas ek friend ko dikhaya'

Zyada tar forwards ke saath koi bahana hota hai. Law inme se kisi ko nahi maanta.

- **"Usne khud mujhe bheji thi."** Woh capture ke liye, aur tumhare liye, consent tha. Explanation 2 ke hisaab se uske consent ke bina use aage bhejna apne aap mein ek offence hai.
- **"Yeh proof hai ki usne cheat kiya" ya "logon ko pata hona chahiye woh kaisi hai."** Law revenge, proof ya warning ke liye koi exception nahi deta.
- **"Yeh toh pehle se group mein thi."** Section 66E har us insaan ko punish karta hai jo aisi image "publishes or transmits" karta hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Har forward ek naya transmission hai.
- **"Maine toh bas ek friend ko apne phone pe dikhayi."** Law "dissemination to third persons" ki baat karta hai, aur ek friend ya ek nazar ke liye koi exception nahi deta.

Photo wale insaan ne inme se koi bhi audience nahi chuni. Law isi galti ko punish karta hai.

## Digital consent practice karna

Digital consent ek aadat hai. Paanch rules zyada tar situations cover kar lete hain:

1. **Capture se pehle poocho**, har baar, aur na ko bina behes ke maano.
2. **Share se pehle poocho**, us specific share ke baare mein: yeh photo, is insaan ko.
3. **Bheji gayi image ko udhaar samjho.** Kahe jaane pe delete karo, aur break-up ke baad bina kahe bhi.
4. **Chain todo.** Agar koi image tum tak pahunche jo tumhare liye nahi thi, toh forward, save ya react mat karo. Platform pe report karo.
5. **Agar yeh tumhare saath hua hai, toh isme tumhari galti nahi hai.** 1930 pe call karo ya cybercrime.gov.in pe complaint karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]], aur har copy platform pe report karo: 20 February 2026 se platforms ko tumhari complaint ke do ghante ke andar nude, sexual ya morphed images hatani padti hain [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Inme se koi bhi rule kisi se photos lena, bhejna ya pyaar karna band karne ko nahi kehta. Yeh sirf wahi ek cheez maangte hain jo law pehle se maangta hai: photo mein jo insaan hai, wahi decide kare ki woh kahan jaayegi.

cyber-crimes-against-women-ncrb-2024.en:
Every year, one table in the National Crime Records Bureau's Crime in India report tries to answer a simple question: what happens to women online? For 2024, its answer begins with 18,615 cyber crimes against women registered by police across India [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Then read along the row. Six named columns, from blackmail to fake profiles, hold a minority of those cases. The biggest column by far, 14,004 cases, is headed "other crimes against women" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The table counts women's cases. It barely describes them.

## The total: 18,615 and a three-year swing

The headline number moves sharply. Police registered 14,409 cyber crimes against women in 2022, 19,510 in 2023 and 18,615 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. A steep rise, then a small dip.

It is tempting to read the dip as progress. Look at the rest of the chapter first. In 2024, total cyber crime registered in India rose 17.9%, to 1,01,928 cases, and fraud was the motive in 72.6% of them [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Overall registration climbed while the women's count fell. That could mean less abuse, fewer complaints reaching an FIR, or cases landing in different columns after the law changed mid-year. The total alone cannot tell these apart.

## What the named categories count

This is everything the 2024 row names, apart from "other" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Column in NCRB's table | Cases, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Publishing or hosting obscene sexual material | 2,511 |
| Cyber stalking or bullying | 1,224 |
| Cyber blackmail or threats | 370 |
| Defamation or morphing | 293 |
| Fake profiles | 114 |
| Sex by deceitful means (new BNS offence) | 99 |

Read them as what they are. 293 cases of defamation or morphing, for the whole country, for a whole year. 114 fake profiles. These are not measures of how often women's photos are doctored or their identities faked. They measure how often that reached a police station, became an FIR and was filed in that particular column.

The last row is new. "Sexual intercourse by deceitful means" is Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which came into force on 1 July 2024, so its 99 cases cover only the second half of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Notice, too, what has no column at all: sextortion, or intimate images shared without consent. If those harms are counted, they are counted under other names.

## 14,004 'other': the box that hides the story

Then comes the column that holds the most and says the least. Of the 18,615 cases, 14,004 are filed as "other crimes against women" [[ncrb-cii-2024]], and the report gives no breakdown of what is inside.

So a reader cannot tell whether that box holds image-based abuse booked under a general section, harassment that police did not record as stalking, fraud against women, or something else entirely. Nobody can track any one of those harms over time.

Nor is this a quirk of the new code. In the 2022 and 2023 editions too, the "other" column held most of the cases [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. For three years running, India's most detailed national count of online crime against women has filed the majority of its cases under a heading that means "none of the above".

## Two rules that shape every number

NCRB prints two rules beside its tables, and both matter here.

The first is the principal offence rule: each FIR is counted once, under its most serious offence, the one with the maximum punishment [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Imagine a 22-year-old in Pune who finds a morphed photo of herself on a fake profile, and then the man behind it messages her family demanding money. One FIR could cover morphing, impersonation, obscene material and extortion. In the table, it becomes one case in one column, whichever offence carries the heaviest punishment. The fake profile and the morphing disappear from the count.

The second is that registration is not incidence.

> "'Rise in crime' and 'increase in registration of crime by police' are clearly two different things." (NCRB, Crime in India 2024)

NCRB adds that steps such as e-FIR facilities or women help desks can push the numbers up [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A state that makes it easier for women to file online can look worse than one that sends them home.

Then 2024 added a complication of its own. The BNS replaced the Indian Penal Code from 1 July 2024, which is why NCRB's 2024 tables split cases into IPC and BNS columns [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]]. Offences changed names and section numbers in mid-year, and new ones appeared. Comparing 2024 with 2023, column by column, means comparing counts made under two penal codes.

## What a useful table would show

None of this needs new technology, only better columns:

- **Open up "other".** Publish the offences inside it, and add a column for intimate images shared without consent.
- **Count every offence in an FIR**, at least in a supplementary table, so the principal offence rule stops erasing morphing and impersonation.
- **Record age and relationship.** For rape, NCRB already reports victims' ages and whether the accused was known to the victim [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Online abuse by former partners deserves the same visibility.
- **Link complaints to FIRs.** India's national cybercrime portal registered 22.68 lakh complaints of all kinds in 2024, most of them about fraud [[ls-uq432-2025]]. The women's table cannot show how many came from women, or how many became FIRs.
- **Follow cases to the end.** Across all cyber crime, police filed chargesheets in just 31.9% of the cases they finished investigating in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The women's table stops at registration.

Until those columns exist, hold 18,615 loosely: it is a count of FIRs, most of them unexplained. Anyone harmed online can still strengthen the record: report, describe every part of what happened, and ask which sections went into the FIR, a copy of which must be given free [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Complaints can be made on the helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].
cyber-crimes-against-women-ncrb-2024.hg:
Har saal National Crime Records Bureau ki Crime in India report ki ek table ek simple sawaal ka jawab dene ki koshish karti hai: online women ke saath kya hota hai? 2024 ke liye jawab shuru hota hai 18,615 se, yaani poore India mein police ne women ke against itne cyber crimes register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ab row ko aage padho. Chhe named columns, blackmail se lekar fake profiles tak, inme se kam hi cases rakhte hain. Sabse bada column, 14,004 cases ka, "other crimes against women" ke naam se hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Table women ke cases ginti toh hai, par unhe samjhaati bahut kam hai.

## Total: 18,615 aur teen saal ka utaar-chadhaav

Headline number kaafi upar-neeche hota hai. Police ne women ke against 2022 mein 14,409, 2023 mein 19,510 aur 2024 mein 18,615 cyber crimes register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Pehle tez uchhaal, phir thodi si girawat.

Is girawat ko progress samajhna aasaan hai. Par pehle chapter ka baaki hissa dekho. 2024 mein India mein total registered cyber crime 17.9% badhkar 1,01,928 cases tak pahuncha, aur inme se 72.6% mein motive fraud tha [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Overall registration upar gaya, jabki women wala count neeche aaya. Iska matlab kam abuse ho sakta hai, ya kam complaints ka FIR tak pahunchna, ya saal ke beech law badalne ke baad cases ka doosre columns mein chale jaana. Sirf total dekhkar in teeno mein farak nahi kiya ja sakta.

## Named categories asal mein kya ginti hain

"Other" ko chhodkar, 2024 ki row jin cheezon ke naam leti hai, woh sab yeh hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| NCRB table ka column | Cases, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Obscene sexual material publish ya host karna | 2,511 |
| Cyber stalking ya bullying | 1,224 |
| Cyber blackmail ya dhamki | 370 |
| Defamation ya morphing | 293 |
| Fake profiles | 114 |
| Deceitful means se sex (naya BNS offence) | 99 |

Inhe waise hi padho jaise yeh hain. Defamation ya morphing ke 293 cases, poore desh mein, poore saal mein. 114 fake profiles. Yeh is baat ka naap nahi hai ki women ki photos kitni baar edit ki jaati hain ya unki fake identity kitni baar banayi jaati hai. Yeh naapte hain ki aisa kitni baar police station tak pahuncha, FIR bani, aur usi khaas column mein file hui.

Aakhri row nayi hai. "Sexual intercourse by deceitful means" Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 69 hai, jo 1 July 2024 se laagu hua, isliye iske 99 cases sirf saal ke doosre hisse ke hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh bhi dekho ki kiska koi column hi nahi hai: sextortion ka, ya bina consent share ki gayi intimate images ka. Agar yeh harms gine bhi jaate hain, toh kisi aur naam se.

## 14,004 'other': woh box jo kahani chhupa leta hai

Phir aata hai woh column jisme sabse zyada cases hain aur jo sabse kam batata hai. 18,615 mein se 14,004 cases "other crimes against women" mein file hue hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]], aur report yeh breakdown nahi deti ki iske andar kya hai.

Toh padhne wala yeh nahi jaan sakta ki is box mein kisi general section mein darj image-based abuse hai, aisa harassment jise police ne stalking ke roop mein record nahi kiya, women ke saath hua fraud hai, ya kuch aur. Inme se kisi bhi harm ko saal-dar-saal track karna kisi ke liye mumkin nahi.

Yeh naye code ki koi ek-baar wali gadbad bhi nahi hai. 2022 aur 2023 ke editions mein bhi zyada tar cases "other" column mein hi the [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Lagaatar teen saal se, women ke against online crime ki India ki sabse detailed national ginti apne zyada tar cases ek aisi heading ke neeche rakh rahi hai jiska matlab hai "inme se koi nahi".

## Do rules jo har number ko shape karte hain

NCRB apni tables ke saath do rules chhaapta hai, aur yahan dono maayne rakhte hain.

Pehla hai principal offence rule: har FIR sirf ek baar gini jaati hai, uske sabse serious offence ke neeche, yaani jiski saza sabse zyada hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Socho, Pune ki ek 22 saal ki ladki ko ek fake profile pe apni morphed photo milti hai, aur phir uske peeche wala aadmi uski family ko message karke paise maangta hai. Ek FIR mein morphing, impersonation, obscene material aur extortion sab ho sakte hain. Table mein woh ek case banta hai, ek column mein, us offence ke neeche jiski saza sabse bhaari hai. Fake profile aur morphing ginti se gayab ho jaate hain.

Doosra rule: registration ka matlab incidence nahi hai.

> "'Rise in crime' and 'increase in registration of crime by police' are clearly two different things." (NCRB, Crime in India 2024)

Matlab, crime ka badhna aur police ka zyada cases register karna do alag cheezein hain. NCRB yeh bhi kehta hai ki e-FIR facility ya women help desks jaise kadam numbers badha sakte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo state women ke liye online complaint karna aasaan banata hai, woh us state se bura dikh sakta hai jo unhe ghar wapas bhej deta hai.

Phir 2024 ne apni ek alag uljhan jodi. 1 July 2024 se BNS ne Indian Penal Code ki jagah le li, isiliye NCRB ki 2024 ki tables cases ko IPC aur BNS columns mein baant kar dikhati hain [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]]. Saal ke beech mein offences ke naam aur section numbers badle, aur naye offences aaye. 2024 ko 2023 se column-by-column compare karne ka matlab hai do alag penal codes ke under hui ginti ko compare karna.

## Ek useful table kya dikhaati

Iske liye kisi nayi technology ki zaroorat nahi, bas behtar columns ki:

- **"Other" ko kholo.** Iske andar ke offences publish karo, aur bina consent share ki gayi intimate images ke liye alag column jodo.
- **FIR ka har offence gino**, kam se kam ek extra table mein, taaki principal offence rule morphing aur impersonation ko mitaana band kare.
- **Age aur rishta record karo.** Rape ke liye NCRB pehle se victims ki age batata hai, aur yeh bhi ki accused victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha ya nahi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ex-partners ke online abuse ko bhi utni hi visibility milni chahiye.
- **Complaints ko FIRs se jodo.** India ke national cybercrime portal pe 2024 mein har tarah ki 22.68 lakh complaints register hui, zyada tar fraud ki [[ls-uq432-2025]]. Women wali table yeh nahi dikha sakti ki inme se kitni women ne ki, ya kitni FIR bani.
- **Cases ko aakhir tak follow karo.** Saare cyber crime ko milakar, 2024 mein police ne jin cases ki investigation poori ki, unme se sirf 31.9% mein chargesheet file hui [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Women wali table registration pe hi ruk jaati hai.

Jab tak yeh columns nahi aate, 18,615 ko poora sach mat samjho: yeh FIRs ki ginti hai, jinme se zyada tar ka koi explanation nahi. Online harm jhelne wala koi bhi insaan phir bhi record ko mazboot kar sakta hai: report karo, jo hua uska har hissa batao, aur poocho ki FIR mein kaun se sections lage; FIR ki copy free mein deni hi padti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Complaint helpline 1930 pe ya cybercrime.gov.in pe ki ja sakti hai [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

cyberstalking-cases-fall-courts-stall.en:
Imagine a 22-year-old in Pune. She tells a former classmate to stop messaging her, then blocks him. A week later he is back with a new account, then another, then in her sister's inbox, then under her office's posts. She does not go to the police, so she never appears in India's crime data. Had she filed, her case would have joined a court queue in which, in 2024, more than 19 in every 20 cases were still waiting at the end of the year. It could as easily be a young man or a trans person, whom the main stalking law may not even cover.

## Two years of falling FIRs

Police registered 1,471 cases of cyber stalking or bullying of women and children in 2022, 1,305 in 2023 and 1,240 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. On its own, that line looks like progress.

Everything around it went the other way.
