- **Label.** All other synthetic content must be prominently labelled and, to the extent technically feasible, carry permanent metadata or another provenance marker, including a unique identifier, that identifies the tool used to make it.

Large social media platforms carry an extra duty under Rule 4(1A): they must ask users to declare whether content is synthetic, and verify that declaration before publishing it [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Two phrases decide how much this protects you. "Prominently" replaced a fixed size: MeitY's October 2025 draft wanted visual labels covering at least 10% of the screen, and audio disclosures during the first 10% of a clip [[meity-draft-sgi-amendment-2025]]. A fixed size could be measured; "prominent" will be argued over. And "to the extent technically feasible" leaves a company room to say a marker could not be added.

For a survivor, the block duty matters most. A fake nude of a real person is not content the rules ask companies to label. It is content they must stop their tools from making.

## Three hours, seven days: the new clocks

Our explainer on the two-hour rule covers takedowns in detail. For deepfakes, three clocks matter, all in force since 20 February 2026 [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]:

| Who starts the clock | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| You, complaining about a nude, sexual or morphed image of yourself | 24 hours | 2 hours |
| A court order or authorised government notice about unlawful content | 36 hours | 3 hours |
| You, with any other grievance | 15 days | 7 days |

The fastest clock is the one you start yourself. The rule behind the two-hour deadline has named artificially morphed images since 2021, so a fake nude needs no court order [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]]. The three-hour route needs an order or a notice, and a police notice must come from an officer not below the rank of Deputy Inspector General [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. A complaint at your local police station does not start that clock by itself.

## From advisory to binding rule, 2023-2026

India got here in three steps. On 26 December 2023, citing growing concern over AI deepfakes, MeitY issued an advisory telling all platforms to inform users, at registration, at every login and while uploading, what content is prohibited under Rule 3(1)(b) of the IT Rules and what penalties apply [[pib-meity-deepfake-advisory-2023]]. An advisory is guidance, not a binding rule. In October 2025 came the draft with its 10% labels [[meity-draft-sgi-amendment-2025]]. On 10 February 2026 came binding rules.

Over the same years, reports to the US National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) with a generative-AI link rose from about 4,700 in 2023 to 67,000 in 2024 and more than 400,000 in 2025. More than 182,000 of the 2025 reports involved offenders possessing, generating or trying to generate AI-made child sexual abuse material, and NCMEC has identified more than 275 child victims of such material since 2023 [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. These are global figures, not Indian ones, but they show what the rules are racing against.

## What a victim can demand today

If a synthetic sexual image of you appears online, you can demand:

1. **Removal within two hours.** Complain to the platform and call it an artificially morphed image of you. A friend can also complain on your behalf [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]].
2. **A decision within seven days** on any other grievance about the content.
3. **A police complaint.** Call 1930 or file at cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. Publishing sexually explicit material online can bring up to five years in prison and a fine of up to Rs 10 lakh on first conviction under Section 67A of the IT Act [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].
4. **A check for the tool's marker.** If the image carries an AI label or metadata, tell the police: where technically feasible, the rules require such markers to identify the tool that made it.
5. **Extra urgency if you are under 18.** Say so at once: creating or sharing a sexual image of a child, even a fake one, is punishable under Section 67B of the IT Act [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

Send links, not files. This is general information, not legal advice. A fake image can now be named, refused and removed by law; what remains is making companies and police move as fast as the rules say.
india-deepfake-rules-2026-explained.hg:
Socho, Bhopal mein college ke second year ki ek student apna class group kholti hai aur usme apni ek nude photo dekhti hai jo usne kabhi li hi nahi: chehra uska, body kisi aur ki, ek app ne dono ko jod diya. Photo fake hai. Par us par jo beetti hai, woh fake nahi. Yahi kisi ladke ya trans insaan ke saath bhi ho sakta hai.

2021 se India ke IT Rules har insaan ko apni "artificially morphed images" hatwane ka haq dete hain [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]]. Par unme na AI se bane content ki definition thi, na yeh likha tha ki AI tools dene wale platforms ke tools kya banane se mana karein. IT Amendment Rules, 2026, jo 10 February ko notify hue aur 20 February se lagu hain, dono kaam karte hain [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

## Law ab deepfake kise maanta hai

Law ka shabd "deepfake" nahi, "synthetically generated information" hai, jiski definition Rule 2(1)(wa) mein hai: aisa audio, visual ya audio-visual content jo computer par artificially ya algorithm se banaya ya badla gaya ho, jo asli aur sach lage, aur jisme koi insaan ya event aise dikhe ki woh asli insaan ya asli event se alag na lage, ya alag na lagne ki sambhavna ho [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Routine ya good-faith editing, accessibility features aur good-faith documents isse bahar hain.

Ise teen sawaalon wala test samjho: kya machine ne banaya ya badla? Kya asli lagta hai? Kya koi insaan ya event aise dikhta hai jaise sach mein hua ho? Face-swap karke bani nude photo teeno par "haan" hai. Photo ki brightness theek karna isme nahi aata, aur saaf-saaf cartoon bhi nahi. Par kisi ki cloned voice aa sakti hai, kyunki definition mein audio bhi hai.

## AI tools ki do zimmedariyan: block karo ya label lagao

Sabse bhaari zimmedari un platforms par hai jo content banane ya badalne ke liye AI tools dete hain [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]:

- **Block.** Unhe aise technical measures lagane honge ki koi user child sexual exploitative and abuse material ya non-consensual intimate imagery wala synthetic content bana hi na sake.
- **Label.** Baaki har synthetic content par prominent label lagana hoga, aur jahan tak technically possible ho, usme permanent metadata ya koi aur provenance marker dalna hoga, ek unique identifier ke saath, jisse pata chale ki use kis tool se banaya gaya.

Bade social media platforms ki ek extra zimmedari hai: Rule 4(1A) ke under unhe users se poochna hoga ki content synthetic hai ya nahi, aur publish karne se pehle us declaration ko verify karna hoga [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Do phrases tay karte hain ki isse tumhari kitni protection hogi. "Prominently" ne ek fixed size ki jagah li hai: MeitY ke October 2025 ke draft mein tha ki visual labels screen ka kam se kam 10% cover karein, aur audio mein clip ke pehle 10% hisse mein disclosure ho [[meity-draft-sgi-amendment-2025]]. Fixed size naapa ja sakta tha; "prominent" par behas hogi. Aur "to the extent technically feasible" company ko yeh kehne ki gunjaish deta hai ki marker dalna possible nahi tha.

Survivor ke liye sabse zaroori hai block wali zimmedari. Kisi asli insaan ki fake nude aisa content nahi hai jis par bas label laga diya jaaye. Yeh aisa content hai jise companies ko apne tools se banne hi nahi dena hai.

## Teen ghante, saat din: nayi ghadiyan

Two-hour rule par humara explainer takedown ka poora process batata hai. Deepfakes ke liye teen ghadiyan matter karti hain, teeno 20 February 2026 se lagu [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]:

| Ghadi kaun shuru karta hai | Pehle | Ab |
|---|---|---|
| Tum, apni nude, sexual ya morphed image ki complaint karke | 24 ghante | 2 ghante |
| Court order ya authorised government notice, unlawful content par | 36 ghante | 3 ghante |
| Tum, kisi aur grievance ke saath | 15 din | 7 din |

Sabse tez ghadi woh hai jo tum khud shuru karte ho. Two-hour deadline wala rule 2021 se hi artificially morphed images ka naam leta hai, isliye fake nude ke liye court order ki zaroorat nahi [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]]. Teen ghante wale raaste ke liye order ya notice chahiye, aur police ka notice kam se kam Deputy Inspector General (DIG) rank ke officer se aana chahiye [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Yaani tumhare local police station mein complaint karne bhar se yeh ghadi shuru nahi hoti.

## Advisory se binding rule tak, 2023-2026

India yahan teen kadmon mein pahuncha. 26 December 2023 ko MeitY ne AI deepfakes par badhti chinta ka hawala dekar ek advisory jaari ki. Isme sabhi platforms se kaha gaya ki woh users ko registration ke waqt, har login par aur upload karte samay saaf batayein ki IT Rules ke Rule 3(1)(b) ke under kaunsa content mana hai aur uski saza kya hai [[pib-meity-deepfake-advisory-2023]]. Advisory sirf guidance hoti hai, binding rule nahi. October 2025 mein 10% labels wala draft aaya [[meity-draft-sgi-amendment-2025]]. Aur 10 February 2026 ko binding rules aa gaye.

Inhi saalon mein US ke National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) tak pahunchi generative AI se judi reports 2023 mein lagbhag 4,700 se badh kar 2024 mein 67,000 aur 2025 mein 4 lakh (400,000) se zyada ho gayi. 2025 ki inme se 1,82,000 se zyada reports aise logon ke baare mein thi jinke paas AI se bana child sexual abuse material tha, ya jo use bana rahe the ya banane ki koshish kar rahe the. 2023 se ab tak NCMEC aise material mein dikhaye gaye 275 se zyada bachchon ki pehchaan kar chuka hai [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. Yeh global figures hain, sirf India ke nahi, par inse pata chalta hai ki rules ka muqabla kis cheez se hai.

## Tum aaj kya demand kar sakte ho

Agar tumhari koi synthetic sexual image online dikhe, to tum yeh maang sakte ho:

1. **2 ghante mein removal.** Platform par complaint karo aur likho ki yeh tumhari artificially morphed image hai. Tumhari taraf se koi dost bhi complaint kar sakta hai [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]].
2. **7 din mein faisla,** us content se judi kisi bhi aur grievance par.
3. **Police complaint.** 1930 par call karo ya cybercrime.gov.in par complaint karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. IT Act ke Section 67A ke under sexually explicit material online publish karne par pehli baar mein 5 saal tak ki jail aur 10 lakh rupaye tak ka fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].
4. **Tool ke marker par nazar.** Agar image par AI label ya metadata hai, to police ko batao: jahan technically possible ho, rules ke hisaab se aise markers se us tool ki pehchaan honi chahiye jisne image banayi.
5. **18 se kam ho to aur jaldi.** Yeh baat turant batao: kisi bachche ki sexual image banana ya share karna, chahe woh fake ho, IT Act ke Section 67B ke under punishable hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

Links bhejo, files nahi. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Fake image ko ab law mein naam diya ja sakta hai, use banne se roka ja sakta hai aur hatwaya ja sakta hai; baaki kaam yeh hai ki companies aur police utni hi tezi se chalein jitna rules kehte hain.

india-has-no-sextortion-statistic.en:
Ask how many people in India were sextorted last year, and the honest answer is that nobody knows. Not the police, not the ministries, not the researchers. Sextortion, the crime of threatening to share someone's intimate images unless they pay or obey, has no separate category in the National Crime Records Bureau's data [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]]. The closest line in its tables, "cyber blackmailing or threatening", recorded 601 cases for the entire country in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That number does not measure sextortion. It measures how little of it India writes down.

## The crime that has no column

NCRB's Crime in India counts FIRs registered by police, not complaints, and it counts each FIR only once. Under its "principal offence rule", when one FIR includes several offences, only the most serious one, the offence carrying the maximum punishment, is counted [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A sextortion FIR might involve extortion, an IT Act section on sexual material and a threat. In the published tables it survives as one of them, and none of them is called sextortion.

Then there is the motive. For every cyber crime, police also record a motive at registration: fraud, extortion, sexual exploitation and so on. A sextortion case can be logged as sexual exploitation, as extortion or as fraud, depending on who writes it down [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. The same crime can end up in three different boxes.

## Four places a sextortion case can hide

Follow one case into the tables and it can land in at least four places, none of them labelled sextortion. The rows overlap, so they cannot be added up:

| Where a case can be counted | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cyber crime, motive "sexual exploitation" | 3,434 | 4,199 | 3,190 |
| Cyber crime, motive "extortion" | 3,648 | 3,326 | 2,536 |
| IT Act Section 67A (sexually explicit material) | 1,931 | 2,168 | 2,197 |

The motive figures come from NCRB's yearly snapshots [[ncrb-cii-2022-snapshots]] [[ncrb-cii-2023-snapshots]] [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]], and the Section 67A series from its cyber crime tables [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. The fourth place, "cyber blackmailing or threatening", held 601 cases in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Read across the rows and they disagree. The sexual exploitation motive rose, then fell. Extortion fell every year. Section 67A rose every year. So did sextortion rise or fall? The tables cannot say. In 2024 total cyber crime rose 17.9%, to 1,01,928 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]], yet the share with a sexual exploitation motive dropped from 4.9% to 3.1% [[ncrb-cii-2023-snapshots]] [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. 2024 was also the year the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the IPC, from 1 July, so the legal labels changed halfway through the year. Our guide to reading the first crime data under the BNS explains why that alone makes comparisons with 2023 shaky. A falling line in a system with no category for the crime tells you more about the counting than about the crime.

## What global reports show that Indian data cannot

Where sextortion is counted as a category of its own, the line moves one way. The US-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC), which receives reports from platforms and the public, logged more than 10,000 reports of financially motivated sextortion in 2022 and more than 28,000 in 2023 [[ncmec-sextortion-data-2026]]. In 2024 it received more than 36,000, and in 2025 more than 50,000 reports of financial sextortion of children, an average of 137 a day [[ncmec-sextortion-data-2026]].

These are global reports to an American clearinghouse, not Indian data, and they say nothing directly about India. But they show what a separate category makes visible: the trend, the victims' ages and who comes forward. When the relationship to the victim was known, 94% of sextortion reports made to NCMEC by the public came from the child victim or a parent, most of them from children themselves [[ncmec-sextortion-data-2026]]. Give people a clear place to report a named crime, and victims and their parents use it.

## 'Fewer than 0.5%': the estimate behind the silence

Without data, one estimate has filled the gap. In March 2022, a senior Maharashtra Cyber police officer wrote that India sees more than 500 sextortion cases a day, and that fewer than 0.5% are registered as FIRs [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]]. Two years later, the WeProtect Global Alliance repeated the 500-a-day figure in a briefing [[weprotect-web-of-deceit-2024]]. That is how an op-ed turns into a statistic.

Treat both numbers as what they are: one senior officer's estimates, not measurements. Nobody has counted, so nobody can say whether 0.5% is too high or too low. What the op-ed does capture is the reason for the silence. The officer linked it to victims' shame and social stigma [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]]. The same force that keeps a case out of the police station keeps it out of the statistics.

## What India should start counting

A data system that took sextortion seriously would not need new technology, only new columns:

- **A sextortion flag** on every FIR and every portal complaint, whatever sections are applied, so the principal offence rule cannot hide it.
- **The victim's age and gender.** Global evidence says teenage boys aged 13 to 17 are the main targets of financial sextortion [[weprotect-web-of-deceit-2024]]. Indian tables cannot show whether that holds here.
- **Portal complaints by type.** The national cybercrime portal already counts the categories it names: about 1.94 lakh complaints about child sexual abuse material and rape or gang-rape content had been reported on it by 30 April 2024 [[pib-wcd-ccpwc-2024]]. No published figure says how many of its complaints concern sextortion, or how many of those became FIRs.
- **Money demanded and lost**, and bank accounts frozen.
- **Outcomes.** Of 1,221 cyber blackmailing or threatening cases before the courts in 2024, two ended in conviction and 98% were still pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Until then, nobody can tell a fall in sextortion from a fall in counting. And every person who reports, even without wanting a court case, adds one line to a record that does not yet exist.
india-has-no-sextortion-statistic.hg:
Kisi se poochho ki pichhle saal India mein kitne logon ke saath sextortion hua, toh sach yeh hai ki kisi ko nahi pata. Na police ko, na ministries ko, na researchers ko. Sextortion matlab kisi ki intimate photos ya videos share karne ki dhamki de ke usse paise ya kuch aur karwana. National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ke data mein is crime ki koi alag category hi nahi hai [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]]. Iske sabse kareeb wali line, "cyber blackmailing ya threatening", mein 2024 mein poore desh se sirf 601 cases record hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh number sextortion ko nahi naapta. Yeh dikhata hai ki India iska kitna kam hissa kaagaz pe utaarta hai.

## Woh crime jiska koi column nahi

NCRB ki Crime in India report police mein register hui FIRs ginti hai, complaints nahi, aur har FIR ko sirf ek baar ginti hai. Iske "principal offence rule" ke hisaab se, agar ek FIR mein kai offences hain, toh sirf sabse serious wala, yaani jismein sabse zyada saza hai, gina jaata hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sextortion ki ek FIR mein extortion, sexual content wali IT Act section aur dhamki, teeno ho sakte hain. Published tables mein inmein se sirf ek bachta hai, aur kisi ka naam sextortion nahi hai.

Phir aata hai motive. Har cyber crime ke liye police registration ke waqt ek motive bhi likhti hai: fraud, extortion, sexual exploitation, waghairah. Sextortion ka case sexual exploitation mein bhi likha ja sakta hai, extortion mein bhi aur fraud mein bhi; depend karta hai ki likh kaun raha hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Ek hi crime, teen alag dabbe.

## Chaar jagah jahan sextortion ka case chhup sakta hai

Ek case ko tables mein follow karo, toh woh kam se kam chaar jagah pahunch sakta hai, aur kisi pe bhi sextortion nahi likha. Yeh rows overlap karti hain, isliye inhe joda nahi ja sakta:

| Case kahan gina ja sakta hai | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cyber crime, motive "sexual exploitation" | 3,434 | 4,199 | 3,190 |
| Cyber crime, motive "extortion" | 3,648 | 3,326 | 2,536 |
| IT Act Section 67A (sexually explicit material) | 1,931 | 2,168 | 2,197 |

Motive wale figures NCRB ke saalana snapshots se hain [[ncrb-cii-2022-snapshots]] [[ncrb-cii-2023-snapshots]] [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]], aur Section 67A ki series uski cyber crime tables se [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Chauthi jagah, "cyber blackmailing ya threatening", mein 2024 mein 601 cases the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Rows ko dhyan se padho, toh teeno alag kahani kehti hain. Sexual exploitation wala motive pehle badha, phir ghata. Extortion har saal ghata. Section 67A har saal badha. Toh sextortion badha ya ghata? Tables nahi bata sakti. 2024 mein total cyber crime 17.9% badh ke 1,01,928 cases ho gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]], phir bhi sexual exploitation motive ka share 4.9% se gir ke 3.1% reh gaya [[ncrb-cii-2023-snapshots]] [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. 2024 woh saal bhi tha jab 1 July se Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne IPC ki jagah li, yaani saal ke beech mein hi legal labels badal gaye. BNS ke baad ke pehle crime data ko kaise padhein, is pe humara guide batata hai ki sirf isi wajah se 2023 se comparison kamzor ho jaata hai. Jis system mein crime ki category hi nahi hai, usmein girti line crime se zyada counting ke baare mein batati hai.

## Global reports kya dikhati hain jo Indian data nahi dikha pata

Jahan sextortion ko apni alag category mein gina jaata hai, wahan line ek hi direction mein jaati hai. US ki National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) ko platforms aur public, dono reports bhejte hain. Use financially motivated sextortion ki 2022 mein 10,000 se zyada aur 2023 mein 28,000 se zyada reports mili [[ncmec-sextortion-data-2026]]. 2024 mein 36,000 se zyada mili, aur 2025 mein bachchon ke financial sextortion ki 50,000 se zyada reports aayi, yaani average roz 137 [[ncmec-sextortion-data-2026]].

Yeh duniya bhar se ek American sanstha ko mili reports hain, Indian data nahi, aur yeh India ke baare mein seedha kuch nahi kehti. Lekin yeh dikhati hain ki alag category hone se kya-kya dikhne lagta hai: trend, victims ki umar, aur kaun aage aa ke batata hai. Public ki jin reports mein yeh pata tha ki bhejne wale ka bachche se kya rishta hai, unmein se 94% ya toh khud us bachche ne bheji ya uske parents ne, aur zyadatar bachchon ne khud [[ncmec-sextortion-data-2026]]. Logon ko ek naam wale crime ki report karne ki saaf jagah do, toh victims aur unke parents use karte hain.

## '0.5% se bhi kam': chuppi ke peeche ka andaaza

Jab data hi nahi hai, toh ek andaaze ne yeh khaali jagah bhar di hai. March 2022 mein Maharashtra Cyber police ke ek senior officer ne likha ki India mein roz sextortion ke 500 se zyada cases hote hain, aur unmein se 0.5% se bhi kam mein FIR register hoti hai [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]]. Do saal baad WeProtect Global Alliance ne apni ek briefing mein roz 500 wala figure dohra diya [[weprotect-web-of-deceit-2024]]. Aise hi ek op-ed dheere-dheere statistic ban jaata hai.

Dono numbers ko wahi maano jo woh hain: ek senior officer ke andaaze, measurement nahi. Kisi ne gina hi nahi, isliye koi nahi keh sakta ki 0.5% zyada hai ya kam. Lekin yeh op-ed chuppi ki wajah zaroor pakadta hai. Officer ne ise victims ki sharm aur social stigma se joda [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]]. Jo darr kisi case ko police station se door rakhta hai, wahi use statistics se bhi door rakhta hai.

## India ko kya ginna shuru karna chahiye

Agar data system sextortion ko seriously le, toh use nayi technology nahi chahiye, bas naye columns:

- **Sextortion ka flag** har FIR aur portal ki har complaint pe, chahe koi bhi section lage, taaki principal offence rule ise chhupa na sake.
- **Victim ki umar aur gender.** Global evidence kehta hai ki financial sextortion ka main target 13 se 17 saal ke teenage ladke hain [[weprotect-web-of-deceit-2024]]. Indian tables yeh nahi dikha sakti ki yahan bhi aisa hai ya nahi.
- **Portal complaints type ke hisaab se.** Cybercrime portal un categories ko pehle se ginta hai jinka naam tay hai: 30 April 2024 tak us pe child sexual abuse material aur rape ya gang-rape content ki kareeb 1.94 lakh complaints aa chuki thi [[pib-wcd-ccpwc-2024]]. Lekin koi published figure nahi batata ki uski kitni complaints sextortion ki thi, ya unmein se kitni FIR bani.
- **Kitne paise maange gaye aur kitne gaye**, aur kitne bank accounts freeze hue.
- **Outcome.** 2024 mein courts ke saamne cyber blackmailing ya threatening ke 1,221 cases the; sirf do mein conviction hua, aur 98% saal ke end tak pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Tab tak koi nahi bata sakta ki sextortion sach mein ghata hai ya bas counting ghati hai. Aur har woh insaan jo report karta hai, chahe use court case na chahiye ho, ek aise record mein ek line jodta hai jo abhi bana hi nahi hai.

india-ncmec-reports-ranking-explained.en:
"India tops the world in child sexual abuse reports" is a headline built on real numbers. They come from the CyberTipline of the US-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC), to which technology platforms, and some members of the public, report suspected child sexual exploitation. The ranking is accurate. The conclusion most readers draw from it, that India has more child abuse than anywhere else, is one the data cannot support. Here are the numbers, and how to read them.

## Four years of NCMEC numbers for India

NCMEC attributed 56.8 lakh CyberTipline reports to India in 2022, 89.2 lakh in 2023, 22.5 lakh in 2024 and 19.3 lakh in 2025 [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]]. India had more reports than any other country in the first three of those years, with the Philippines second each time, and was second in 2025 [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]].

| Year | Reports linked to India | India's place |
|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 56,75,324 | First |
| 2023 | 89,23,738 | First |
| 2024 | 22,52,528 | First |
| 2025 | 19,33,900 | Second in reports, first in referrals |

At the 2023 peak, India's 89.2 lakh reports were almost a quarter of the 36.2 million NCMEC received from the whole world [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]].

## First in the world: what the ranking measures

A report is linked to a country by where the suspected upload or user appears to be. NCMEC itself says its country numbers are not indicative of the level of child sexual abuse in a country, and that proxies and anonymisers can distort them; most reports concern uploads of abuse material detected by US platforms [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]]. Three things drive India's place.

**Users.** India has a vast number of people on the platforms that scan and report. Adjusted for population, India's rate is lower than that of several countries [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]].

**Detection.** The counts reflect how hard platforms look and how they report, not how common abuse is [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]].

**Location.** In 2025 the biggest single row in NCMEC's country table was not a country at all but "Unknown", with more reports than either the US or India [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]].

The type of report matters too. In 2025 the US overtook India on total reports, 20,61,893 against 19,33,900. But India stayed first on referrals, the reports with enough information for police action: 17,69,595, against 14,80,183 for the US [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]]. India's referrals had risen from 15,21,666 in 2024 [[ncmec-cybertipline-by-country-2024]]. The headline number fell; the number that matters most to police went up.

## Why the numbers fell in 2024

Worldwide, NCMEC's reports fell from 36.2 million in 2023 to 20.5 million in 2024, then edged up to 21.3 million in 2025 [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. NCMEC said the 2024 drop came from report "bundling" and from some platforms reporting less, not because the crimes stopped [[ncmec-2024-in-numbers-2025]]. Bundling means large platforms combine related reports into one. Counted as separate incidents, 2024's 20.5 million reports came to 29.2 million [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]].

India's fall was far steeper than the world's: from 89.2 lakh to 22.5 lakh in one year. The country table does not show how much of that came from bundling. What it does show is that a ranking built on report counts can swing by tens of lakhs when a few large platforms change how they report.

## What the figures do prove

Strip away the ranking and something hard remains. Year after year, platforms have detected suspected child sexual abuse material being uploaded and shared from accounts in India by the lakh [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]]. Much of that material records real children being abused. The Supreme Court has told Indian courts to stop calling it "child pornography" and to say "child sexual exploitation and abuse material" instead [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]].

Each upload, download or exchange is a crime. Section 67B of the IT Act punishes creating, collecting, browsing, downloading or exchanging such material with up to five years in jail and a fine of up to Rs 10 lakh on a first conviction, and seven years on a repeat [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. On 23 September 2024 the Supreme Court ruled that viewing, storing or possessing it can be an offence too, under Section 15 of POCSO and Section 67B [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]].

What the figures cannot tell you is how many children in India are abused. India has had no national survey of child sexual abuse since the government's 2007 study [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. NCMEC's table keeps being read as that missing measure. It was never built to be one.

## From a US tip-off to an Indian police station

On 26 April 2019, India's National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) signed an agreement with NCMEC to receive its CyberTipline reports [[pib-wcd-ccpwc-2024]]. As the Supreme Court described the route, platforms report to NCMEC, NCMEC passes India-linked reports to NCRB, and NCRB sends them on to the states through the national cybercrime reporting portal [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. More than 69.05 lakh tips had reached states and union territories by 31 March 2024 [[pib-wcd-ccpwc-2024]].

The pipeline can work. The Supreme Court's own 2024 ruling began with an NCMEC tip routed through NCRB to the Tamil Nadu police [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]]. The court also held that platforms reporting abuse material to NCMEC must report it to India's Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police as well [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

But the funnel narrows sharply at the police station. In 2024, when NCMEC linked 15,21,666 referrals to India, police registered 1,036 cases under Section 67B [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Tips and FIRs are different units, so one cannot simply be divided by the other. Still, the gap is where the real question lies: not where India ranks, but how many tips end with an offender charged and a child protected. That is the figure worth demanding.
india-ncmec-reports-ranking-explained.hg:
"India child sexual abuse reports mein duniya mein No. 1" ek aisi headline hai jiske peeche asli numbers hain. Yeh numbers US ke National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) ki CyberTipline se aate hain, jahan technology platforms, aur kuch aam log bhi, suspected child sexual exploitation ki report karte hain. Ranking sahi hai. Par zyada tar log isse jo nateeja nikaalte hain, ki India mein baaki har jagah se zyada child abuse hota hai, data us nateeje ko support nahi karta. Yeh rahe numbers, aur unhe padhne ka sahi tareeka.

## India ke liye NCMEC ke chaar saal ke numbers

NCMEC ne 2022 mein 56.8 lakh, 2023 mein 89.2 lakh, 2024 mein 22.5 lakh aur 2025 mein 19.3 lakh CyberTipline reports India se jodi [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]]. Inme se pehle teen saal India ki reports kisi bhi doosre desh se zyada thin, har baar Philippines doosre number pe tha, aur 2025 mein India doosre number pe aa gaya [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]].

| Saal | India se judi reports | India ki position |
|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 56,75,324 | Pehla |
| 2023 | 89,23,738 | Pehla |
| 2024 | 22,52,528 | Pehla |
| 2025 | 19,33,900 | Reports mein doosra, referrals mein pehla |

2023 ke peak pe India ki 89.2 lakh reports, NCMEC ko poori duniya se mili 36.2 million reports ka lagbhag ek-chauthai thin [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]].

## Duniya mein pehla: ranking asal mein kya naapti hai

Koi report kisi desh se is aadhaar pe judti hai ki suspected upload ya user kahan dikhta hai. NCMEC khud kehta hai ki uske country numbers kisi desh mein child sexual abuse ke level ka sanket nahi hain, aur proxies aur anonymisers inhe bigaad sakte hain; zyada tar reports US platforms ke detect kiye gaye abuse material ke uploads ke baare mein hoti hain [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]]. India ki position teen cheezein tay karti hain.

**Users.** India ke bahut zyada log un platforms pe hain jo scan aur report karte hain. Aabadi ke hisaab se dekhein, toh India ka rate kai deshon se kam hai [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]].

**Detection.** Yeh ginti dikhati hai ki platforms kitni mehnat se dhoondhte hain aur kaise report karte hain, yeh nahi ki abuse kitna aam hai [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]].

**Location.** 2025 mein NCMEC ki country table ki sabse badi row koi desh tha hi nahi, balki "Unknown" thi, jisme US aur India dono se zyada reports thin [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]].

Report ka type bhi maayne rakhta hai. 2025 mein total reports mein US ne India ko peeche chhod diya, 20,61,893 ke muqable 19,33,900. Par referrals mein, yaani woh reports jinme police action ke liye kaafi jaankari hoti hai, India pehle number pe raha: 17,69,595, jabki US ke 14,80,183 the [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]]. 2024 mein India ke referrals 15,21,666 the [[ncmec-cybertipline-by-country-2024]]. Headline wala number gira; police ke liye sabse kaam ka number badha.

## 2024 mein numbers kyun gire

Duniya bhar mein NCMEC ki reports 2023 ke 36.2 million se girkar 2024 mein 20.5 million ho gayi, phir 2025 mein thodi badhkar 21.3 million hui [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. NCMEC ne kaha ki 2024 ki giraavat report "bundling" aur kuch platforms ke kam report karne se aayi, isliye nahi ki crimes ruk gaye [[ncmec-2024-in-numbers-2025]]. Bundling ka matlab hai ki bade platforms judi hui reports ko milakar ek report bana dete hain. Alag-alag incidents ki tarah ginein, toh 2024 ki 20.5 million reports 29.2 million banti hain [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]].

India ki giraavat duniya se kahin zyada tez thi: ek hi saal mein 89.2 lakh se 22.5 lakh. Country table yeh nahi batati ki isme se kitna hissa bundling ki wajah se tha. Par yeh zaroor dikhata hai ki report counts pe bani ranking mein dasiyon lakh ka utaar-chadhaav aa sakta hai, jab kuch bade platforms report karne ka tareeka badal dete hain.

## Figures asal mein kya saabit karte hain

Ranking ko hata do, toh ek kadwa sach bachta hai. Saal dar saal, platforms ne India ke accounts se lakhon ki sankhya mein suspected child sexual abuse material upload aur share hote detect kiya hai [[ncmec-reports-by-country-2025]]. Is material ka bada hissa asli bachchon ke abuse ka record hai. Supreme Court ne Indian courts se kaha hai ki ise "child pornography" kehna band karein aur "child sexual exploitation and abuse material" kahein [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]].

Har upload, download ya exchange ek crime hai. IT Act ka Section 67B aisa material banane, collect, browse, download ya exchange karne pe first conviction mein paanch saal tak ki jail aur Rs 10 lakh tak ka fine, aur dobara conviction pe saat saal tak ki saza deta hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. 23 September 2024 ko Supreme Court ne kaha ki ise dekhna, store karna ya paas rakhna bhi POCSO ke Section 15 aur Section 67B ke under offence ho sakta hai [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]].

Yeh figures jo nahi bata sakte, woh yeh hai ki India mein kitne bachchon ka abuse hota hai. Sarkar ki 2007 ki study ke baad India mein child sexual abuse pe koi national survey nahi hua [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. NCMEC ki table ko baar-baar usi missing naap ki tarah padha jaata hai. Woh is kaam ke liye kabhi bani hi nahi thi.

## US ki tip se Indian police station tak

26 April 2019 ko India ke National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ne NCMEC ki CyberTipline reports lene ke liye uske saath ek agreement sign kiya [[pib-wcd-ccpwc-2024]]. Supreme Court ne yeh rasta aise samjhaya: platforms NCMEC ko report karte hain, NCMEC India se judi reports NCRB ko deta hai, aur NCRB unhe national cybercrime reporting portal ke zariye states ko bhejta hai [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. 31 March 2024 tak 69.05 lakh se zyada tips states aur union territories tak pahunch chuki thin [[pib-wcd-ccpwc-2024]].

Yeh pipeline kaam kar sakti hai. Supreme Court ka apna 2024 wala faisla ek NCMEC tip se hi shuru hua tha, jo NCRB ke zariye Tamil Nadu police tak pahunchi thi [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]]. Court ne yeh bhi kaha ki jo platforms abuse material ki report NCMEC ko karte hain, unhe India ki Special Juvenile Police Unit ya local police ko bhi report karna hoga [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

Par police station tak aate-aate yeh funnel bahut patla ho jaata hai. 2024 mein, jab NCMEC ne 15,21,666 referrals India se jode, police ne Section 67B ke under 1,036 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Tips aur FIRs alag units hain, isliye ek ko doosre se seedha divide nahi kiya ja sakta. Phir bhi asli sawaal isi gap mein hai: India ki ranking kya hai, yeh nahi, balki kitni tips ka ant ek offender pe charge aur ek bachche ki hifaazat mein hota hai. Yahi woh figure hai jo maangna chahiye.

india-porn-ban-timeline-2015-2026.en:
In July 2015, the Supreme Court refused to order porn websites blocked. Within weeks the government ordered 857 of them blocked anyway, then narrowed the order within days. Since 2024 it has gone after a different target, streaming platforms accused of obscene content, blocking 50 in two years while some resurfaced at new web addresses. This timeline follows each attempt and what it achieved. It also separates two things the public debate keeps mixing up: what adults may choose to watch in private, and what is a crime for everyone.

## July-August 2015: a court refuses, a ministry blocks, then retreats

The first push came through a court. In a public interest petition, advocate Kamlesh Vaswani asked the Supreme Court to have pornographic websites blocked. In July 2015 the court declined to pass an interim order. Chief Justice H.L. Dattu observed that the court could not stop an adult from watching pornography in the privacy of their room, calling it a question of personal liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution [[hindu-sc-adult-porn-privacy-2015]].

The government moved anyway. The telecom department ordered internet service providers to block 857 pornographic websites, a block the BBC reported on 3 August 2015. After public outrage, the order was modified within days. By 5 August, providers were asked to block only sites carrying child sexual abuse material [[bbc-india-porn-ban-reversal-2015]].

Within days, then, the state had retreated to the one category the law treats as beyond argument: material that abuses children. That boundary runs through everything that followed.

## 2021-2026: from age checks to the streaming crackdown

The next phase went after streaming platforms rather than porn websites in general, and it began with rules. Since 2021, the Digital Media Ethics Code, part of the IT Rules, has required streaming platforms to provide parental locks for content rated U/A 13+ or higher and a "reliable age verification mechanism" for adult ("A") content [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2026]]. The rules set no comparable age check for other websites that carry adult content, and we found no public record of how the streaming check is enforced.

Then came the blocking orders:

- **March 2024:** the Information and Broadcasting (I&B) Ministry blocked 18 streaming platforms over obscene content [[indiatoday-ott-ban-2025]].
- **July 2025:** the government ordered intermediaries to disable access to 25 more platforms, including Ullu, ALTT and Desiflix, covering 26 websites and 14 apps, for hosting obscene and sexually explicit content. It used powers under the IT Act, 2000 and the IT Rules, 2021 [[indiatoday-ott-ban-2025]]. With the 18 of March 2024, the total stood at 43 by December 2025 [[ls-uq680-2026]].
- **February 2026:** the I&B Ministry blocked five more platforms over allegedly obscene content [[moneycontrol-ott-block-2026]].
- **22 July 2026:** the ministry told the Lok Sabha that 50 platforms had been blocked in two years. It cited Sections 67 and 67A of the IT Act, Section 294 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Indecent Representation of Women Act [[ls-uq680-2026]].

## Mirror domains: why blocked services come back

When the February 2026 order came, officials said platforms blocked in March 2024 had resurfaced on new domains [[moneycontrol-ott-block-2026]]. That is the built-in weakness of blocking. An order names specific web addresses and apps. A new address is not covered until someone notices it and a fresh order is issued. Meanwhile the official count keeps rising: 43 platforms in December 2025, 50 by July 2026 [[ls-uq680-2026]].

Blocking an address does not remove the demand behind it. And demand that people are embarrassed to talk about is an opening for fraud. In 2026, India's cyber crime agency documented one.

## 2026: when 'porn apps' became malware

On 26 August 2026, the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) issued advisory TAU/ADV/018. It warned that fake pornography apps advertised on Facebook and Instagram, under names such as "Night Play", "Reloop" and "Kyss", were being used to take over Android phones and commit financial fraud [[i4c-advisory-porn-apps-2026]]. The advisory describes malicious Android apps posing as pornography apps. Once installed, they use the phone's accessibility permissions to take control of it, and the fraud follows.

The ads ran on two mainstream social media platforms, in the same year the government was still blocking streaming services. Wanting adult content is not a crime. Tapping such an ad can still cost someone their money, in a fraud they may feel too embarrassed to report. Report it anyway: the police are looking for the fraudster, not judging what you searched for.

## What the law actually forbids

This is general information, not legal advice.

The 2015 refusal still describes the position for adults: watching adult pornography in private is not an offence [[hindu-sc-adult-porn-privacy-2015]]. What the law punishes is publishing or sending obscene and sexually explicit material, and anything that involves a child or someone who did not consent:

- **Publishing or sending.** Publishing or transmitting obscene material online carries up to three years in jail and a fine of up to Rs 5 lakh on a first conviction (Section 67 of the IT Act). Sexually explicit material carries up to five years and Rs 10 lakh (Section 67A) [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Forwarding a clip in a group chat is transmitting it.
- **Children.** Section 67B punishes creating, collecting, browsing, downloading or exchanging child sexual abuse material [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. On 23 September 2024 the Supreme Court held that viewing, storing or possessing it is an offence under Section 15 of the POCSO Act and Section 67B, and told courts to stop calling it "child pornography" [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]].
- **Consent.** Capturing or sharing images of a person's private parts without consent is an offence under Section 66E of the IT Act, whoever the person is [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Under Section 77 of the BNS, sharing a private image of a woman without her consent is voyeurism even if she agreed to the image being taken [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Eleven years of blocking orders have not settled the argument about adult content. The lines that protect people were never drawn by a blocking list. They are age and consent: no child, ever, and no one filmed or shared without their agreement. To report a crime on either line, call 1930 or use cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].
india-porn-ban-timeline-2015-2026.hg:
July 2015 mein Supreme Court ne porn websites block karne ka order dene se mana kar diya. Kuch hi hafton mein sarkar ne phir bhi 857 websites block karne ka order de diya, aur phir kuch dinon mein us order ko chhota kar diya. 2024 se sarkar ka nishaana badal gaya: ab woh streaming platforms hain jin pe obscene content ka aarop hai. Do saal mein 50 block hue, aur kuch naye web addresses pe phir se aa gaye. Yeh timeline har koshish aur uske nateeje ko follow karti hai. Saath hi woh do cheezein alag karti hai jinhe public debate baar-baar mila deti hai: adults private mein kya dekhna chunte hain, aur kya sabke liye crime hai.

## July-August 2015: court mana karta hai, ministry block karti hai, phir peeche hatti hai

Pehli koshish court ke zariye hui. Advocate Kamlesh Vaswani ne ek public interest petition mein Supreme Court se pornographic websites block karwane ki maang ki. July 2015 mein court ne interim order dene se mana kar diya. Chief Justice H.L. Dattu ne kaha ki court kisi adult ko apne kamre ki privacy mein pornography dekhne se nahi rok sakta, aur ise Constitution ke Article 21 ke tahat personal liberty ka sawaal bataya [[hindu-sc-adult-porn-privacy-2015]].

Sarkar ne phir bhi kadam uthaya. Telecom department ne internet service providers ko 857 pornographic websites block karne ka order diya, aur BBC ne 3 August 2015 ko is block ki khabar di. Public mein gussa failne ke baad, kuch hi dinon mein order badal diya gaya. 5 August tak providers se sirf woh sites block karne ko kaha gaya jin pe child sexual abuse material tha [[bbc-india-porn-ban-reversal-2015]].

Yaani kuch hi dinon mein sarkar us ek category tak peeche hat gayi jise kanoon kisi bahas ke laayak nahi maanta: woh material jo bachchon ka shoshan karta hai. Yahi seema aage ki har ghatna mein dikhti hai.

## 2021-2026: age checks se streaming crackdown tak

Agla daur porn websites ki jagah streaming platforms ke peeche gaya, aur iski shuruaat rules se hui. 2021 se Digital Media Ethics Code, jo IT Rules ka hissa hai, streaming platforms se U/A 13+ ya usse upar ki rating wale content ke liye parental locks, aur adult ("A") content ke liye "reliable age verification mechanism" maangta hai [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2026]]. Adult content dikhane wali doosri websites ke liye rules mein aisa koi age check nahi hai, aur humein koi public record nahi mila ki streaming wala check kaise lagu hota hai.

Phir blocking orders aaye:

- **March 2024:** Information and Broadcasting (I&B) Ministry ne obscene content ke liye 18 streaming platforms block kiye [[indiatoday-ott-ban-2025]].
- **July 2025:** sarkar ne intermediaries ko 25 aur platforms ka access band karne ka order diya, jinmein Ullu, ALTT aur Desiflix shaamil the, aur jismein 26 websites aur 14 apps aate the. Wajah thi obscene aur sexually explicit content. Iske liye IT Act, 2000 aur IT Rules, 2021 ki powers use hui [[indiatoday-ott-ban-2025]]. March 2024 ke 18 milake, December 2025 tak total 43 ho gaya [[ls-uq680-2026]].
- **February 2026:** I&B Ministry ne kathit obscene content ke liye paanch aur platforms block kiye [[moneycontrol-ott-block-2026]].
- **22 July 2026:** ministry ne Lok Sabha ko bataya ki do saal mein 50 platforms block hue hain. Isne IT Act ke Sections 67 aur 67A, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 294 aur Indecent Representation of Women Act ka hawala diya [[ls-uq680-2026]].

## Mirror domains: blocked services laut kyun aati hain

February 2026 ka order aaya toh officials ne kaha ki March 2024 mein block hue platforms naye domains pe phir se aa gaye the [[moneycontrol-ott-block-2026]]. Blocking ki yahi andar se bani kamzori hai. Order mein specific web addresses aur apps ke naam hote hain. Naya address tab tak cover nahi hota jab tak koi use notice karke naya order na nikaale. Is beech official ginti badhti ja rahi hai: December 2025 mein 43 platforms, July 2026 tak 50 [[ls-uq680-2026]].

Ek address block karne se uske peeche ki demand khatam nahi hoti. Aur jis demand ke baare mein log baat karne mein sharmaate hain, woh fraud ke liye ek mauka hai. 2026 mein India ki cyber crime agency ne aisa hi ek mauka darj kiya.

## 2026: jab 'porn apps' malware ban gaye

26 August 2026 ko Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) ne advisory TAU/ADV/018 jaari ki. Isne chetaavni di ki Facebook aur Instagram pe "Night Play", "Reloop" aur "Kyss" jaise naamon se advertise kiye ja rahe nakli pornography apps se Android phones pe kabza kiya ja raha hai aur financial fraud ho raha hai [[i4c-advisory-porn-apps-2026]]. Advisory aise malicious Android apps ke baare mein hai jo pornography apps hone ka naatak karte hain. Install hone ke baad yeh phone ki accessibility permissions use karke us pe control le lete hain, aur phir fraud hota hai.

Yeh ads do mainstream social media platforms pe chal rahe the, usi saal jab sarkar streaming services block kar hi rahi thi. Adult content chahna crime nahi hai. Phir bhi aisa ek ad tap karna kisi ke paise le ja sakta hai, aise fraud mein jise report karne mein woh sharmaaye. Phir bhi report karo: police fraudster ko dhoondh rahi hai, yeh nahi dekh rahi ki tumne kya search kiya.

## Kanoon asal mein kya mana karta hai

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Adults ke liye 2015 ka faisla aaj bhi situation batata hai: private mein adult pornography dekhna offence nahi hai [[hindu-sc-adult-porn-privacy-2015]]. Kanoon jis cheez ki saza deta hai, woh hai obscene aur sexually explicit material publish karna ya bhejna, aur aisa kuch bhi jismein koi bachcha ho ya koi aisa insaan jisne consent nahi diya:

- **Publish karna ya bhejna.** Online obscene material publish ya transmit karne pe pehli baar mein teen saal tak ki jail aur 5 lakh rupaye tak ka fine hai (IT Act ka Section 67). Sexually explicit material pe paanch saal tak ki jail aur 10 lakh rupaye (Section 67A) [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Group chat mein koi clip forward karna bhi use transmit karna hai.
- **Bachche.** Section 67B child sexual abuse material banane, ikattha karne, browse karne, download karne ya exchange karne ki saza deta hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. 23 September 2024 ko Supreme Court ne kaha ki use dekhna, store karna ya apne paas rakhna POCSO Act ke Section 15 aur Section 67B ke tahat offence hai, aur courts se kaha ki ise "child pornography" kehna band karein [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]].
- **Consent.** Kisi bhi insaan ke private parts ki images bina consent ke kheenchna ya share karna IT Act ke Section 66E ke tahat offence hai, woh insaan koi bhi ho [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. BNS ke Section 77 ke tahat kisi aurat ki private image uski marzi ke bina share karna voyeurism hai, chahe usne image khinchwane ke liye haan kaha ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Gyarah saal ke blocking orders adult content wali bahas ko suljha nahi paaye. Logon ko bachane wali lines kabhi blocking list ne kheenchi hi nahi. Woh lines hain umar aur consent: koi bachcha kabhi nahi, aur koi bhi insaan uski marzi ke bina film ya share nahi. In dono mein se kisi bhi line ka crime report karna ho toh 1930 pe call karo ya cybercrime.gov.in use karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

is-it-cyberstalking-bns-section-78.en:
Imagine a 19-year-old in Pune. A senior from her coaching class asks her out, and she says no. He keeps messaging, so she blocks him. The next morning a follow request arrives from an account with no photo. By the end of the month there have been six accounts, and one asks why she was at a café on Saturday.

People around her may call it a crush, or "just the internet". The law has a harder word. Stalking became a separate offence in India only in 2013 [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]], and since 1 July 2024 it has been Section 78 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. Here are straight answers. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Is messaging from new accounts after a 'no' really stalking?

It can be. Section 78 describes stalking in two ways [[indiacode-bns-2023]]: a man who follows a woman and contacts her, or tries to, repeatedly to foster personal interaction despite a clear indication that she is not interested; or a man who monitors a woman's use of the internet, email or any other electronic communication.

A "no" followed by a block is about as clear an indication as exists, and a fresh account built to get around the block is the "repeatedly, despite" the section is written for. Watching her through fake accounts, or turning up where she posted she would be, can point to the following and monitoring it describes. Whether a pattern meets the test is for police and courts to decide, which is why your record matters.

The penalty is up to three years in prison on a first conviction and up to five for a repeat [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police registered 9,865 stalking cases in 2024, 1.4 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB's cyber-crime tables separately record 1,240 cases of cyber stalking or bullying of women and children, down from 1,471 in 2022 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A falling count is not a falling problem: most online harassment is never reported.

## What should I save before I block or report?

Save first, block second. An account that is renamed or deleted can take its username and messages with it.

- **Every message**, as screenshots showing the date, time and username, not just the display name.
- **Each profile**, screenshotted, with its link or handle copied into a note.
- **Your "no":** the message where you refused, or the date you first blocked him. It shows the "clear indication" the law asks for.
- **A screen recording** scrolling through the whole chat, so nothing looks cut.
- **A log:** date, time, platform, account, what happened, who saw it. Add offline incidents too, such as calls from unknown numbers.

Keep copies off your phone, with a friend or in your email. Do not reply or threaten him back: it gives him the contact he wants.

## Where do I file, and who must record it?

Use three routes at once.

**The platform.** Report every new account. It builds a record and can shut accounts down.

**The cyber crime portal.** File at cybercrime.gov.in or call the toll-free helpline 1930 [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]], and save the acknowledgement number. A portal complaint is not, by itself, an FIR.

**The police.** Under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), you can report at any police station, wherever the offence happened (a Zero FIR), or electronically (an e-FIR), which is taken on record once you sign it within three days. You must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. When a woman reports stalking, a woman officer must record it [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Say: "I want to report stalking under Section 78 of the BNS. Please register an FIR, recorded by a woman officer."

One catch. Because stalking carries up to three years on a first conviction, Section 173(3) may allow police, with a Deputy Superintendent's permission, to hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days before registering it [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Ask whether one has been ordered.

## What if the stalker is not a man, or I am not a woman?

Then Section 78, as written, does not fit. Like sexual harassment, stalking under the BNS can only be committed by a man against a woman [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. That is despite the Home Ministry's July 2024 claim that various offences had been made gender-neutral, "covering all victims and perpetrators regardless of gender" [[pib-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. A man hounded by an ex, a woman stalked by another woman, a non-binary student chased across accounts: none is covered.

Other routes remain. If you are under 18, POCSO protects you whatever your gender [[pocso-act-2012]]. If you are transgender, Section 18(d) of the Transgender Persons Act punishes harming a transgender person's safety or well-being, including sexual, verbal and emotional abuse, but only with six months to two years [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Section 66E of the IT Act, on capturing or sharing images of private parts without consent, covers every gender [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Threats of harm can be reported to the police whatever your gender. Platform reports and 1930 work for everyone.

## What happens after the FIR?

As soon as police learn of the offence, a magistrate, as far as practicable a woman, must record your statement [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. If the defence tries to put your past on trial, the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam says a victim's character or previous sexual experience is not relevant to consent in a stalking prosecution [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Then comes the wait. In 2024, courts convicted in 25.2% of completed stalking trials, and 52,273 stalking cases, 92.8% of those before the courts, were still pending at year end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Online cases fare worse: of 4,348 cyber stalking and bullying cases against women and children before the courts, only 33 ended in conviction, a 22.8% rate among completed trials, and 95.3% were still pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

So treat the FIR as protection as much as punishment: a case on record, an officer he must answer to, a file every new account adds to. Keep logging, send each new incident to the investigating officer, and if you fear for your physical safety, call 112.
is-it-cyberstalking-bns-section-78.hg:
Socho, Pune ki ek 19 saal ki ladki hai. Coaching class ka ek senior use date par chalne ko kehta hai, aur woh mana kar deti hai. Woh message karta rehta hai, toh woh use block kar deti hai. Agle din subah bina photo wale ek account se follow request aati hai. Mahine ke end tak chhe account ho chuke hote hain, aur unmein se ek poochhta hai ki woh Saturday ko café mein kyun thi.

Uske aas-paas ke log ise crush keh sakte hain, ya "bas internet hai". Law ke paas iske liye ek sakht shabd hai. India mein stalking 2013 mein jaakar ek alag offence bana [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]], aur 1 July 2024 se yeh Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 78 hai [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. Yahan seedhe jawab hain. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahin.

## Kya 'na' ke baad naye accounts se message karna sach mein stalking hai?

Ho sakta hai. Section 78 stalking ko do tarah se describe karta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Pehla: woh aadmi jo kisi woman ka peecha karta hai aur personal interaction badhane ke liye baar-baar usse contact karta hai, ya karne ki koshish karta hai, jabki woman saaf ishaara de chuki hai ki woh interested nahin hai. Doosra: woh aadmi jo kisi woman ke internet, email ya kisi bhi electronic communication ke use ko monitor karta hai.

'Na' ke baad block se zyada saaf ishaara mushkil se milega, aur block se bachne ke liye banaya gaya naya account wahi "baar-baar, phir bhi" hai jiske liye yeh section likha gaya hai. Fake accounts se uspar nazar rakhna, ya wahan pahunch jaana jahan usne post kiya tha ki woh hogi, us peecha karne aur monitor karne ki taraf ishaara kar sakta hai jiski baat section karta hai. Koi pattern is test par khara utarta hai ya nahin, yeh police aur court tay karte hain, isliye tumhara record itna zaroori hai.

Saza hai pehli conviction par teen saal tak ki jail aur dobara conviction par paanch saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police ne 2024 mein stalking ke 9,865 cases darj kiye, yaani 1.4 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB ki cyber crime tables alag se women aur bachchon ki cyber stalking ya bullying ke 1,240 cases record karti hain, jo 2022 mein 1,471 the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ginti ka girna problem ka girna nahin hai: zyadatar online harassment kabhi report hi nahin hota.

## Block ya report karne se pehle kya save karun?

Pehle save, phir block. Jo account apna naam badal le ya delete ho jaaye, woh apna username aur messages bhi saath le ja sakta hai.

- **Har message** ka screenshot, jismein date, time aur username dikhe, sirf display name nahin.
- **Har profile** ka screenshot, aur uska link ya handle ek note mein copy karke rakho.
- **Tumhara "na":** woh message jismein tumne mana kiya, ya woh date jab tumne use pehli baar block kiya. Isse woh "saaf ishaara" dikhta hai jo law maangta hai.
- **Ek screen recording**, poori chat scroll karte hue, taaki kuch bhi kata hua na lage.
- **Ek log:** date, time, platform, account, kya hua, kisne dekha. Offline incidents bhi jodo, jaise unknown numbers se aaye calls.

Copies phone ke bahar bhi rakho, kisi dost ke paas ya apne email mein. Reply mat karo, palat kar dhamki bhi mat do: isse use wahi contact mil jaata hai jo woh chahta hai.

## Complaint kahan karun, aur use record kaun karega?

Teeno raaste ek saath use karo.

**Platform.** Har naye account ko report karo. Isse record banta hai aur accounts band ho sakte hain.

**Cyber crime portal.** cybercrime.gov.in par complaint karo ya toll-free helpline 1930 par call karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]], aur acknowledgement number save karo. Portal ki complaint apne aap mein FIR nahin hoti.

**Police.** Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 173 ke under kisi bhi police station mein report ki ja sakti hai, offence chahe kahin bhi hua ho (Zero FIR), ya electronically (e-FIR), jo tab record par aati hai jab tum teen din ke andar us par sign kar do. FIR ki copy tumhe free milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jab koi woman stalking report kare, toh use woman officer hi record karegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Bolo: "Mujhe BNS ke Section 78 ke under stalking report karni hai. Please FIR darj kijiye, aur use woman officer record karein."

Ek catch hai. Kyunki pehli conviction par stalking ki saza teen saal tak hai, Section 173(3) police ko Deputy Superintendent ki permission se case darj karne se pehle 14 din tak ki preliminary enquiry karne ki chhoot de sakta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Poochho ki kya aisi enquiry ka order hua hai.

## Agar stalker aadmi nahin hai, ya main woman nahin hoon, toh?

Toh Section 78, jaisa likha hai, fit nahin hota. Sexual harassment ki tarah, BNS mein stalking sirf ek aadmi hi kisi woman ke khilaaf kar sakta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh tab hai jab Home Ministry ne July 2024 mein daawa kiya tha ki kai offences gender-neutral bana diye gaye hain, "covering all victims and perpetrators regardless of gender", yaani har gender ke victims aur accused par lagu [[pib-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. Ex ke peecha na chhodne se pareshaan ek aadmi, doosri woman ki stalking jhelti ek woman, ek non-binary student jiska har naye account se peecha hota hai: inmein se koi cover nahin hota.

Doosre raaste phir bhi hain. Agar tum 18 se kam ho, toh POCSO tumhe protect karta hai, tumhara gender kuch bhi ho [[pocso-act-2012]]. Agar tum transgender ho, toh Transgender Persons Act ka Section 18(d) kisi transgender insaan ki safety ya well-being ko nuksaan pahunchane par, sexual, verbal aur emotional abuse samet, saza deta hai, lekin sirf chhe mahine se do saal tak [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Bina consent private parts ki images lena ya share karna IT Act ke Section 66E ke under aata hai, gender chahe koi bhi ho [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Nuksaan pahunchane ki dhamkiyan police ko report ki ja sakti hain, tumhara gender kuch bhi ho. Platform reports aur 1930 sabke liye kaam karte hain.

## FIR ke baad kya hota hai?

Jaise hi police ko offence ka pata chalta hai, ek magistrate ko, jahan tak ho sake woman magistrate ko, tumhara statement record karna hoga [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Agar defence tumhare past ko hi trial par daalne ki koshish kare, toh Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam kehta hai ki stalking ke case mein victim ka character ya pichhla sexual experience consent ke sawaal par relevant nahin hai [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Phir shuru hota hai intezaar. 2024 mein courts ne poore hue stalking trials mein se 25.2% mein conviction diya, aur saal ke end mein stalking ke 52,273 cases, yaani court mein pade cases ka 92.8%, abhi bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Online cases ka haal aur bura hai: court ke saamne women aur bachchon ke cyber stalking aur bullying ke 4,348 cases mein se sirf 33 conviction par khatam hue, poore hue trials mein 22.8% ki rate, aur 95.3% abhi bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Isliye FIR ko jitna saza ka raasta samjho, utna hi protection ka: record par ek case, ek officer jise use jawab dena hai, aur ek file jismein har naya account judta jaata hai. Log rakhte raho, har naya incident investigating officer ko bhejo, aur agar apni physical safety ka darr lage, toh 112 call karo.

it-act-66e-67-67a-67b-explained.en:
Four sections of the Information Technology Act, 2000 deal with sexual images and videos online: 66E, 67, 67A and 67B. They sound alike. They are not. In 2024, police registered 2,914 cases under Section 67, 2,197 under 67A and 1,036 under 67B, but only 436 under 66E [[ncrb-cii-2024]], the one section written around consent and the privacy of the body. Here is what each covers, where the new criminal code fits in, and why the section on the paper matters. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Section 66E: privacy of the body

Section 66E punishes anyone who "intentionally or knowingly captures, publishes or transmits the image of a private area of any person without his or her consent, under circumstances violating the privacy of that person". The maximum is three years in prison, a fine of up to Rs 2 lakh, or both [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

Three things make it different. It turns on consent, not on whether an image is "obscene". It covers capturing as well as sharing, so a phone hidden in a trial room and a forward in a group chat can both fall under it. And it protects "any person": women, men and transgender people alike.

Its weakness is the punishment. There is no minimum sentence, and a conviction can end in a fine alone. Its low count is partly about counting, too: NCRB records each FIR only once, under its most serious offence [[ncrb-cii-2024]], so a case that also invokes Section 67A, which carries a longer maximum, is likely to be counted there instead.

## Sections 67 and 67A: obscene and sexually explicit material

Section 67 covers publishing or transmitting obscene material online: up to three years and a fine of up to Rs 5 lakh on first conviction, and up to five years on a repeat. Section 67A is the heavier version for sexually explicit material: up to five years and Rs 10 lakh, and up to seven years on a repeat conviction [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

These are the sections police reach for most. Cases under 67A rose from 1,931 in 2022 to 2,168 in 2023 and 2,197 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. But notice the question they ask: is the material obscene or sexually explicit? Not: did the person in it agree? They are content laws, written around obscenity rather than consent.

For a victim, that framing has a cost. The case has to prove what the material shows, when the real wrong was that it was shared without consent.

## Section 67B: anything involving under-18s

Section 67B covers material depicting children, meaning anyone under 18, and it reaches far beyond publishing. It punishes creating, collecting, browsing, downloading or exchanging such material, enticing children into online sexual relationships, and recording abuse, with up to five years and a Rs 10 lakh fine on first conviction and seven years on a repeat [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

In 2024, in the Just Rights for Children Alliance case, the Supreme Court held that viewing, storing or possessing child sexual abuse material is an offence under Section 15 of the POCSO Act and under Section 67B, and told courts to stop using the term "child pornography" [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]]. The rule for a teenager or college student is blunt: a sexual image of anyone under 18 is abuse material in law, whoever took it. Do not forward it. Do not keep it. Report it.

The cases barely move. Of 2,885 Section 67B cases before Indian courts in 2024, trials were completed in only 156, with 57 convictions, and 94.5% were still pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Where BNS Section 77 fits

The criminal code has its own offence for the same harm. Since 1 July 2024, when the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced the Indian Penal Code [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]], it is Section 77, voyeurism, which makes it a crime to share a private image of a woman without her consent, even if she agreed to the image being taken [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. So one act can fall under 66E and Section 77 at once, but the two are not the same:

| | IT Act Section 66E | BNS Section 77 |
|---|---|---|
| Who it protects | Any person | Women and girls |
| First conviction | Up to 3 years, a fine up to Rs 2 lakh, or both | 1 to 3 years in prison |
| Repeat conviction | No separate penalty | 3 to 7 years |

The BNS defines a "woman" as a female of any age [[indiacode-bns-2023]], so Section 77 covers girls too. It also carries procedural protections: a woman's complaint of voyeurism must be recorded by a woman officer [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], and in a Section 77 prosecution her character or previous sexual experience is not relevant to the question of consent [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. For men and transgender people, 66E remains the main route.

## Which section fits your case

A rough map, not a substitute for a lawyer:

- **Someone secretly photographed or filmed your body in a private moment:** 66E, and for a woman or girl, Section 77.
- **You agreed to an intimate photo, and it was shared without your consent:** 66E, and for a woman or girl, Section 77.
- **A sexually explicit image or video of you was posted or sent around:** 67A as well.
- **The person in the image is under 18:** 67B, with the POCSO Act.
- **Someone keeps sending you obscene material:** 67.

When you report, describe every element: the capture, each share, any threat, and the age of the person in the image, so the FIR can carry every section that fits. Then ask which sections were applied, and read the copy of the FIR you must be given free [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

And be ready for a long wait. Of 19,731 cases under the obscenity sections before Indian courts in 2024, 601 ended in conviction and 94.7% were still pending at year end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Complaints can be made on the cyber crime helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].
it-act-66e-67-67a-67b-explained.hg:
Information Technology Act, 2000 ke chaar sections online sexual images aur videos se deal karte hain: 66E, 67, 67A aur 67B. Sunne mein ek jaise lagte hain. Hain nahi. 2024 mein police ne Section 67 ke under 2,914 cases, 67A ke under 2,197 aur 67B ke under 1,036 cases register kiye, par 66E ke under sirf 436 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], jabki yahi akela section hai jo consent aur body ki privacy ke around likha gaya hai. Neeche samjho ki har section kya cover karta hai, naya criminal code kahan fit hota hai, aur kagaz pe likha section kyun maayne rakhta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Section 66E: body ki privacy

Section 66E use punish karta hai jo "intentionally or knowingly captures, publishes or transmits the image of a private area of any person without his or her consent, under circumstances violating the privacy of that person". Yaani jo jaan-boojhkar kisi ke private area ki image bina consent ke khinche, publish kare ya aage bheje, aisi situation mein jahan us insaan ki privacy toot rahi ho. Maximum saza teen saal ki jail, Rs 2 lakh tak ka fine, ya dono hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

Teen cheezein ise alag banati hain. Yeh consent pe tika hai, is baat pe nahi ki image "obscene" hai ya nahi. Yeh capture aur share dono ko cover karta hai, isliye trial room mein chhupa phone aur group chat mein kiya gaya forward, dono iske under aa sakte hain. Aur yeh "any person" ko protect karta hai: women, men aur transgender log, sabko barabar.

Iski kamzori hai saza. Koi minimum sentence nahi hai, aur conviction sirf fine pe bhi khatam ho sakta hai. Iska kam count kuch had tak ginti ke tareeke ki wajah se bhi hai: NCRB har FIR ko sirf ek baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke neeche [[ncrb-cii-2024]], isliye jis case mein Section 67A bhi laga ho, jiski maximum saza lambi hai, woh shayad wahin gina jaata hai.

## Sections 67 aur 67A: obscene aur sexually explicit material

Section 67 online obscene material publish ya transmit karne ko cover karta hai: pehli conviction pe teen saal tak ki jail aur Rs 5 lakh tak ka fine, aur dobara conviction pe paanch saal tak. Section 67A sexually explicit material ke liye iska bhaari version hai: paanch saal tak aur Rs 10 lakh, aur dobara conviction pe saat saal tak [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

Police sabse zyada inhi sections ka use karti hai. 67A ke cases 2022 mein 1,931 se badhkar 2023 mein 2,168 aur 2024 mein 2,197 ho gaye [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Par dhyaan do ki yeh sections kya sawaal poochte hain: kya material obscene ya sexually explicit hai? Yeh nahi ki kya image wale insaan ne haan kaha tha. Yeh content laws hain, jo consent ke bajaye obscenity ke around likhe gaye hain.

Victim ke liye is framing ki ek keemat hai. Case ko yeh prove karna padta hai ki material mein kya dikh raha hai, jabki asli galti yeh thi ki use bina consent share kiya gaya.

## Section 67B: 18 se kam umar walon se judi har cheez

Section 67B us material ko cover karta hai jisme bachche dikhaaye gaye hon, yaani 18 se kam umar ka koi bhi insaan, aur yeh sirf publish karne se kahin aage jaata hai. Yeh aisa material banana, collect karna, browse karna, download karna ya exchange karna, bachchon ko online sexual relationships mein phansana, aur abuse record karna, sab punish karta hai: pehli conviction pe paanch saal tak aur Rs 10 lakh fine, aur dobara pe saat saal [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

2024 mein, Just Rights for Children Alliance case mein, Supreme Court ne kaha ki child sexual abuse material dekhna, store karna ya apne paas rakhna POCSO Act ke Section 15 aur Section 67B ke under offence hai, aur courts se "child pornography" term ka use band karne ko kaha [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]]. Kisi teenager ya college student ke liye rule seedha hai: 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi insaan ki sexual image law mein abuse material hai, chahe kisi ne bhi li ho. Ise forward mat karo. Apne paas mat rakho. Report karo.

Cases mushkil se aage badhte hain. 2024 mein Indian courts ke saamne Section 67B ke 2,885 cases the; inme se sirf 156 mein trial poora hua, 57 mein conviction hua, aur saal ke end tak 94.5% pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## BNS Section 77 kahan fit hota hai

Criminal code mein bhi isi harm ke liye apna offence hai. 1 July 2024 se, jab Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne Indian Penal Code ki jagah li [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]], yeh Section 77 hai, yaani voyeurism, jo kisi woman ki private image bina uske consent share karne ko crime banata hai, chahe usne image lene ke liye haan kaha ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Toh ek hi kaam 66E aur Section 77 dono mein aa sakta hai, par dono ek jaise nahi hain:

| | IT Act Section 66E | BNS Section 77 |
|---|---|---|
| Kise protect karta hai | Kisi bhi insaan ko | Women aur girls ko |
| Pehli conviction | 3 saal tak, Rs 2 lakh tak fine, ya dono | 1 se 3 saal ki jail |
| Dobara conviction | Koi alag saza nahi | 3 se 7 saal |

BNS "woman" ko kisi bhi umar ki female ke roop mein define karta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], isliye Section 77 girls ko bhi cover karta hai. Iske saath kuch procedural protections bhi laagu hoti hain: voyeurism ki complaint agar woman kar rahi hai, toh use woman officer hi record karegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], aur Section 77 ke case mein uska character ya pichhla sexual experience consent ke sawaal pe relevant nahi hai [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. Men aur transgender logon ke liye 66E hi main raasta hai.

## Tumhare case mein kaunsa section fit hota hai

Ek rough map, lawyer ka substitute nahi:

- **Kisi ne chupke se private moment mein tumhari body ki photo ya video li:** 66E, aur woman ya girl ke case mein Section 77 bhi.
- **Tumne intimate photo ke liye haan kaha, aur use bina consent share kar diya gaya:** 66E, aur woman ya girl ke case mein Section 77 bhi.
- **Tumhari sexually explicit image ya video post ki gayi ya ghumayi gayi:** saath mein 67A bhi.
- **Image wala insaan 18 se kam hai:** 67B, POCSO Act ke saath.
- **Koi tumhe baar-baar obscene material bhej raha hai:** 67.

Report karte waqt har hissa batao: image kaise li gayi, har share, koi dhamki, aur image wale insaan ki age, taaki FIR mein har fit hone wala section lag sake. Phir poocho ki kaun se sections lage, aur FIR ki woh copy padho jo tumhe free mein deni hi padti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Aur lambe intezaar ke liye taiyaar raho. 2024 mein Indian courts ke saamne obscenity sections ke 19,731 cases the; inme se 601 mein conviction hua aur saal ke end tak 94.7% pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Complaint cyber crime helpline 1930 pe ya cybercrime.gov.in pe ki ja sakti hai [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

loan-app-morphed-photo-harassment.en:
Consider this situation. A 24-year-old in Hyderabad borrows a small amount through an instant-loan app, tapping "allow" on every permission screen to get the money faster. A few days after the due date, a WhatsApp message arrives: her own face, cut from a selfie, on a naked body. Below it are names from her phone: her mother, her manager, her cousin. "Pay today or they all get this."

The image is fake. The threat is a crime. And the law is more on her side than the blackmailer wants her to believe. Police data barely registers this abuse: in all of India in 2024, police registered 293 cases of cyber defamation or morphing against women and 370 of cyber blackmail or threats against women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB counts FIRs, not complaints, and online sexual abuse is heavily under-reported. This guide is general information, not legal advice.

## How the threat works: contacts, morphs and shame

The method needs three things, and an app given every permission may already hold two: your contact list and a photo of your face. The third is your fear. The contact list is the audience. Any ordinary selfie or profile photo is enough raw material for a morph. You never need to have sent an intimate photo for this to happen to you.

In the example above, everything is built to rush her: a deadline measured in hours, and names chosen because they matter most to her. The aim is to make paying feel easier than explaining.

Nothing here depends on gender: anyone can be targeted, though the NCRB counts above cover crimes against women only.

## What the law says about morphed images

Indian law names this exact harm. Rule 3(2)(b) of the IT Rules, 2021 covers content that shows a person in full or partial nudity or in a sexual act, or impersonates them, "including artificially morphed images" of that person [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]]. Since 20 February 2026, a platform must remove such content within two hours of that person's complaint, down from 24 hours [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Sending the morph can be a crime too. Under the IT Act, publishing or transmitting obscene material online carries up to three years and a fine of up to Rs 5 lakh on first conviction; sexually explicit material, up to five years and up to Rs 10 lakh, and seven years on a repeat conviction [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. The takedown rule already names morphed images, so "it was only a fake" does not make the harm lawful.

Money demanded under threat is the kind of case police log as extortion. They recorded extortion as the motive in 2,536 cyber crime cases in 2024, and sexual exploitation in 3,190 [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. A debt changes none of this: no law allows a lender to make sexual images of you or threaten to send them.

## Paying under threat: what it does and does not buy

Paying does not buy deletion. A morph can be remade at any time from any photo of you, so "we deleted it" is a promise nobody can check. Paying also teaches the person threatening you that threats work.
