Be honest about the slow road too. Of 1,221 cyber blackmail or threat cases before Indian courts in 2024, only two ended in conviction, and 98% were still pending at year end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A conviction, if it comes, will come late. That is why the steps below put warning people and removing images first: they work in hours, not years.

If you did borrow, keep your own record of the amount, the app and every repayment with its transaction ID. It helps police separate a loan from the crime built on top of it.

## Warn your contacts, then report on 1930

The blackmail works only if your contacts see the image before they hear from you. Reverse the order. Send a short message to family, close friends and, if needed, your workplace: "A loan app has stolen my contact list and is sending fake, edited photos of me to scare me into paying. If you get anything, it is fake. Don't open, forward or reply. Send me a screenshot of the number, then delete it." Call the one or two people whose reaction you fear most first.

Then report. Call 1930, the toll-free cyber crime helpline, or file at cybercrime.gov.in, the national portal run by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. Put both crimes in one complaint: the money demand, with every phone number, payment ID and the app's name, and the morphed images. Keep the acknowledgement number [[cybercrime-portal]]. Under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, you can also report at any police station, wherever the offence took place, and get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Save evidence before you clean up: screenshots of the app's page, the loan terms, the permissions it asked for, and every message and caller. Then remove the app's access to your contacts and photos, and uninstall it.

## Getting the images taken down in two hours

If the morph is posted anywhere public, such as a page, a fake profile or a group, use the platform's complaint form and name the rule. A Rule 3(2)(b) complaint can come from you or anyone on your behalf [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]], so a friend who spots the post can file it. Write: "This is an artificially morphed sexual image of me, shared without consent. Rule 3(2)(b), IT Rules: remove within two hours." Add every link and note the time you sent it [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Images sent privately are harder to reach, because a platform cannot see inside encrypted chats. There, your early message is the main defence: ask contacts to report the sender's account in the app and block it.

Shame is meant to make you feel alone, but you did nothing wrong. If the pressure becomes too much, Tele-MANAS on 14416 offers free counselling round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

The image is fake. The fear is real, and it is the only thing the blackmailer is really selling.
loan-app-morphed-photo-harassment.hg:
Yeh situation socho. Hyderabad ki ek 24 saal ki ladki ek instant-loan app se chhota sa amount udhaar leti hai, aur paise jaldi milein isliye har permission screen pe "allow" daba deti hai. Due date ke kuch din baad ek WhatsApp message aata hai: uska apna chehra, ek selfie se kaata hua, ek nangi body pe laga hua. Neeche uske phone ke naam likhe hain: uski mummy, uska manager, uska cousin. "Aaj pay karo, warna sabko yeh milega."

Image fake hai. Dhamki crime hai. Aur law us blackmailer ki soch se kahin zyada uski taraf hai. Police data mein yeh abuse mushkil se dikhta hai: 2024 mein poore India mein police ne women ke khilaf cyber defamation ya morphing ke 293 cases aur cyber blackmail ya dhamki ke 370 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB FIRs ginta hai, complaints nahi, aur online sexual abuse bahut kam report hota hai. Yeh guide general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Dhamki kaise kaam karti hai: contacts, morphs aur sharm

Is tareeke ko teen cheezein chahiye, aur jis app ko har permission mil gayi, uske paas do pehle se ho sakti hain: tumhari contact list aur tumhare chehre ki photo. Teesri cheez hai tumhara darr. Contact list audience hai. Koi bhi normal selfie ya profile photo morph banane ke liye kaafi raw material hai. Iske liye zaroori nahi ki tumne kabhi koi intimate photo bheji ho.

Upar wale example mein sab kuch use hadbadi mein daalne ke liye bana hai: ghanton mein naapi gayi deadline, aur woh naam jo uske liye sabse zyada matter karte hain. Maqsad yeh hai ki samjhaane se aasaan paise dena lage.

Ismein gender se kuch fark nahi padta: koi bhi target ho sakta hai, bas upar wale NCRB counts sirf women ke khilaf crimes ginte hain.

## Morphed images pe law kya kehta hai

Indian law is nuksaan ka seedha naam leta hai. IT Rules, 2021 ka Rule 3(2)(b) aise content pe laagu hota hai jo kisi ko poora ya aadha nude ya sexual act mein dikhaye, ya uska impersonation kare, "including artificially morphed images", yaani us insaan ki artificially morph ki gayi images samet [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]]. 20 February 2026 se platform ko aisa content us insaan ki complaint ke 2 ghante ke andar hatana hota hai; pehle yeh time 24 ghante tha [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Morph bhejna bhi crime ho sakta hai. IT Act ke under online obscene material publish ya transmit karne pe pehli conviction mein 3 saal tak ki jail aur Rs 5 lakh tak ka fine ho sakta hai; sexually explicit material pe 5 saal tak aur Rs 10 lakh tak, aur dobara conviction pe 7 saal tak [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Takedown rule khud morphed images ka naam leta hai, isliye "photo toh fake thi" kehne se nuksaan legal nahi ho jaata.

Dhamki deke paise maangne wale cases police extortion ke roop mein darj karti hai. 2024 mein police ne 2,536 cyber crime cases mein motive extortion darj kiya, aur 3,190 mein sexual exploitation [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Karz se inmein se kuch nahi badalta: koi law kisi lender ko tumhari sexual images banane ya unhe bhejne ki dhamki dene ki ijaazat nahi deta.

## Dhamki mein paise dena: isse kya milta hai, kya nahi

Paise dene se deletion nahi milta. Morph tumhari kisi bhi photo se kabhi bhi dobara banaya ja sakta hai, isliye "humne delete kar diya" aisa promise hai jise koi check nahi kar sakta. Aur paise dene se dhamki dene wala yeh seekhta hai ki dhamki kaam karti hai.

Lambi road ke baare mein bhi honest raho. 2024 mein Indian courts ke saamne cyber blackmail ya dhamki ke 1,221 cases the; inmein se sirf do mein conviction hua, aur saal ke end tak 98% pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Conviction aayega bhi, toh der se aayega. Isliye neeche ke steps mein logon ko warn karna aur images hatwana sabse pehle hai: yeh saalon mein nahi, ghanton mein kaam karte hain.

Agar tumne sach mein udhaar liya tha, toh apna khud ka record rakho: kitna liya, kaun si app se, aur har repayment uske transaction ID ke saath. Isse police ko loan aur uske upar khade kiye gaye crime ka fark samajhne mein madad milti hai.

## Pehle contacts ko warn karo, phir 1930 pe report karo

Blackmail tabhi kaam karta hai jab tumhare contacts image tumse sunne se pehle dekh lein. Yeh order ulta kar do. Family, close friends aur zaroorat ho toh office ko ek chhota message bhejo: "Ek loan app ne meri contact list chura li hai aur mujhe darakar paise vasoolne ke liye meri fake, edited photos bhej raha hai. Agar tumhe kuch bhi mile, woh fake hai. Na kholna, na forward karna, na reply karna. Mujhe number ka screenshot bhej do, phir use delete kar do." Jin ek-do logon ke reaction se tumhe sabse zyada darr lagta hai, unhe sabse pehle call karo.

Phir report karo. Toll-free cyber crime helpline 1930 pe call karo, ya cybercrime.gov.in pe complaint file karo, jo Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) ka national portal hai [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. Dono crimes ek hi complaint mein daalo: paise ki demand, har phone number, payment ID aur app ke naam ke saath, aur morphed images. Acknowledgement number sambhaal ke rakho [[cybercrime-portal]]. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita ke Section 173 ke under tum kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakte ho, chahe crime kahin bhi hua ho, aur FIR ki copy tumhe free mein milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Saaf-safai se pehle evidence save karo: app ke page, loan terms aur maangi gayi permissions ke screenshots, aur har message aur har caller ka record. Phir app se apne contacts aur photos ka access hatao, aur use uninstall karo.

## 2 ghante mein images hatwana

Agar morph kahin public jagah post hua hai, jaise koi page, fake profile ya group, toh platform ka complaint form use karo aur rule ka naam likho. Rule 3(2)(b) ki complaint tum khud ya tumhari taraf se koi bhi kar sakta hai [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]], isliye jis dost ko post dikhe, woh bhi file kar sakta hai. Likho: "This is an artificially morphed sexual image of me, shared without consent. Rule 3(2)(b), IT Rules: remove within two hours." Har link jodo aur complaint bhejne ka time note karo [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Private mein bheji gayi images tak pahunchna mushkil hai, kyunki encrypted chats ke andar platform dekh hi nahi sakta. Wahan tumhara pehle bheja gaya message hi sabse bada bachav hai: contacts se kaho ki app mein sender ka account report karein aur use block kar dein.

Sharm ka kaam hai tumhe akela mehsoos karwana, par tumne kuch galat nahi kiya. Agar pressure bahut zyada ho jaaye, toh Tele-MANAS 14416 pe din-raat free counselling milti hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Image fake hai. Darr asli hai, aur blackmailer asal mein sirf wahi bech raha hai.

mrs-x-delhi-high-court-ncii-case.en:
The petitioner appears in the court record only as Mrs X, and this story keeps it that way. Her case was about non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII): intimate images shared online without consent. On 26 April 2023, Justice Subramonium Prasad of the Delhi High Court ruled on her petition and went beyond her own case, telling the government and search engines to build a system that stops such images resurfacing after they are taken down [[delhihc-mrs-x-2023]].

## The problem: an image that would not stay down

When the court ruled, India's main tool was a 24-hour clock. Rule 3(2)(b) of the IT Rules, 2021 required platforms to remove, within 24 hours of a complaint by the person or someone on their behalf, content showing them nude or in a sexual act, or impersonating them, including artificially morphed images [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]].

That rule works one copy at a time. Consider what it means in practice. A woman finds her image on one site and complains. The copy comes down. A week later it is on two other sites under new names, and a search for her name brings up both. Each copy needs a new complaint and a new wait, and each search result is a fresh exposure to colleagues, relatives and strangers.

The court's directions take aim at that loop.

## What the court ordered on 26 April 2023

The judgment's directions read like a design brief [[delhihc-mrs-x-2023]]:

- **A status tracker.** The cybercrime.gov.in portal must let a complainant follow an NCII complaint. The portal had run since a pilot launch on 30 August 2019, built with a specific focus on crimes against women and children [[pib-mha-i4c-launch-2020]]. With a tracker, a complainant does not have to guess what happened to the complaint.
- **A round-the-clock helpline.** The court asked for a fully functioning NCII helpline available at all times. Images do not wait for office hours.
- **Search-engine tokens.** Search engines must use a token or digital identifier so that content they have de-indexed does not resurface. In plain words: the search engine remembers what it removed and checks new copies against it.

## Why the court avoided 'revenge porn'

The judgment chose not to use the phrase "revenge porn", treating it as only a subset of NCII [[delhihc-mrs-x-2023]]. That is more than a style note.

Our reading of why it matters: "revenge" suggests the person in the image provoked it, through a breakup or a betrayal, and invites the blaming question: what did you do? "Porn" suggests content made for an audience by people who agreed to it. Neither word fits an image taken in private, stolen from a phone, sold by a stranger or morphed with software. The IT Rules already cover artificially morphed images [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]], and a morphed image needs no jilted ex at all.

The criminal law draws the same line. Under Section 77 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), sharing a private image of a woman without her consent is voyeurism even if she agreed to the image being taken [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Consent to a photo is not consent to its circulation. "NCII" puts the crime where it belongs: on the sharing.

## After the judgment: the 2025 SOP and the 2026 rule

The next big step came from another court. On 11 November 2025 the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY) issued a Standard Operating Procedure on NCII, framed on the Madras High Court's directions in a different case. It told all platforms to remove flagged content within 24 hours, large platforms to use hash-matching to stop re-uploads, and the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) to keep a secure NCII hash bank [[pib-meity-ncii-sop-2025]]. Hash-matching works on the same logic as the Delhi court's token: remember the image, block the copy.

Then the clock itself changed. Since 20 February 2026, under the IT Amendment Rules notified on 10 February, platforms must remove nude, sexual or morphed images of a person within two hours of that person's complaint, down from 24 [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

| Date | What changed |
|---|---|
| 26 April 2023 | Delhi High Court, Mrs X: complaint tracker, round-the-clock helpline, search-engine tokens |
| 11 November 2025 | MeitY's SOP: 24-hour removal, hash-matching, I4C hash bank |
| 20 February 2026 | IT Amendment Rules in force: removal within two hours of a complaint |

## What is still missing

Takedown has sped up. Counting and punishing have not.

- **Data.** NCRB's table of cyber crimes against women has no column for non-consensual intimate images. In 2024 it recorded 18,615 cyber crimes against women, including 2,511 cases of publishing obscene sexual material and 293 of defamation or morphing [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Police registered 436 cases that year under Section 66E of the IT Act, on capturing or publishing images of private parts without consent [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A leaked-image case can sit under any of these heads, so official data cannot say how many people this happens to.
- **Courts.** Of 19,731 cases under the IT Act's obscenity sections before courts in 2024, 601 ended in conviction and 94.7% were still pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The platform has two hours; the trial has no clock.
- **Gender.** Section 77 of the BNS is written for women. A man or trans person whose images are shared must rely on laws such as Section 66E of the IT Act, which protects any person [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

Her name is not in this story, and it never needed to be. The tools now open to everyone follow the logic of her case: report to the platform and start the two-hour clock, file on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]], and fingerprint the image with StopNCII [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]] or Take It Down [[ncmec-take-it-down]] so that copies on partner platforms can be blocked at upload.
mrs-x-delhi-high-court-ncii-case.hg:
Court record mein petitioner ka naam sirf "Mrs X" likha hai, aur yeh story bhi use isi naam se bulayegi. Uska case non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) ke baare mein tha, yaani aisi intimate images jo bina consent online share ki gayi. 26 April 2023 ko Delhi High Court ke Justice Subramonium Prasad ne uski petition par faisla sunaya aur baat sirf uske case tak nahi rakhi. Court ne government aur search engines se kaha ki aisa system banao jo hatne ke baad aisi images ko phir se ubharne se roke [[delhihc-mrs-x-2023]].

## Problem: ek image jo hat kar bhi nahi hatti thi

Jab court ne faisla diya, tab India ka main tool tha ek 24 ghante ki ghadi. IT Rules, 2021 ke Rule 3(2)(b) ke hisaab se platforms ko complaint milne ke 24 ghante ke andar aisa content hatana tha jisme insaan nude dikhe, kisi sexual act mein dikhe, ya koi uska roop dhar kar pesh ho, artificially morphed images samet. Complaint woh insaan khud kar sakta tha ya uski taraf se koi aur [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]].

Par yeh rule ek baar mein ek hi copy par kaam karta hai. Socho, real life mein yeh kaisa dikhta hai. Ek aurat ko apni image ek site par dikhti hai, woh complaint karti hai, copy hat jaati hai. Ek hafte baad wahi image do aur sites par naye naamon se aa jaati hai, aur uska naam search karo to dono dikh jaati hain. Har copy ke liye nayi complaint, naya intezaar, aur har search result use phir se colleagues, rishtedaaron aur anjaan logon ki nazron ke saamne le aata hai.

Court ke directions isi chakkar ko nishana banate hain.

## 26 April 2023 ko court ne kya order diya

Judgment ke directions ek design brief jaise padhte hain [[delhihc-mrs-x-2023]]:

- **Status tracker.** cybercrime.gov.in portal par complaint karne wala apni NCII complaint ka status dekh sake. Yeh portal 30 August 2019 ko pilot ke taur par shuru hua tha, aur shuru se iska khaas focus aurton aur bachchon ke khilaf crimes par tha [[pib-mha-i4c-launch-2020]]. Tracker ho to complaint karne wale ko andaaza nahi lagana padta ki complaint ka kya hua.
- **Round-the-clock helpline.** Court ne NCII ke liye ek fully functioning helpline maangi jo har waqt khuli rahe. Images office hours dekh kar nahi phailti.
- **Search engines ke liye tokens.** Search engines token ya digital identifier wala tareeka apnayein, taaki jo content de-index hua hai woh phir na ubhre. Aasaan shabdon mein: search engine yaad rakhe ki usne kya hataya tha, aur har nayi copy ko usse match kare.

## Court ne 'revenge porn' shabd kyun nahi apnaya

Judgment ne "revenge porn" phrase nahi apnaya aur ise NCII ka sirf ek chhota hissa maana [[delhihc-mrs-x-2023]]. Yeh sirf shabdon ka khel nahi hai.

Humari samajh mein yeh kyun zaroori hai: "revenge" se lagta hai ki photo wale insaan ne hi kuch kiya hoga, jaise breakup ya dhokha, aur phir blame karne wala sawaal uthta hai: "tumne kya kiya tha?" "Porn" se lagta hai ki yeh kisi audience ke liye bana content hai jisme sabki haan thi. Yeh dono shabd us image par fit nahi baithte jo private mein li gayi, phone se churayi gayi, kisi anjaan ne bechi, ya software se morph ki gayi. IT Rules pehle se artificially morphed images ko cover karte hain [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]], aur morphed image ke peeche kisi naraaz ex ka hona zaroori nahi.

Criminal law bhi yahi line kheenchta hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 77 ke under kisi aurat ki private image uski marzi ke bina share karna voyeurism hai, chahe image khinchwane ke liye usne haan kaha ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Photo ki haan, use phailane ki haan nahi hai. "NCII" crime ko sahi jagah rakhta hai: share karne par.

## Judgment ke baad: 2025 ka SOP aur 2026 ka rule

Agla bada kadam ek doosre court se aaya. 11 November 2025 ko Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY) ne NCII par ek Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) jaari kiya, jo Madras High Court ke ek alag case mein diye gaye directions par bana. Isne sabhi platforms ko flagged content 24 ghante mein hatane ko kaha, bade platforms ko hash-matching se re-uploads rokne ko kaha, aur Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) ko ek secure NCII hash bank rakhne ko kaha [[pib-meity-ncii-sop-2025]]. Hash-matching ka logic Delhi court ke token jaisa hi hai: image yaad rakho, copy roko.

Phir ghadi hi badal gayi. 10 February 2026 ko notify hue IT Amendment Rules ke under, 20 February 2026 se platforms ko kisi insaan ki nude, sexual ya morphed image us insaan ki complaint ke 2 ghante ke andar hatani hoti hai; pehle 24 ghante milte the [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

| Date | Kya badla |
|---|---|
| 26 April 2023 | Delhi High Court, Mrs X: complaint tracker, round-the-clock helpline, search engines ke liye tokens |
| 11 November 2025 | MeitY ka SOP: 24 ghante mein removal, hash-matching, I4C hash bank |
| 20 February 2026 | IT Amendment Rules lagu: complaint ke 2 ghante ke andar removal |

## Ab bhi kya missing hai

Takedown tez hua hai. Ginti aur saza nahi.

- **Data.** NCRB ki "cyber crimes against women" wali table mein non-consensual intimate images ka koi alag column nahi hai. 2024 mein isme aurton ke khilaf 18,615 cyber crimes darj hue, jinme 2,511 cases obscene sexual material publish karne ke the aur 293 defamation ya morphing ke [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi saal police ne IT Act ke Section 66E ke under 436 cases darj kiye; yeh section private parts ki image bina consent khinchne ya publish karne par lagta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Leaked image ka case in mein se kisi bhi khaane mein ho sakta hai, isliye sarkari data yeh nahi bata sakta ki aisa kitne logon ke saath hota hai.
- **Courts.** 2024 mein IT Act ke obscenity sections ke 19,731 cases courts mein the; inme se sirf 601 mein conviction hua aur saal ke end mein 94.7% abhi bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Platform ke paas 2 ghante hain; trial ki koi ghadi nahi.
- **Gender.** BNS ka Section 77 sirf aurton ke liye likha gaya hai. Agar kisi mard ya trans insaan ki images share hon, to use IT Act ke Section 66E jaise laws ka sahara lena padega, jo har insaan ko bachata hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Uska naam is story mein nahi hai, aur iski zaroorat bhi nahi thi. Jo tools ab sabke liye khule hain, woh uske case wali soch par hi chalte hain: platform par report karke 2 ghante ki ghadi shuru karo, 1930 par call karo ya cybercrime.gov.in par complaint karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]], aur image ka fingerprint StopNCII [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]] ya Take It Down [[ncmec-take-it-down]] par banao, taaki partner platforms par copies upload hote hi block ho sakein.

online-age-verification-india-gaps.en:
Ask who is responsible for keeping a 13-year-old away from adult content online in India, and the answer changes with the app she opens. On a streaming platform, there is a written duty to check. On an ordinary website, the same rules say nothing. And on Facebook and Instagram in 2026, ads for fake pornography apps were running, according to a warning from the government's own cyber crime agency. We read the rules, the data law and the blocking record to see who is required to check a child's age and who is not. This is general information, not legal advice.

## What the rules say about age

Since 2021, the Digital Media Ethics Code, which is part of the IT Rules, has put two duties on streaming platforms, which the text calls publishers of online curated content. For anything rated U/A 13+ or higher, a platform must ensure that access controls, including parental locks, are "made available". For content rated "A", it must "implement a reliable age verification mechanism" [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2026]].

The two duties are not equal. A parental lock only has to be offered: it protects a child if someone at home finds it and sets a PIN. Age verification for adult titles is the platform's own job. But we found no public record of how that check is enforced.

## Who the rules do not cover

The age-check clause applies to curated streaming services. The IT Rules text we reviewed contains no comparable age-check duty for other websites that host adult content [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2026]]. So the written duty exists where content is already rated and catalogued, and is missing on the open web, where it is neither.

Large social media platforms have duties of a different kind. Since 2021 the rules have required them to use automated tools to proactively identify content depicting rape or child sexual abuse, and the February 2026 amendment hardened "endeavour to deploy" into a duty to "deploy appropriate technical measures" [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. That rule is aimed at illegal material. It does not ask how old the person scrolling is.

Then there are ads. On 26 August 2026 the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) issued advisory TAU/ADV/018, warning that fake pornography apps advertised on Facebook and Instagram, under names such as "Night Play", "Reloop" and "Kyss", were being used to take over Android phones and commit financial fraud [[i4c-advisory-porn-apps-2026]]. The advisory is about fraud, not children, and it does not say who saw the ads. What it records is that porn-themed ads ran on two mainstream platforms, and that the apps were side-loaded, meaning installed from a link, outside the app store and its parental controls.

Consider a 13-year-old in Kanpur who uses her mother's phone after school. The streaming app has a parental lock that nobody switched on. The browser asks her nothing. The feed shows ads chosen for the account holder, who is an adult. At no point has any system been told that the person holding the phone is a child.

## Blocked, then back on a new domain

Where the state has acted on adult content, it has acted by blocking. The Information and Broadcasting Ministry told the Lok Sabha on 22 July 2026 that 50 streaming platforms had been disabled in two years for showing obscene content, citing Sections 67 and 67A of the IT Act among other laws. The count stood at 43 in December 2025 [[ls-uq680-2026]]. In February 2026 the ministry blocked five more platforms, and officials said platforms blocked in March 2024 had resurfaced on new domains [[moneycontrol-ott-block-2026]].

Two things follow. A block attaches to a web address, so a new address needs a new order, and the list only grows. And blocking is not age verification. It removes a service for everyone, adults included, and does nothing to tell an adult from a child on the services that remain. The platforms were blocked for obscenity. Whether any of them ran the age check the 2021 rules required is not something the public record tells us.

> A block removes one address for everyone. It does not tell a 13-year-old from a 30-year-old on any service that is still open.

## The DPDP promise for under-18s

The widest promise sits in a different law. The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 defines a child as anyone who has not completed 18 years. Section 9 requires a platform to obtain verifiable consent from a parent before processing a child's personal data, and bars tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising directed at children [[meity-dpdp-act-2023]].

Three cautions apply before any family relies on it.

- **It may not be in force yet.** The Act lets the government bring its provisions into force on different dates. We could not verify when Section 9 takes effect, or what age-verification method the DPDP Rules, 2025 prescribe. Until that is confirmed, it is a promise, not a protection.
- **It is a data law.** It governs what a platform may do with a child's data, not what a child can watch. A ban on ads targeted at children does not stop a child seeing an ad aimed at the adult whose phone she is holding.
- **It needs the platform to know who is a child.** The Act's word is "verifiable". A typed-in birth year is easy to fake. Stronger checks mean documents or a parent's account, and those carry a privacy cost for adults too. That trade-off is the hard part of every age-verification law.

## Controls that work at home

Until the rules catch up, the working age gate is whoever sets up the phone: a parent, or an older sibling who knows the settings better. None of these steps is a wall, and each takes minutes.

- **Give the child their own profile.** A supervised child account, through Family Link on Android or Screen Time on an iPhone, lets an adult approve app installs and filter the browser. On a shared phone, at least create a separate user profile and lock the payment apps.
- **Switch on the lock the rules made platforms build.** Any streaming platform carrying U/A 13+ content must offer a parental lock [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2026]]. Set the PIN and use a children's profile.
- **Close the side door.** On Android, keep "install unknown apps" switched off for every app, so that nothing installs from an ad or a forwarded link.
- **Filter search.** Turn on SafeSearch and restricted modes in the browser and video apps.
- **Talk, because filters leak.** A 15-year-old can borrow a friend's phone. Tell children that what they may come across is staged, and that they will not be punished for telling you what they saw. In September 2024 the Supreme Court itself recommended comprehensive sex education covering consent [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

One situation is not a parenting matter but a crime. Section 67B of the IT Act punishes enticing children into online sexual relationships [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. If an adult sends a child sexual material or asks for images, call the 24x7 Child Helpline 1098 [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]], or report it on 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

India has written an age check for the most regulated corner of the internet and promised a wider one in its data law. We could verify the enforcement of neither. For now, a child's age online is checked by the adults at home, or by nobody.
online-age-verification-india-gaps.hg:
Poocho ki India mein 13 saal ki bachchi ko online adult content se door rakhne ki zimmedaari kiski hai, toh jawab is baat se badal jaata hai ki woh kaun sa app kholti hai. Streaming platform pe check karne ki ek likhi hui duty hai. Aam website pe wahi rules chup hain. Aur 2026 mein Facebook aur Instagram pe nakli pornography apps ke ads chal rahe the, yeh sarkar ki apni cyber crime agency ki warning kehti hai. Humne rules, data law aur blocking ka record padha, yeh dekhne ke liye ki bachche ki umar check karna kiske liye zaroori hai aur kiske liye nahi. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Rules umar ke baare mein kya kehte hain

2021 se Digital Media Ethics Code, jo IT Rules ka hissa hai, streaming platforms pe do duties daalta hai. Text inhe publishers of online curated content kehta hai. U/A 13+ ya usse upar ki rating wale content ke liye platform ko yeh pakka karna hota hai ki access controls, parental locks samet, "made available" hon, yaani uplabdh karaye jaayein. "A" rating wale content ke liye use "implement a reliable age verification mechanism" karna hota hai, yaani umar check karne ka ek bharosemand tareeka lagana hota hai [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2026]].

Yeh dono duties barabar nahi hain. Parental lock ko bas offer karna hota hai: woh bachche ko tabhi bachata hai jab ghar mein koi use dhoondh kar PIN set kare. Adult titles ke liye age verification platform ka apna kaam hai. Par humein koi public record nahi mila ki yeh check lagu kaise karwaya jaata hai.

## Rules kise cover nahi karte

Age-check wala clause curated streaming services pe lagu hota hai. IT Rules ke jis text ko humne padha, usmein adult content host karne wali doosri websites ke liye aisi koi age-check duty nahi hai [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2026]]. Yaani likhi hui duty wahan hai jahan content pehle se rated aur catalogued hai, aur open web pe gayab hai, jahan content na rated hai na catalogued.

Bade social media platforms ki duties alag kism ki hain. 2021 se rules unse maangte hain ki woh automated tools se rape ya child sexual abuse dikhane wala content khud dhoondhein, aur February 2026 ke amendment ne "endeavour to deploy" ko sakht karke "deploy appropriate technical measures" ki duty bana diya [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Yeh rule illegal material ke liye hai. Yeh nahi poochta ki scroll karne wale ki umar kya hai.

Phir aate hain ads. 26 August 2026 ko Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) ne advisory TAU/ADV/018 jaari ki, jismein warning thi ki Facebook aur Instagram pe "Night Play", "Reloop" aur "Kyss" jaise naamon se advertise kiye ja rahe nakli pornography apps se Android phones pe kabza kiya ja raha hai aur financial fraud ho raha hai [[i4c-advisory-porn-apps-2026]]. Advisory fraud ke baare mein hai, bachchon ke baare mein nahi, aur yeh nahi batati ki ads kisne dekhe. Jo yeh record karti hai woh yeh hai ki porn-themed ads do mainstream platforms pe chale, aur apps side-loaded the, yaani ek link se install hue, app store aur uske parental controls ke bahar.

Kanpur ki ek 13 saal ki bachchi ko socho jo school ke baad apni mummy ka phone use karti hai. Streaming app mein parental lock hai, jise kisi ne on nahi kiya. Browser usse kuch nahi poochta. Feed woh ads dikhata hai jo account holder ke liye chune gaye hain, aur account holder ek adult hai. Kisi bhi point pe kisi system ko yeh bataya hi nahi gaya ki phone pakadne wala insaan ek bachcha hai.

## Block hue, phir naye domain pe wapas

Jahan sarkar ne adult content pe action liya hai, wahan block karke liya hai. Information and Broadcasting Ministry ne 22 July 2026 ko Lok Sabha ko bataya ki do saal mein 50 streaming platforms obscene content dikhane ke liye band kiye gaye, aur isne doosre kanoonon ke saath IT Act ke Sections 67 aur 67A ka hawala diya. December 2025 mein yeh ginti 43 thi [[ls-uq680-2026]]. February 2026 mein ministry ne paanch aur platforms block kiye, aur officials ne kaha ki March 2024 mein block hue platforms naye domains pe phir se aa gaye the [[moneycontrol-ott-block-2026]].

Isse do baatein nikalti hain. Block ek web address pe lagta hai, toh naye address ke liye naya order chahiye, aur list bas badhti jaati hai. Aur blocking age verification nahi hai. Woh ek service ko sabke liye hata deti hai, adults ke liye bhi, aur jo services bachi rehti hain un pe adult aur bachche mein farak karne ke liye kuch nahi karti. Platforms obscenity ke liye block hue. Unmein se kisi ne woh age check chalaya ya nahi jo 2021 ke rules maangte the, yeh public record humein nahi batata.

> Block ek address ko sabke liye hata deta hai. Jo service ab bhi khuli hai, us pe woh 13 saal ke bachche aur 30 saal ke adult mein farak nahi karta.

## Under-18 ke liye DPDP ka vaada

Sabse bada vaada ek alag kanoon mein hai. Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 ke hisaab se bachcha woh hai jisne 18 saal poore nahi kiye. Section 9 kehta hai ki platform kisi bachche ka personal data process karne se pehle uske parent ka verifiable consent le, aur bachchon ki tracking, behavioural monitoring aur un pe targeted advertising pe rok lagata hai [[meity-dpdp-act-2023]].

Koi bhi family is pe bharosa kare, usse pehle teen saavdhaaniyan.

- **Ho sakta hai yeh abhi lagu na ho.** Act sarkar ko apne provisions alag-alag dates pe lagu karne deta hai. Hum verify nahi kar paaye ki Section 9 kab se lagu hota hai, ya DPDP Rules, 2025 age verification ka kaun sa tareeka batate hain. Jab tak yeh confirm na ho, yeh ek vaada hai, protection nahi.
- **Yeh data ka kanoon hai.** Yeh tay karta hai ki platform bachche ke data ke saath kya kar sakta hai, yeh nahi ki bachcha kya dekh sakta hai. Bachchon pe targeted ads ki rok us ad ko nahi rokti jo us adult ke liye tha jiska phone bachchi ke haath mein hai.
- **Iske liye platform ko pata hona chahiye ki bachcha kaun hai.** Act ka shabd hai "verifiable". Type kiya hua birth year aasani se jhootha likha ja sakta hai. Zyada mazboot check ka matlab hai documents ya parent ka account, aur iski privacy wali keemat adults ko bhi chukani padti hai. Har age-verification kanoon ka mushkil hissa yahi trade-off hai.

## Controls jo ghar pe kaam karte hain

Jab tak rules peeche hain, asli age gate woh insaan hai jo phone set up karta hai: koi parent, ya bada bhai-behen jo settings zyada achhe se jaanta hai. Inmein se koi bhi step deewar nahi hai, aur har ek mein kuch hi minute lagte hain.

- **Bachche ko uski apni profile do.** Supervised child account, Android pe Family Link ya iPhone pe Screen Time ke zariye, kisi adult ko app installs approve karne aur browser filter karne deta hai. Shared phone pe kam se kam ek alag user profile banao aur payment apps lock kar do.
- **Woh lock on karo jo rules ne platforms se banwaya hai.** U/A 13+ content dikhane wale har streaming platform ko parental lock offer karna hi hota hai [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2026]]. PIN set karo aur bachchon wali profile use karo.
- **Side door band karo.** Android pe "install unknown apps" har app ke liye band rakho, taaki kisi ad ya forward hue link se kuch install na ho.
- **Search filter karo.** Browser aur video apps mein SafeSearch aur restricted modes on karo.
- **Baat karo, kyunki filters leak karte hain.** 15 saal ka bachcha kisi dost ka phone maang sakta hai. Bachchon ko batao ki jo unke saamne aa sakta hai woh staged hota hai, aur jo dekha use tumhe batane pe unhe saza nahi milegi. September 2024 mein khud Supreme Court ne comprehensive sex education ki sifaarish ki thi jismein consent shaamil ho [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

Ek situation parenting ka maamla nahi, crime hai. IT Act ka Section 67B bachchon ko online sexual relationships mein phuslane ki saza deta hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Agar koi adult kisi bachche ko sexual material bheje ya images maange, toh 24x7 Child Helpline 1098 pe call karo [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]], ya 1930 ya cybercrime.gov.in pe report karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

India ne internet ke sabse zyada regulated kone ke liye ek age check likha hai, aur apne data law mein usse bade check ka vaada kiya hai. Hum dono mein se kisi ka bhi enforcement verify nahi kar paaye. Filhaal online bachche ki umar ghar ke adults check karte hain, ya koi nahi.

online-grooming-19-seconds-games-dms.en:
Imagine a 12-year-old in Indore playing a multiplayer game on his mother's phone after homework. A high-ranked player starts praising his moves. Within minutes there is a gift of in-game currency, a "you're better than everyone in this lobby", and a question: "Which other app are you on? Let's squad up there." Nothing about it looks dangerous. It is not meant to.

This explainer is for the older sibling, parent, teacher or coach who needs to know how it works, and how to interrupt it. It is general information, not legal advice.

## The 19-second opening

Risk-intelligence data cited in the WeProtect Global Alliance's Global Threat Assessment 2023 found that offenders in social gaming environments can draw children into high-risk grooming conversations within 19 seconds of the first message, and within 45 minutes on average [[weprotect-gta-2023]]. The data come from one firm, and 19 seconds is the fastest case, not the typical one. The average is the real warning: 45 minutes is shorter than an evening's play.

Multiplayer games put children and adult strangers in one lobby, with chat and voice built in. But a lobby is semi-public, with other players watching. That is why a request to move to a private chat on another app, where no one else can see, is a warning sign in itself.

## Stage by stage: trust, isolation, the first request

UNICEF describes the pattern: online abusers, known to the child or strangers, often win the trust of the child or a caregiver before manipulating the child into sharing sexual images or videos; some abuse is livestreamed [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. Online, the stages can compress into one evening. In a game, it can look like this.

- **Trust.** Praise, in-game gifts, help to level up, a claim to be "just a year older". The child feels chosen.
- **Isolation.** "Add me on another app." "Don't tell your parents, they'll take your phone." Disappearing messages. The child's fear of losing the device can become the offender's leverage.
- **The first request.** A dare, a question about the child's body, a photo "just for me", the camera switched on. Each step creates another secret to protect.
- **Coercion.** Once there is an image, threats can follow. Financial sextortion mainly targets boys aged 13 to 17, who are typically deceived into believing they are talking to a young woman, and the move from first message to coercion can take minutes to hours [[weprotect-web-of-deceit-2024]].

It does not always stay online. In 2025 the US-based child-protection centre NCMEC received 1.4 million reports of online enticement of children, a 158% increase on 2024, including more than 800 in which an offender travelled to meet a child in person [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. Part of that rise reflects a new US law requiring platforms to report enticement.

## 'Self-generated' does not mean consenting

The Internet Watch Foundation recorded a 360% increase in "self-generated" sexual imagery of children aged 7 to 10 from the first half of 2020 to 2022 [[weprotect-gta-2023]]. "Self-generated" means the child held the camera. Such imagery is usually produced under grooming or coercion: the child is behind the lens, but someone else is directing.

The label tempts adults to blame the child: "Why did you send it?" The law does not ask that question. POCSO defines a child as anyone under 18 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], and a child's "consent" is no defence. The adult who asked for the image committed the offence; the child who was manipulated into sending it is the victim.

One rule for adults who find such an image: do not download, screenshot or forward it, even as proof. Collecting or exchanging sexual material depicting children is itself a crime under Section 67B of the IT Act [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Save usernames, links and the non-sexual messages instead.

## Section 67B(c): the law on online enticement

Section 67B is usually described as India's law against child sexual abuse material. Its clause (c) goes further: it punishes anyone who "cultivates, entices or induces children to online relationship" of a sexual kind. The section also covers creating, collecting, browsing, downloading or exchanging such material, and recording abuse. The penalty is up to five years in prison and a fine of up to Rs 10 lakh on first conviction, and up to seven years on a repeat [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

So grooming is not just the run-up to a crime: under clause (c), the enticing is itself an offence, before any image is sent or any meeting happens.

Enforcement is thin. Police recorded 1,753 cyber crimes against children in 2024, 1,099 of them involving sexually explicit material depicting children [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Of 2,885 Section 67B cases before the courts that year, trials were completed in only 156, and 57 ended in conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Signs to watch, and the conversation to have

UNICEF lists common signs that a child is distressed by something that happened online: headaches or stomach aches, trouble sleeping, changes in appetite, unexplained sadness, irritability or anxiety, distress after being online, avoiding devices or being unusually secretive about them, and fear of going to school [[unicef-parenting-negative-online-experience-2026]]. None of them proves abuse. Darkness to Light, a child-protection nonprofit, lists special attention to one child and gift giving among grooming red flags [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Watch, too, for an older online "friend" and new apps or accounts.

Have the conversation before anything happens, and make one promise you will keep: "If anyone online asks you to move to another app, keep a secret from me or send a photo, tell me. You will not lose your phone for telling me." The fear of losing the device can keep a child quiet.

If a child discloses, stay calm and say it is not their fault. Do not confront the offender. Report the account on the platform, file at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]], and call the Child Helpline 1098 [[wcd-childline]], which runs round the clock [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Teachers and coaches cannot promise total secrecy: under POCSO, anyone who knows or suspects that a child sexual offence has been or is likely to be committed must report it to the police [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]].
online-grooming-19-seconds-games-dms.hg:
Socho, Indore ka ek 12 saal ka ladka homework ke baad apni mummy ke phone par ek multiplayer game khel raha hai. Ek high-rank player uske moves ki tareef karne lagta hai. Kuch hi minute mein in-game currency ka gift aa jaata hai, phir "tum is lobby mein sabse achhe ho", aur phir ek sawaal: "Aur kaun si app par ho? Wahan squad banate hain." Ismein kuch bhi khatarnaak nahin lagta. Lagna bhi nahin chahiye, yahi toh plan hai.

Yeh explainer us bade bhai ya behen, parent, teacher ya coach ke liye hai jise samajhna hai ki yeh kaise hota hai, aur ise beech mein kaise roka jaaye. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahin.

## 19 second ki shuruaat

WeProtect Global Alliance ki Global Threat Assessment 2023 mein quote kiye gaye risk-intelligence data ke mutabik, social gaming environments mein offenders pehle message ke 19 seconds ke andar bachchon ko high-risk grooming conversations mein kheench sakte hain, aur average mein 45 minute mein [[weprotect-gta-2023]]. Yeh data ek hi firm ka hai, aur 19 seconds sabse tez case hai, aam case nahin. Asli warning average mein hai: 45 minute ek shaam ki gaming se bhi kam hain.

Multiplayer games mein bachche aur anjaan adults ek hi lobby mein hote hain, aur chat aur voice saath mein milte hain. Lekin lobby semi-public hoti hai, doosre players dekh rahe hote hain. Isiliye kisi doosri app par private chat mein aane ki request, jahan koi aur na dekh sake, apne aap mein ek warning sign hai.

## Stage by stage: bharosa, akelapan, pehli request

UNICEF yeh pattern batata hai: online abusers, chahe bachche ke jaan-pehchaan wale hon ya anjaan, aksar pehle bachche ka ya uske caregiver ka bharosa jeette hain, aur phir bachche ko sexual images ya videos share karne ke liye manipulate karte hain; kuch abuse livestream bhi hota hai [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. Online yeh saare stages ek hi shaam mein simat sakte hain. Game mein yeh kuch aisa dikh sakta hai.

- **Bharosa.** Tareef, in-game gifts, level up karne mein madad, "bas ek saal bada hoon" wala daawa. Bachcha khud ko special mehsoos karta hai.
- **Akelapan.** "Mujhe doosri app par add karo." "Parents ko mat batana, woh tumhara phone le lenge." Disappearing messages. Phone chhin jaane ka bachche ka darr hi offender ka hathiyaar ban sakta hai.
- **Pehli request.** Ek dare, bachche ke body ke baare mein koi sawaal, "sirf mere liye" ek photo, camera on karna. Har step ek naya secret banata hai jise chhupana padta hai.
- **Dabaav.** Ek baar image aa gayi, toh dhamkiyan shuru ho sakti hain. Financial sextortion zyadatar 13 se 17 saal ke ladkon ko target karta hai, jinhe aksar dhokhe se yeh yakeen dilaya jaata hai ki woh kisi young woman se baat kar rahe hain, aur pehle message se dabaav tak pahunchne mein kuch minute se kuch ghante lag sakte hain [[weprotect-web-of-deceit-2024]].

Yeh hamesha online tak nahin rehta. 2025 mein US ke child-protection centre NCMEC ko bachchon ke online enticement ki 1.4 million reports aayin, 2024 se 158% zyada, jinmein 800 se zyada aisi thin jinmein offender bachche se milne khud pahunch gaya [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. Is badhat ka kuch hissa ek naye US law ki wajah se bhi hai, jo platforms ke liye enticement report karna zaroori banata hai.

## 'Self-generated' ka matlab consent nahin

Internet Watch Foundation ne 2020 ke pehle half se 2022 tak 7 se 10 saal ke bachchon ki "self-generated" sexual imagery mein 360% ki badhat record ki [[weprotect-gta-2023]]. "Self-generated" ka matlab bas itna hai ki camera bachche ke haath mein tha. Aisi imagery zyadatar grooming ya dabaav mein banti hai: lens ke peeche bachcha hai, lekin direction koi aur de raha hai.

Yeh label adults ko bachche par hi ilzaam lagane ki taraf le jaata hai: "Tumne bheja hi kyun?" Law yeh sawaal poochhta hi nahin. POCSO 18 se kam umar ke har insaan ko child maanta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], aur bachche ki "consent" koi defence nahin hai. Jis adult ne image maangi, offence usne kiya; jis bachche se manipulate karke image bhijwayi gayi, woh victim hai.

Aisi image milne par adults ke liye ek rule: use download, screenshot ya forward mat karo, saboot ke liye bhi nahin. Bachchon ko dikhane wala sexual material collect ya exchange karna IT Act ke Section 67B ke under khud ek crime hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Uski jagah usernames, links aur non-sexual messages save karo.

## Section 67B(c): online enticement par law

Section 67B ko aam taur par child sexual abuse material ke khilaaf India ka law kaha jaata hai. Lekin iska clause (c) aage jaata hai: yeh har us insaan ko saza deta hai jo "cultivates, entices or induces children to online relationship", yaani bachchon ko sexual kism ke online relationship mein phansata, lubhata ya uksaata hai. Yeh section aise material ko banana, collect karna, browse, download ya exchange karna, aur abuse record karna bhi cover karta hai. Saza hai pehli conviction par paanch saal tak ki jail aur Rs 10 lakh tak ka fine, aur dobara karne par saat saal tak [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

Matlab grooming kisi crime ki sirf taiyaari nahin hai: clause (c) ke under phansana apne aap mein offence hai, koi image bheje jaane ya koi mulaqat hone se pehle hi.

Enforcement kamzor hai. Police ne 2024 mein bachchon ke khilaaf 1,753 cyber crimes darj kiye, jinmein se 1,099 bachchon ko dikhane wale sexually explicit material se jude the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Us saal court ke saamne Section 67B ke 2,885 cases mein se sirf 156 ke trial poore hue, aur 57 conviction par khatam hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Kin signs par nazar rakhein, aur kya baat karein

UNICEF un aam signs ki list deta hai jo batate hain ki bachcha online hui kisi baat se pareshaan hai: sir dard ya pet dard, neend mein dikkat, bhookh mein badlaav, bina wajah udaasi, chidchidapan ya anxiety, online rehne ke baad pareshaani, devices se bachna ya unke baare mein ajeeb tarah se secretive hona, aur school jaane se darr [[unicef-parenting-negative-online-experience-2026]]. Inmein se koi bhi sign abuse saabit nahin karta. Child-protection nonprofit Darkness to Light grooming ke red flags mein kisi ek bachche par khaas dhyan dena aur gifts dena ginta hai [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Saath hi dhyan do: koi umar mein bada online "dost", aur achanak nayi apps ya accounts.

Kuch hone se pehle hi yeh baat kar lo, aur ek vaada karo jise nibha sako: "Agar online koi bhi tumhe doosri app par aane ko kahe, mujhse kuch chhupane ko kahe ya photo bhejne ko kahe, toh mujhe batana. Batane ki wajah se tumhara phone nahin chhinega." Phone chhin jaane ka darr bachche ko chup rakh sakta hai.

Agar bachcha kuch bataye, toh shaant raho aur kaho ki ismein uski galti nahin hai. Offender se khud mat bhido. Account ko platform par report karo, cybercrime.gov.in par complaint karo ya 1930 par call karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]], aur Child Helpline 1098 par call karo [[wcd-childline]], jo din-raat chalti hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Teachers aur coaches poori secrecy ka vaada nahin kar sakte: POCSO ke under jo bhi jaanta hai ya shak karta hai ki kisi bachche ke khilaaf sexual offence hua hai ya hone wala hai, use police ko report karna hi hoga [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]].

online-sexual-abuse-counts-unicef-650-mi.en:
"At least nobody touched her." It is the line people reach for when a girl's photo goes round a college WhatsApp group or a boy is blackmailed over a recorded video call. The sentence files online abuse as embarrassment, not violence.

UNICEF's numbers file it differently. Its first global estimates of sexual violence against children, released on 10 October 2024, found that more than 370 million girls and women alive today, about 1 in 8, were raped or sexually assaulted before 18 [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. Count non-contact sexual violence, such as online or verbal sexual abuse, and the figure rises to about 650 million: 1 in 5 [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]].

## 370 million to 650 million: what changes when online abuse counts

The first number counts rape and sexual assault. The second adds what UNICEF calls non-contact forms, such as online or verbal sexual abuse [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. In a teenager's life that can mean sexual messages they never asked for, pressure to send pictures, or an intimate image used as a threat.

UNICEF says its non-contact estimates draw on broader data and some indirect methods [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]], so 650 million is rougher than 370 million. But leave out online and verbal abuse, and you leave out a large share of the children who were sexually violated.

Most childhood sexual violence happens in adolescence, with a significant spike between ages 14 and 17 [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. Those are the years when a teenager's social life runs through a phone.

## Boys and men in the same data

An estimated 240 million to 310 million boys and men alive today, around 1 in 11, were raped or sexually assaulted in childhood; with non-contact forms included, the estimate is 410-530 million [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. UNICEF gives ranges, not single figures, because data on boys are thinner and it had to use indirect methods.

In online sextortion, the evidence points mostly at boys and young men. When the Canadian Centre for Child Protection analysed more than 6,500 first-hand accounts by victims of sexual extortion, 98% were male where gender could be identified [[weprotect-gta-2023]]. Those were self-selected posts, not a survey, but WeProtect also finds that sextortion for money mainly targets boys aged 13 to 17 [[weprotect-web-of-deceit-2024]]. In India, POCSO protects every child below 18, whatever their gender [[pocso-act-2012]].

## The screen as a crime scene in Indian law

Indian law does not wait for touch. In 2021 the Supreme Court set aside the Bombay High Court's "skin-to-skin" ruling, holding that "the important ingredient for constituting the offence of sexual assault under POCSO is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child" [[barandbench-satish-2021]].

POCSO also treats sexual harassment of a child as an offence of its own, separate from sexual assault. Police recorded 3,502 such cases in 2024, each FIR counted once under its most serious charge [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Section 67B of the IT Act punishes creating, browsing, downloading or exchanging child sexual abuse material and enticing children into online sexual relationships, with up to five years on first conviction [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. In September 2024 the Supreme Court held that storing such material with the intent the law specifies is itself an offence under Section 15 of POCSO, even if it is never shared, and told courts to stop calling it "child pornography" [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

Adults are covered too. Under Section 77 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), sharing a woman's private image without her consent is voyeurism even if she agreed to the photo, with one to three years on first conviction [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. For anyone, IT Act Section 66E punishes capturing or sharing images of private parts without consent, and Section 67A punishes publishing sexually explicit material with up to five years on first conviction [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Since 2026, platforms that offer AI tools must use technical measures to block synthetic content that contains child sexual abuse material or intimate imagery made without consent [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

## Why 'only online' still harms

Online abuse often starts with trust: UNICEF warns that abusers, known to the child or strangers, first win over a child or caregiver, then manipulate the child into sharing sexual images; some abuse is livestreamed [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. The Internet Watch Foundation recorded a 360% increase in "self-generated" sexual imagery of children aged 7 to 10 between the first half of 2020 and 2022 [[weprotect-gta-2023]]. "Self-generated" means made by the child, usually under grooming or coercion. It does not mean consent.

Nor does it stay online. In 2025 NCMEC, the US centre that receives platforms' child-exploitation reports, logged 1.4 million reports of online enticement, more than 800 involving an offender who travelled to meet a child [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]].

And the distress is real. UNICEF's signs that a child is distressed by something online include trouble sleeping, unexplained sadness or anxiety, avoiding devices and fear of going to school [[unicef-parenting-negative-online-experience-2026]]. NCMEC says it has known since 2021 of at least 36 teenage boys in the United States who took their own lives after being sextorted [[ncmec-2024-in-numbers-2025]]. If threats or messages make you feel you cannot go on, call Tele-MANAS on 14416, free and round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

> Abuse does not need a room or a touch. A screen is enough.

## Answering someone who says 'it's just a photo'

This is general information, not legal advice.

- **"Nobody touched you."** The Supreme Court says sexual intent, not skin contact, makes sexual assault under POCSO. And Section 67B of the IT Act punishes enticing a child into an online sexual relationship, where there is no touch at all.
- **"It's just a photo."** Shared without consent, it is a crime: Section 77 of the BNS for women, Sections 66E and 67A of the IT Act for anyone. Agreeing to a photo is not agreeing to its spread.
- **"It's fake, so it doesn't count."** Since 20 February 2026, platforms must remove nude, sexual or morphed images of a person within two hours of their complaint [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].
- **A police officer who says "it's only online".** You can report at any police station, wherever the offence happened, or by e-FIR, signed within three days, and you must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Or call 1930, the cyber crime helpline, or file at cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

The 650 million is not a count of people embarrassed online. It counts girls and women who were sexually abused as children, and for many of them a screen was simply where it happened.
online-sexual-abuse-counts-unicef-650-mi.hg:
"Kam se kam kisi ne use chhua to nahi." Jab kisi ladki ki photo college ke WhatsApp group mein ghoomne lagti hai, ya kisi ladke ko record ki gayi video call ke naam par blackmail kiya jata hai, to log aksar yahi line bol dete hain. Yeh ek line online abuse ko sharm ka maamla bana deti hai, violence ka nahi.

UNICEF ke aankde ise alag khaane mein rakhte hain. Bachchon ke khilaaf sexual violence par uske pehle global estimates, jo 10 October 2024 ko jaari hue, batate hain ki aaj zinda 370 million se zyada ladkiyon aur auraton ka, yaani lagbhag har 8 mein se 1 ka, 18 saal se pehle rape ya sexual assault hua [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. Non-contact sexual violence bhi gino, jaise online ya verbal sexual abuse, to yeh aankda lagbhag 650 million ho jata hai: har 5 mein se 1 [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]].

## 370 million se 650 million: online abuse ginne se kya badalta hai

Pehla number rape aur sexual assault ginta hai. Doosra usme woh bhi jodta hai jise UNICEF non-contact forms kehta hai, jaise online ya verbal sexual abuse [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. Ek teenager ki zindagi mein iska matlab ho sakta hai bina maange aaye sexual messages, pictures bhejne ka pressure, ya kisi intimate image ke zariye di gayi dhamki.

UNICEF kehta hai ki non-contact estimates ke liye usne zyada tarah ka data aur kuch indirect methods use kiye [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]], isliye 650 million ka aankda 370 million jitna pakka nahi hai. Par online aur verbal abuse ko chhod do, to un bachchon ka ek bada hissa ginti se bahar ho jata hai jinke saath sexual violence hua.

Bachpan ka zyada tar sexual violence teenage mein hota hai, aur 14 se 17 saal ki umar mein isme saaf uchhaal dikhta hai [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. Yahi woh saal hain jab ek teenager ki social life phone par chalti hai.

## Usi data mein ladke aur mard

Andaza hai ki aaj zinda 240 million se 310 million ladkon aur mardon ka, yaani lagbhag har 11 mein se 1 ka, bachpan mein rape ya sexual assault hua; non-contact forms milakar yeh estimate 410-530 million hai [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. UNICEF ek pakka number nahi, range deta hai, kyunki ladkon par data kam hai aur use indirect methods use karne pade.

Online sextortion mein evidence zyada tar ladkon aur young men ki taraf ishaara karta hai. Canadian Centre for Child Protection ne sexual extortion ke victims ke 6,500 se zyada first-hand accounts analyse kiye, aur jahan gender pata chal saka, unme 98% male the [[weprotect-gta-2023]]. Yeh victims ki apni marzi se daali gayi posts thi, koi survey nahi, par WeProtect bhi kehta hai ki paison ke liye kiya jaane wala sextortion zyada tar 13 se 17 saal ke ladkon ko target karta hai [[weprotect-web-of-deceit-2024]]. India mein POCSO 18 se kam umar ke har bachche ko protect karta hai, uska gender chahe kuch bhi ho [[pocso-act-2012]].

## Indian law mein screen bhi crime scene hai

Indian law chhoone ka intezaar nahi karta. 2021 mein Supreme Court ne Bombay High Court ka "skin-to-skin" wala faisla radd kar diya aur kaha ki "the important ingredient for constituting the offence of sexual assault under POCSO is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child", yaani POCSO mein sexual assault ki asli shart sexual intent hai, skin se skin ka touch nahi [[barandbench-satish-2021]].

POCSO bachche ke sexual harassment ko bhi ek alag offence maanta hai, jo sexual assault se alag gina jata hai. Police ne 2024 mein aise 3,502 case darj kiye, aur har FIR sirf ek baar, uske sabse serious charge ke under gini gayi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

IT Act ka Section 67B child sexual abuse material banane, browse karne, download karne ya exchange karne par, aur bachchon ko online sexual relationship mein phansane par saza deta hai: pehli conviction par 5 saal tak [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. September 2024 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki aisa material law mein likhe irade ke saath store karna khud POCSO ke Section 15 ke under offence hai, chahe use kabhi share na kiya gaya ho, aur courts se kaha ki ise "child pornography" kehna band karein [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

Adults bhi covered hain. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 77 ke under kisi aurat ki private image uski consent ke bina share karna voyeurism hai, chahe usne photo khinchwane ke liye haan kaha ho; pehli conviction par 1 se 3 saal ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Kisi ke bhi case mein, IT Act ka Section 66E bina consent private parts ki images lene ya share karne par saza deta hai, aur Section 67A sexually explicit material publish karne par pehli conviction par 5 saal tak ki [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. 2026 se AI tools dene wale platforms ko technical measures lagakar aisa synthetic content block karna hoga jisme child sexual abuse material ho ya bina consent bani intimate imagery ho [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

## 'Sirf online' bhi chot kyun pahunchata hai

Online abuse aksar bharose se shuru hota hai: UNICEF warn karta hai ki abuser, chahe bachche ka jaan-pehchaan wala ho ya ajnabi, pehle bachche ya uske guardian ka bharosa jeetta hai, phir bachche ko sexual images share karne ke liye manipulate karta hai; kuch abuse livestream bhi hota hai [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. Internet Watch Foundation ne 2020 ke pehle chhah mahinon se 2022 tak 7 se 10 saal ke bachchon ki "self-generated" sexual imagery mein 360% ki badhotri record ki [[weprotect-gta-2023]]. "Self-generated" ka matlab hai ki bachche ne khud banayi, aksar grooming ya dabaav mein. Iska matlab consent nahi hai.

Aur yeh online tak ruka bhi nahi rehta. 2025 mein NCMEC, yaani US ka woh centre jahan platforms child exploitation ki reports bhejte hain, ko online enticement ki 1.4 million reports mili, jinme se 800 se zyada mein abuser bachche se milne ke liye safar karke pahuncha [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]].

Aur yeh takleef asli hoti hai. UNICEF ke mutabik agar online kuch hone se bachcha pareshaan hai, to uske signs mein neend na aana, bina wajah udaasi ya anxiety, phone se door bhaagna aur school jaane se darna shaamil hain [[unicef-parenting-negative-online-experience-2026]]. NCMEC kehta hai ki 2021 se woh United States ke kam se kam 36 teenage ladkon ke baare mein jaanta hai jinhone sextortion ka shikaar hone ke baad apni jaan le li [[ncmec-2024-in-numbers-2025]]. Agar dhamkiyon ya messages ki wajah se tumhe lagta hai ki tum aur nahi seh sakte, to Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call karo; yeh free hai aur din-raat chalta hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

> Abuse ke liye na kamra chahiye, na chhoona. Ek screen kaafi hai.

## Jo kahe 'yeh to bas ek photo hai', use kya jawab do

Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

- **"Kisi ne chhua to nahi."** Supreme Court kehta hai ki POCSO mein sexual assault sexual intent se banta hai, skin contact se nahi. Aur IT Act ka Section 67B bachche ko online sexual relationship mein phansane par saza deta hai, jahan chhoona hota hi nahi.
- **"Yeh to bas ek photo hai."** Bina consent share hui, to yeh crime hai: auraton ke liye BNS ka Section 77, aur kisi ke bhi liye IT Act ke Sections 66E aur 67A. Photo ke liye haan kehna, uske failne ke liye haan kehna nahi hai.
- **"Yeh fake hai, to count nahi hota."** 20 February 2026 se platforms ko kisi insaan ki nude, sexual ya morphed images uski complaint ke 2 ghante ke andar hatani hongi [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].
- **Koi police officer jo kahe "yeh to sirf online hai".** Tum kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakte ho, offence chahe kahin bhi hua ho, ya e-FIR ke zariye, jise 3 din ke andar sign karna hota hai, aur tumhe FIR ki copy free milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Ya cyber crime helpline 1930 par call karo, ya cybercrime.gov.in par complaint karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

650 million un logon ki ginti nahi hai jo online sharminda hue. Yeh un ladkiyon aur auraton ki ginti hai jinka bachpan mein sexual abuse hua, aur unme se bahuton ke liye screen bas woh jagah thi jahan yeh hua.

online-sexual-crime-conviction-gap.en:
In 2024, India's courts had 1,221 cases of cyber blackmail or threatening before them. Two ended in a conviction. At the end of the year, 98% were still waiting [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That one line from the National Crime Records Bureau's *Crime in India 2024* sums up what happens to online sexual crime once it reaches a courtroom: it waits. Here are five lines from NCRB's court tables, what the two numbers on each line actually measure, and the cases that drop out before any judge sees them.

## Five lines from NCRB's court tables

NCRB has no crime head called sextortion. The nearest line is cyber blackmail or threatening, which also holds other kinds of threats, and some sextortion cases are filed under IT Act sections or as extortion instead. With that caveat, this is how the lines for online sexual crime looked in court in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Crime head | Cases before courts | Convictions | Pending at year end |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cyber blackmail or threatening | 1,221 | 2 | 98% |
| Cyber stalking or bullying of women and children | 4,348 | 33 | 95.3% |
| Obscene or sexually explicit material (IT Act Section 67 group) | 19,731 | 601 | 94.7% |
| Child sexual abuse material (Section 67B, part of the 67 group) | 2,885 | 57 | 94.5% |
| All cyber crime | 99,693 | 2,596 | 90.9% |

"Cases before courts" means everything the courts had in hand that year: cases left over from earlier years plus new chargesheets. Now compare what flowed in. In 2024 police registered 601 new cyber-blackmail cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]] and 1,01,928 new cyber crime cases of every kind [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. On every line, cases arrive far faster than verdicts leave.

## Conviction rate and pendency: two different questions

NCRB reports two figures for each line, and they answer different questions. The conviction rate asks: of the trials that finished this year, how many ended in a conviction? Pendency asks: of all the cases before the courts, how many are still waiting?

The first can look healthy while the second is grim. Courts completed 4,567 cyber crime trials in 2024 and convicted in 2,596 of them, more than half [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Measured against the 99,693 cases before the courts, that is fewer than 3 convictions in every 100 cases.

Child sexual abuse material shows the same trap. Its conviction rate of 36.5% sounds like more than one case in three. But trials were completed in only 156 of the 2,885 cases, so the 57 convictions came from a thin slice of the pile [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Cyber stalking and bullying of women and children had a conviction rate of 22.8%. In plain numbers, that was 33 convictions against 4,348 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

> A conviction rate tells you how the few finished trials ended. Pendency tells you how many people are still waiting for one.

When a headline quotes a conviction rate, ask what it was divided by.

## 31.9%: the chargesheet gap before court

The court tables only show the cases that survived the police stage. In 2024, police filed a chargesheet in just 31.9% of the cyber crime cases they disposed of [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In more than two of every three, the case left the police stage without one, so nobody was sent for trial in it. For crimes against women as a whole, the chargesheeting rate was 77.2% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Child sexual abuse material fared better at this stage, with a chargesheeting rate of 69.3%. But 48.1% of the 2,356 such cases police had to investigate were still open at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

NCRB's tables do not say why the cyber crime figure is so low. Online cases can be hard to finish: an accused may hide behind a fake profile or sit in another state. That may account for part of the gap. It does not excuse a file that nobody works on.

## What delay does to victims and offenders

On paper, the punishments are heavy. Publishing sexually explicit material online carries up to five years in jail and a fine of up to Rs 10 lakh on a first conviction; capturing or sharing images of someone's private parts without consent carries up to three years [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. But a law deters through the likelihood of punishment, not only its size. A blackmailer reading the 2024 tables sees two convictions in a year, across the whole country.

For the person who complained, a pending case is not a pause. Consider a 20-year-old in Indore whose former partner posts their private photos in a college group chat. If police file a chargesheet under the IT Act's obscenity sections, the 2024 tables say more than nine in ten such cases were still waiting for a verdict at the year's end. That can mean hearing after hearing, long after the day the photos spread.

Delay also gives the image time. Unless someone acts, it can stay online and travel further while the case waits.

None of this is a reason to stay silent. An FIR creates an official record, and no conviction can happen without one. Slow courts are a reason to use every faster tool alongside it.

## Faster routes than a verdict

This is general information, not legal advice.

- **Report to the platform first.** Since 20 February 2026, platforms must remove nude, sexual or morphed images of a person within two hours of that person's complaint, down from 24 hours [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].
- **Stop re-uploads.** StopNCII.org, for images taken as an adult, and Take It Down, for images taken under 18, share only a digital fingerprint of the image with partner platforms [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]] [[ncmec-take-it-down]].
- **Report the crime.** Call 1930 or file at cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. Any police station must record a complaint about a cognizable offence, wherever it happened. An e-FIR must be signed within three days, and you are entitled to a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Keep the evidence.** Save screenshots, links, numbers and payment details before you block anyone.

A verdict may take years. Getting an image taken down should take two hours. Use both.
online-sexual-crime-conviction-gap.hg:
2024 mein India ki courts ke saamne cyber blackmail ya dhamki ke 1,221 cases the. Saza sirf do mein hui. Saal ke end tak 98% cases abhi bhi intezaar mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. National Crime Records Bureau ki *Crime in India 2024* report ki yeh ek line batati hai ki online sexual crime jab courtroom tak pahunchta hai, toh uske saath kya hota hai: woh intezaar karta hai. Yahan NCRB ke court tables ki paanch lines hain, har line ke do numbers asal mein kya naapte hain, aur woh cases jo judge tak pahunchne se pehle hi gayab ho jaate hain.

## NCRB ke court tables ki paanch lines

NCRB mein sextortion naam ka koi crime head hi nahi hai. Sabse kareeb wali line cyber blackmail ya dhamki ki hai, jismein doosri tarah ki dhamkiyan bhi aati hain, aur kuch sextortion cases IT Act ke sections ya extortion ke tahat file hote hain. Is baat ko dhyan mein rakhte hue, 2024 mein court mein online sexual crime ki lines aisi dikhti thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Crime head | Courts ke saamne cases | Convictions | Saal ke end tak pending |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cyber blackmail ya dhamki | 1,221 | 2 | 98% |
| Auraton aur bachchon ki cyber stalking ya bullying | 4,348 | 33 | 95.3% |
| Obscene ya sexually explicit material (IT Act Section 67 group) | 19,731 | 601 | 94.7% |
| Child sexual abuse material (Section 67B, 67 group ka hissa) | 2,885 | 57 | 94.5% |
| Saara cyber crime | 99,693 | 2,596 | 90.9% |

"Courts ke saamne cases" ka matlab hai woh sab kuch jo us saal court ke haath mein tha: pichhle saalon ke bache hue cases, plus nayi chargesheets. Ab dekho andar kitna aaya. 2024 mein police ne cyber blackmail ke 601 naye cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]], aur har tarah ke 1,01,928 naye cyber crime cases [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Har line pe cases jitni tezi se aate hain, faisle usse kahin dheere nikalte hain.

## Conviction rate aur pendency: do alag sawaal

NCRB har line ke liye do figures deta hai, aur dono alag sawaalon ka jawab dete hain. Conviction rate poochhta hai: is saal jo trials khatam hue, unmein se kitne mein saza hui? Pendency poochhti hai: courts ke saamne jitne cases the, unmein se kitne abhi bhi intezaar mein hain?

Pehla number achha dikh sakta hai jab doosra bahut bura ho. 2024 mein courts ne 4,567 cyber crime trials poore kiye aur unmein se 2,596 mein saza di, yaani aadhe se zyada [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lekin courts ke saamne pade 99,693 cases ke hisaab se dekho, toh yeh har 100 cases mein 3 se bhi kam convictions hain.

Child sexual abuse material mein bhi yahi jaal hai. Iska conviction rate 36.5% hai, jo sunne mein teen mein se ek se zyada case lagta hai. Lekin 2,885 cases mein se sirf 156 mein trial poora hua, toh 57 convictions dher ke ek bahut patle hisse se aaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Auraton aur bachchon ki cyber stalking aur bullying ka conviction rate 22.8% tha. Seedhe numbers mein, yeh 4,348 cases ke saamne 33 convictions the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

> Conviction rate batata hai ki jo gine-chune trials khatam hue, unka kya hua. Pendency batati hai ki kitne log abhi bhi apne trial ka intezaar kar rahe hain.

Jab koi headline conviction rate bataye, toh poochho ki use kis number se divide kiya gaya.

## 31.9%: court se pehle ka chargesheet gap

Court tables mein sirf woh cases dikhte hain jo police stage paar kar paaye. 2024 mein police ne jin cyber crime cases ko niptaya, unmein se sirf 31.9% mein chargesheet file hui [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har teen mein se do se zyada cases bina chargesheet ke police stage se nikal gaye, yaani unmein kisi ko trial ke liye bheja hi nahi gaya. Auraton ke khilaaf crimes mein kul mila ke chargesheet rate 77.2% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Child sexual abuse material ke cases is stage pe behtar rahe, unka chargesheet rate 69.3% tha. Lekin police ke paas jaanch ke liye aise 2,356 cases the, aur unmein se 48.1% saal ke end tak khule pade the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

NCRB ke tables yeh nahi batate ki cyber crime ka yeh figure itna kam kyun hai. Online cases ko poora karna mushkil ho sakta hai: accused fake profile ke peeche chhupa ho sakta hai ya kisi doosre state mein baitha ho sakta hai. Gap ka kuch hissa shayad isi se aata ho. Lekin us file ka koi bahaana nahi banta jis pe koi kaam hi nahi karta.

## Deri victims aur offenders ke saath kya karti hai

Kagaz pe sazaayein bhaari hain. Online sexually explicit material publish karne pe pehli baar mein paanch saal tak ki jail aur 10 lakh rupaye tak ka fine hai. Kisi ke private parts ki images bina consent ke kheenchne ya share karne pe teen saal tak ki jail hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Lekin kanoon ka darr saza ke pakke hone se aata hai, sirf uske bade hone se nahi. 2024 ke tables padhne wala blackmailer dekhta hai: poore desh mein, ek saal mein, do convictions.

Complaint karne wale ke liye pending case koi aaram ka waqt nahi hai. Socho Indore mein koi 20 saal ka insaan hai, jiske ex-partner ne uski private photos college ke group chat mein daal di. Agar police IT Act ke obscenity sections mein chargesheet file kare bhi, toh 2024 ke tables kehte hain ki aise das mein se nau se zyada cases saal ke end tak faisle ka intezaar kar rahe the. Matlab ek ke baad ek hearing ho sakti hai, photos failne ke din ke bahut baad tak.

Deri image ko bhi waqt de deti hai. Jab tak koi kadam na uthaye, case ke intezaar mein woh online rehti hai aur aur door tak failti hai.

Iska matlab chup rehna nahi hai. FIR ek official record banati hai, aur uske bina koi saza ho hi nahi sakti. Dheemi courts ka matlab hai ki FIR ke saath-saath har tez tareeka bhi use karo.

## Faisle se tez raaste

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

- **Sabse pehle platform pe report karo.** 20 February 2026 se platforms ko kisi insaan ki nude, sexual ya morphed images uski complaint ke do ghante ke andar hatani hoti hain. Pehle yeh time 24 ghante tha [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].
- **Dobara upload hone se roko.** StopNCII.org, jo adult umar mein li gayi images ke liye hai, aur Take It Down, jo 18 se kam umar mein li gayi images ke liye hai, partner platforms ke saath image ka sirf ek digital fingerprint share karte hain [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]] [[ncmec-take-it-down]].
- **Crime report karo.** 1930 pe call karo ya cybercrime.gov.in pe complaint file karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. Cognizable offence ki complaint koi bhi police station record karega, chahe crime kahin bhi hua ho. E-FIR pe teen din ke andar sign karna hota hai, aur FIR ki copy free mein lena tumhara haq hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Saboot sambhaal ke rakho.** Kisi ko block karne se pehle screenshots, links, numbers aur payment details save kar lo.

Faisle mein saalon lag sakte hain. Image hatwane mein do ghante lagne chahiye. Dono raaste use karo.

phone-privacy-settings-safety-audit.en:
Imagine a 19-year-old in Indore, half asleep, answering a video call from a new follower. Nothing was hacked. The phone did what its default settings allow: a stranger could call, just as an advertisement can hand you an app to install and a private photo can copy itself to the family tablet. Many attacks that end in blackmail or an emptied bank account start this way. This audit closes those doors in one sitting of about half an hour.

## The attacks you are actually likely to face

In a 2023 Snap survey of more than 6,000 teens and young adults in six countries including India, 65% said they or their friends had been targeted in sextortion schemes through catfishing or hacking [[weprotect-snap-sextortion-research-2023]].
