Take It Down, run by the US National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC), is for nude, partially nude or sexually explicit images or videos taken when the person was under 18. It is free and anonymous, sends only the fingerprint, and is available in Hindi [[ncmec-take-it-down]]. What counts is your age in the image, not today: a 25-year-old trying to stop a photo taken at 16 should use Take It Down.

In 2025 the site had more than 1.6 million visitors, and only the United States sent more of them than India; by the end of that year it worked in 36 languages [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. Visits show need, not removals.

Helping a teenager as a parent, teacher or older sibling? Sit with them while they use it on their own device. Do not keep, screenshot or forward the image "as proof". Section 67B of the IT Act punishes not only publishing child sexual abuse material but also collecting, downloading or exchanging it, with up to five years in jail on first conviction [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Write down the links and account names instead. And hashing does not replace reporting: under the POCSO Act, anyone who knows of a sexual offence against a child must inform the police [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]].

## India's own hash bank and the de-indexing order

On 26 April 2023, in Mrs X v. Union of India, the Delhi High Court told search engines to adopt a token or digital-identifier approach so that intimate images they had de-indexed would not resurface [[delhihc-mrs-x-2023]]. De-indexing takes a page out of search results; the token is meant to stop a fresh copy slipping back in.

On 11 November 2025, the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY) issued a Standard Operating Procedure on non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII), framed on the Madras High Court's directions. Large platforms must use hash-matching to stop re-uploads, and the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) collects NCII complaints and keeps a secure NCII hash bank [[pib-meity-ncii-sop-2025]].

The difference for you: StopNCII and Take It Down let you act on your own and in private, today. India's route runs through I4C, which runs cybercrime.gov.in; the cyber crime helpline is 1930 [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. Use both.

## What hashing cannot do

Hashing is a lock, not a cure.

- **It works only where platforms have signed up.** StopNCII's fingerprints reach partner platforms, and only they act [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]]. Take It Down works only on public or unencrypted platforms that participate [[ncmec-take-it-down]]. A site that has not joined never sees the list.
- **It cannot see inside encrypted private chats,** where many forwards travel.
- **It needs the file.** You can only fingerprint an image already on your device. If it shows you under 18 and you do not have it, never download it to make a fingerprint; report the links instead.
- **Edited copies can slip through.** A cropped, filtered or re-filmed version may not match, so keep reporting new versions.
- **It punishes no one.** Under Section 77 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), sharing a private image of a woman without her consent is voyeurism even if she agreed to the photo being taken: one to three years in prison on first conviction [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 66E of the IT Act protects a person of any gender whose private area is photographed or published without consent: up to three years, a fine of up to Rs 2 lakh, or both [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

If the image went up within the last hour, start with our first-hour guide: save the links, report every post, make the fingerprint, then call 1930. The crime belongs to whoever shared the image, never to the person in it.
stopncii-take-it-down-hashing-guide.hg:
Socho, Pune mein ek 22 saal ki ladki hai. Breakup ke baad uski ek photo, jo usne kabhi apne boyfriend ko bheji thi, ek fake account par daal di jaati hai. Woh report karti hai, photo hat jaati hai. Chaar din baad ek dost use naya link bhejta hai: same photo, naya account. Har re-upload ke saath darr bhi wapas aata hai aur bhaag-daud bhi.

Hash-matching tools se partner platforms kisi intimate photo ya video ki copies block kar sakte hain, aur tumhe woh image kisi ko bhejni nahi padti. Do tools free hain: adults ke liye StopNCII.org, aur 18 se kam umar mein li gayi images ke liye Take It Down. 20 February 2026 se India mein platforms ko kisi insaan ki nude, sexual ya morphed image us insaan ki complaint ke 2 ghante ke andar hatani hoti hai [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Hashing hi wahi photo turant wapas aane se rok sakti hai.

## Hash kya hai, aur tumhari photo phone se bahar kyun nahi jaati

Hash ko photo ka digital fingerprint samjho: photo se bana ek chhota sa code. Ek hi photo se har baar wahi code banta hai, isliye jis platform ke paas yeh code hai, woh upload hote hi copy pehchaan leta hai. Lekin code photo nahi hai. Jaise angoothe ke nishaan se insaan pehchana jaata hai, par us nishaan mein kisi ko uska chehra nahi dikhta. Code jiske paas hai, woh tumhe nahi dekh sakta.

Dono tools yeh fingerprint tumhare apne device par hi banate hain, aur aage sirf code jaata hai. Take It Down kehta hai ki tum anonymous reh sakte ho aur tumhe apni photos ya videos kisi ko bhejni nahi padengi [[ncmec-take-it-down]]; StopNCII content upload kiye bina hash banata hai, aur partner platforms naye uploads ko usse match karte hain [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]].

## StopNCII: adults ke liye, step by step

StopNCII.org ko UK ki charity SWGfL chalati hai, un images ke liye jo tab li gayi jab photo wala insaan 18 ya usse bada tha. November 2025 tak yeh 20 lakh (2 million) images protect kar raha tha, 2024 se 97% zyada, aur chaar saal pehle launch hone ke baad se 7.85 lakh (785,000) se zyada cases mein madad kar chuka tha [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]]. Dhyaan rahe: yeh un images ki ginti hai jinhe logon ne protect karne ke liye daala, hatayi gayi images ki nahi.

1. Aisa phone ya computer lo jo sirf tumhara ho.
2. StopNCII.org par case shuru karo aur confirm karo ki photo mein tum hi ho, aur photo ke waqt tumhari age 18 ya usse zyada thi.
3. Photos ya videos select karo. Files tumhare device mein hi rahengi.
4. Case number aur PIN save karo; case ka status dekhne ya case wapas lene ke liye yahi chahiye.
5. Har platform par nayi copies report karte raho. StopNCII tumhare liye poora internet search nahi karta: yeh fingerprints apne partner platforms ko deta hai, aur action bhi sirf wahi lete hain [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]].

Mard aur trans log bhi ise use kar sakte hain.

## Take It Down: 18 se kam umar mein li gayi images ke liye

Take It Down ko US ka National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) chalata hai. Yeh un nude, semi-nude ya sexually explicit photos aur videos ke liye hai jo tab bane jab insaan 18 se chhota tha. Yeh free aur anonymous hai, sirf fingerprint bhejta hai, aur Hindi mein bhi available hai [[ncmec-take-it-down]]. Yahan aaj ki age nahi, photo wali age matter karti hai: agar tum aaj 25 ke ho aur photo 16 saal ki umar ki hai, to Take It Down use karo.

2025 mein site par 16 lakh (1.6 million) se zyada visitors aaye, aur US ke baad sabse zyada India se; saal ke end tak yeh 36 languages mein chal raha tha [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. Visits zaroorat dikhate hain; kitni photos hati, yeh nahi.

Parent, teacher ya bade bhai-behen ke taur par kisi teenager ki madad kar rahe ho? Uske paas baitho aur tool uske apne phone par chalwao. "Proof" ke naam par woh photo na rakho, na screenshot lo, na forward karo. IT Act ka Section 67B child sexual abuse material publish karne par hi nahi, use collect, download ya exchange karne par bhi saza deta hai: pehli baar mein 5 saal tak ki jail [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Photo ki jagah links aur account names likh lo. Aur hashing report karne ki jagah nahi le sakti: POCSO Act ke under jise bhi kisi bachche ke khilaf sexual offence ka pata ho, use police ko batana hi hota hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]].

## India ka apna hash bank, aur de-indexing ka order

26 April 2023 ko Mrs X v. Union of India case mein Delhi High Court ne search engines se kaha ki woh token ya digital identifier wala tareeka apnayein, taaki jo intimate images search se hatayi gayi hain woh wapas na aayein [[delhihc-mrs-x-2023]]. De-indexing ka matlab hai page ka search results se gayab ho jaana; token ka kaam hai ki nayi copy chupke se wapas na aa paaye.

11 November 2025 ko Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY) ne non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) par ek Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) jaari kiya, jo Madras High Court ke directions par bana. Iske hisaab se bade platforms ko hash-matching se re-uploads rokne honge, aur Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) NCII complaints ek jagah jama karega aur ek secure NCII hash bank rakhega [[pib-meity-ncii-sop-2025]].

Tumhare liye farak kya hai? StopNCII aur Take It Down se tum aaj hi, khud aur privately kadam utha sakte ho. India wala raasta I4C se hokar jaata hai, jo cybercrime.gov.in chalata hai; cyber crime helpline 1930 hai [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. Dono use karo.

## Hashing kya nahi kar sakti

Hashing ek taala hai, ilaaj nahi.

- **Yeh sirf jude hue platforms par kaam karti hai.** StopNCII ke fingerprints sirf partner platforms tak jaate hain, aur action bhi wahi lete hain [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]]. Take It Down sirf un public ya unencrypted platforms par chalta hai jo isse jude hain [[ncmec-take-it-down]]. Jo site nahi judi, us tak yeh list pahunchti hi nahi.
- **Yeh encrypted private chats ke andar nahi dekh sakti,** jahan bahut saare forwards ghoomte hain.
- **Iske liye file chahiye.** Fingerprint sirf usi photo ka banega jo pehle se tumhare device par hai. Agar photo mein tum 18 se chhote ho aur woh tumhare paas nahi hai, to fingerprint banane ke liye use kabhi download mat karo; bas links report karo.
- **Edited copies bach sakti hain.** Crop ki hui, filter lagi ya dobara record ki gayi copy shayad match na kare, isliye har nayi copy report karte raho.
- **Yeh kisi ko saza nahi dilati.** Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 77 ke under kisi aurat ki private image uski marzi ke bina share karna voyeurism hai, chahe photo khinchwane ke liye usne haan kaha ho: pehli baar mein 1 se 3 saal ki jail [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. IT Act ka Section 66E har gender ke logon ko bachata hai: kisi ke private parts ki photo bina consent khinchne ya publish karne par 3 saal tak ki jail, 2 lakh rupaye tak ka fine, ya dono [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Agar photo pichhle ek ghante mein hi daali gayi hai, to pehle humari first-hour guide padho: links save karo, har post report karo, fingerprint banao, phir 1930 par call karo. Crime uska hai jisne photo phailayi, photo mein dikhne wale ka kabhi nahi.

teen-sexting-pocso-it-act-67b.en:
Imagine a 16-year-old in Bhopal who sends a photo to someone they trust. A week later it is in three class groups. Is the student in trouble? Are the people forwarding it? Should the friend they confided in keep quiet? Indian law answers each question clearly. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Is a nude of a 16-year-old really 'abuse material'?

Yes. The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, in force since 14 November 2012, defines a child as anyone under 18, boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Section 67B of the IT Act, on sexually explicit material depicting children, draws the same line [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. The law does not ask whether the picture was a selfie, who it was meant for, or whether the person in it said yes. It asks how old they were.

On 23 September 2024 the Supreme Court told courts to stop saying "child pornography", and urged Parliament to replace the term in POCSO with "child sexual exploitation and abuse material" (CSEAM) [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]]. A 16-year-old's nude falls in that category.

Images children take of themselves are called "self-generated", in quotation marks, because the label can hide the grooming or pressure behind them. The Internet Watch Foundation recorded a 360% rise in such imagery of children aged 7 to 10 between the first half of 2020 and 2022 [[weprotect-gta-2023]]. Nobody believes a seven-year-old chose that. At 16 the pressure looks different, a partner who keeps asking or an online "friend" who sends a photo first, but the law's answer is the same.

## I forwarded it, I did not take it: does that matter?

Less than you think. Section 67B punishes not only making such material but collecting, browsing, downloading or exchanging it: up to 5 years in jail and a fine of up to Rs 10 lakh on a first conviction, up to seven years on a repeat [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. In 2024 the Supreme Court held that even viewing, storing or possessing it can be an offence under Section 15 of POCSO and Section 67B [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]].

The age that matters is that of the person in the picture, not yours. In a first-year college group, some are 18 and some 17. An 18-year-old who forwards a 17-year-old classmate's photo is an adult distributing child sexual abuse material. "It was already in every group" is no defence: each forward puts it on another phone.

So don't forward, save or screenshot it "as proof". Report the message in the app, note the group, sender and time, and tell an adult you trust. Then delete the image: as the Supreme Court read Section 15, the offence covers storing such material without deleting, destroying or reporting it [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]].

## Can I get in trouble for a photo of myself?

The uncomfortable answer: on paper, yes. Section 67B covers creating sexually explicit images of anyone under 18, and its text makes no exception for the person in the picture [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

But a child is not processed like an adult. Anyone under 18 accused of an offence goes before a Juvenile Justice Board, and only a 16- or 17-year-old accused of the gravest category of offence, one with a minimum sentence of seven years or more, can be sent for trial as an adult [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]. Section 67B sets a maximum sentence, not a minimum.

And if someone asked, pushed or tricked you into sending it, the law names what they did: Section 67B separately punishes enticing a child into an online sexual relationship [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. If they now threaten to share the photo unless you send more or pay, that is sextortion, and the crime is theirs. They are counting on your fear. The 24x7 Child Helpline, 1098, is run by child-protection staff [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]; its job is to protect you.

## Someone told me: do I have to report?

If you are an adult, whether parent, teacher or coach, yes. Sections 19 and 21 of POCSO make reporting child sexual abuse mandatory for anyone who knows of it. Failing to report can bring up to six months in jail or a fine; the head of a school or institution who fails to report abuse by staff faces up to a year and a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. So a teacher cannot promise total secrecy, only to explain each step first and to stay with the student.

If you are a teenager, the Section 19 duty technically covers you too, but a child cannot be punished for not reporting [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Your job is simpler: believe your friend, don't ask to see the image, and help them tell an adult they trust or call 1098.

Reporting does not put a child on display. POCSO bars any media report from revealing a child victim's name, photograph, school or neighbourhood without the Special Court's permission [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], and the Supreme Court has ordered that FIRs in POCSO cases must not be made public [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

## How do I get it taken down?

Start with Take It Down, run by the US-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC). It is free, anonymous and available in Hindi, for nude or sexual images taken when you were under 18, even if you are older now [[ncmec-take-it-down]]. You never send the photo: only its digital fingerprint, a hash, goes to participating platforms. It works only on public or unencrypted platforms that have signed up, not inside encrypted chats. In 2025 India sent more visitors to the site than any country except the United States [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. You are not alone.

Report every copy on the platform too. Since 20 February 2026, platforms in India must remove nude or sexual images of a person within two hours of that person's complaint [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. For a police complaint, call 1930 or file at cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]], with an adult you trust if you are under 18. Screenshot any threats and the sender's username, but never attach the image; say where it is. If it feels too heavy, Tele-MANAS on 14416 is free, round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].
teen-sexting-pocso-it-act-67b.hg:
Socho, Bhopal mein ek 16 saal ke student ne kisi bharose wale insaan ko ek photo bheji. Ek hafte baad woh photo teen class groups mein ghoom rahi hai. Kya student legal trouble mein hai? Aur forward karne wale? Jis friend ko student ne sab bataya, kya use chup rehna chahiye? Indian law in sab sawaalon ka saaf jawab deta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Kya 16 saal ke kisi insaan ki nude photo sach mein 'abuse material' hai?

Haan. Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, jo 14 November 2012 se lagu hai, 18 se kam umar ke har insaan ko child maanta hai, ladke aur ladkiyan dono [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. IT Act ka Section 67B, jo bachchon ko dikhane wale sexually explicit material pe hai, wahi line kheenchta hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Law yeh nahi poochta ki photo selfie thi, kiske liye thi, ya photo wale insaan ne haan kaha tha. Woh bas yeh poochta hai ki uski umar kitni thi.

23 September 2024 ko Supreme Court ne courts se kaha ki "child pornography" kehna band karein, aur Parliament se apeel ki ki POCSO mein yeh term badalkar "child sexual exploitation and abuse material" (CSEAM) kiya jaaye [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]]. 16 saal ke kisi insaan ki nude photo isi category mein aati hai.

Bachche apni jo images khud lete hain, unhe "self-generated" kaha jaata hai, quotation marks ke saath, kyunki yeh label unke peeche ki grooming ya pressure ko chhupa sakta hai. Internet Watch Foundation ne 2020 ki pehli chhamahi se 2022 ke beech 7 se 10 saal ke bachchon ki aisi imagery mein 360% badhat record ki [[weprotect-gta-2023]]. Koi nahi maanta ki saat saal ke bachche ne yeh khud chuna. 16 ki umar mein pressure alag dikhta hai, ek partner jo baar-baar maangta rehta hai, ya online koi "friend" jo pehle khud photo bhejta hai, par law ka jawab wahi rehta hai.

## Maine sirf forward kiya, photo li nahi: kya isse fark padta hai?

Jitna tum sochte ho, utna nahi. Section 67B sirf aisa material banane pe nahi, use collect, browse, download ya exchange karne pe bhi saza deta hai: first conviction pe 5 saal tak ki jail aur Rs 10 lakh tak ka fine, dobara conviction pe saat saal tak [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. 2024 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki aisa material dekhna, store karna ya apne paas rakhna bhi POCSO ke Section 15 aur Section 67B ke under offence ho sakta hai [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]].

Umar photo wale insaan ki maayne rakhti hai, tumhari nahi. First-year college group mein koi 18 ka hota hai, koi 17 ka. Jo 18 saal ka student 17 saal ke classmate ki photo forward karta hai, woh ek adult hai jo child sexual abuse material faila raha hai. "Woh toh pehle se har group mein thi" koi defence nahi hai: har forward use ek aur phone tak pahuncha deta hai.

Isliye na forward karo, na save karo, na "proof ke liye" screenshot lo. App mein message report karo, group ka naam, bhejne wala aur time note karo, aur kisi trusted adult ko batao. Phir image delete karo: Supreme Court ne Section 15 ko jis tarah padha, uske hisaab se aisa material bina delete, destroy ya report kiye store karna offence ke daayre mein aata hai [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]].

## Kya apni hi photo ke liye mujh pe case ho sakta hai?

Uncomfortable jawab: kagaz pe, haan. Section 67B 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi insaan ki sexually explicit images banane ko cover karta hai, aur uske text mein photo wale insaan ke liye koi exception nahi hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

Par bachche ke saath adult jaisa process nahi hota. 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi accused ka case Juvenile Justice Board ke saamne jaata hai, aur sirf woh 16 ya 17 saal ka accused, jis pe sabse gambhir category ke offence ka aarop ho, yaani jiski minimum saza saat saal ya usse zyada hai, adult ki tarah trial ke liye bheja ja sakta hai [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]. Section 67B maximum saza tay karta hai, minimum nahi.

Aur agar kisi ne tumse photo maangi, pressure daala ya chaalaki se mangwayi, toh law uske kaam ko naam deta hai: Section 67B alag se kisi bachche ko online sexual relationship mein phansane ki saza deta hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Agar ab dhamki mil rahi hai ki aur photos ya paise nahi diye toh photo share kar di jaayegi, toh yeh sextortion hai, aur crime unka hai. Unka poora khel tumhare darr pe tika hai. 24x7 Child Helpline 1098 ko child-protection staff chalata hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]; uska kaam tumhe protect karna hai.

## Kisi ne mujhe bataya: kya mujhe report karna hoga?

Agar tum adult ho, chahe parent, teacher ya coach, toh haan. POCSO ke Sections 19 aur 21 kehte hain ki jise bhi child sexual abuse ka pata ho, uske liye report karna zaroori hai. Report na karne pe chhe mahine tak ki jail ya fine ho sakta hai; school ya institution ka head agar staff ke kiye abuse ki report nahi karta, toh use ek saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Isliye teacher poori secrecy ka promise nahi kar sakte, sirf yeh ki har step pehle samjhayenge aur student ke saath rahenge.

Agar tum teenager ho, toh Section 19 ki duty technically tum pe bhi lagti hai, par report na karne pe kisi bachche ko saza nahi di ja sakti [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Tumhara kaam simple hai: friend ki baat pe yakeen karo, image dekhne ko mat maango, aur kisi trusted adult ko batane ya 1098 pe call karne mein uski help karo.

Report karne ka matlab bachche ka tamasha banana nahi hai. POCSO kisi bhi media report ko Special Court ki permission ke bina child victim ka naam, photo, school ya mohalla bataane se rokta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], aur Supreme Court ka order hai ki POCSO cases ki FIRs public nahi ki ja saktin [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

## Photo hatwayein kaise?

Shuruaat Take It Down se karo, jise US ka National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) chalata hai. Yeh free hai, anonymous hai aur Hindi mein bhi hai, un nude ya sexual images ke liye jo tumhari 18 se kam umar mein li gayi thin, chahe tum ab badi umar ke ho [[ncmec-take-it-down]]. Photo tum kabhi bhejte hi nahi: sirf uska digital fingerprint, yaani hash, participating platforms tak jaata hai. Yeh sirf un public ya unencrypted platforms pe kaam karta hai jo isse jude hain, encrypted chats ke andar nahi. 2025 mein United States ke baad sabse zyada visitors India se is site pe aaye [[ncmec-cybertipline-data-2025]]. Tum akele nahi ho.

Platform pe bhi har copy report karo. 20 February 2026 se India mein platforms ko kisi insaan ki nude ya sexual images us insaan ki complaint ke do ghante ke andar hatani padti hain [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Police complaint ke liye 1930 pe call karo ya cybercrime.gov.in pe complaint file karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]; 18 se kam ho toh kisi trusted adult ke saath. Dhamkiyon aur bhejne wale ke username ka screenshot lo, par image kabhi attach mat karo; bas batao ki woh kahan hai. Agar sab bahut bhaari lage, toh Tele-MANAS 14416 free hai, din-raat chalta hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

two-hour-takedown-rule-explained.en:
From 2021, India's rule on leaked intimate images ran on a 24-hour clock. Then, in a notification dated 10 February 2026, the government struck out the words "twenty-four hours" and wrote "two hours". Since 20 February 2026, platforms must remove nude, sexual or morphed images of a person within two hours of that person's complaint [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. An intimate image does its damage while it circulates. Here is what the rule covers, what it forces platforms to do, and where it still falls short. This is general information, not legal advice.

## What Rule 3(2)(b) covers, in plain words

Rule 3(2)(b) of the IT Rules, 2021 applies to content that, on the face of it, exposes a person's private area, shows them in full or partial nudity or in a sexual act, or impersonates them, including artificially morphed images [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]]. That last clause matters in the age of AI. A fake nude built from a photo of your face counts, even if your body was never photographed.

Three features make the rule unusual. The complaint can come from the person in the content or from anyone on their behalf, so a friend, parent or lawyer can file it. No FIR, court order or police letter is needed. And the platform must "take all reasonable and practicable measures to remove or disable access to such content", with the clock running from the moment it receives the complaint [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]].

## 24 hours to two: what changed on 20 February 2026

The IT Amendment Rules, 2026 tightened three clocks at once [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]:

| Duty | Before | Since 20 February 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| Remove intimate images after a person's complaint | 24 hours | 2 hours |
| Act on a court order or authorised government notice | 36 hours | 3 hours |
| Resolve other user grievances | 15 days | 7 days |

Of the three, the two-hour clock is the fastest, and you can start it yourself, without a court or an officer. So wording matters. A complaint that does not say what the content is may be handled as an ordinary grievance, on the seven-day track. Say four things: that you are the person shown (or are filing for them), the exact links, what the content shows, and "Rule 3(2)(b) of the IT Rules, two hours". Our guide to the first hour after a leak has a ready-to-paste version.

The same amendment requires platforms that offer AI tools to block users from creating synthetic child sexual abuse material or intimate images made without consent, and to label other synthetic content prominently [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

## Hash-matching and the I4C hash bank

A takedown removes the copy you found. The next copy is a separate problem. On 11 November 2025, the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY) issued a Standard Operating Procedure on non-consensual intimate imagery, framed on the Madras High Court's directions. It told all platforms to remove flagged content within 24 hours, told large platforms to use hash-matching and crawlers to stop re-uploads, and made the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) the central collector of such complaints and keeper of a secure hash bank [[pib-meity-ncii-sop-2025]]. Its 24-hour window has since been overtaken by the two-hour rule.

The February 2026 amendment then hardened a separate duty. Since 2021, large platforms had only to "endeavour to deploy" automated tools that find rape and child sexual abuse content and copies of content already taken down; now they must "deploy appropriate technical measures" [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. In plain words, a large platform that removed your image once is expected to catch it when it comes back. Smaller platforms have no such duty under Rule 4(4); there, removal still starts with a complaint or an order. Our guide to StopNCII and Take It Down explains how to hash an image yourself.

## When a platform ignores the clock: grievance officers and escalation

Start with the platform's own grievance channel, which the rules oblige it to run: since February 2026 it must resolve ordinary grievances within seven days [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Yours is not ordinary. Send your record: the links, the time you complained, and the fact that two hours have passed. Keep every reply; it is evidence for the next step.

Then use the state's channel. Call 1930 or file at cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]; under the SOP, I4C is the hub for exactly these complaints [[pib-meity-ncii-sop-2025]]. Know one limit: your local police station cannot trigger the three-hour clock on its own, because the 2026 amendment requires police notices to platforms to come from an officer not below the rank of Deputy Inspector General [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Courts have stepped in where the system lagged. In Mrs X v. Union of India (26 April 2023), the Delhi High Court directed that cybercrime.gov.in carry a status tracker for intimate-image complaints, that a round-the-clock helpline for such complaints be set up, and that search engines use digital identifiers so de-indexed images do not resurface [[delhihc-mrs-x-2023]].

## What the rule still cannot do

It waits for a complaint. Outside large platforms' proactive duties, nothing moves until someone finds the content and reports it. Private encrypted chats are the hardest place to enforce it, because the platform cannot see what is forwarded there. Hash tools reach only platforms that take part: StopNCII's fingerprints go only to its partner platforms [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]], and Take It Down works only on public or unencrypted ones [[ncmec-take-it-down]].

And it punishes no one. Removal is not justice, and the criminal track is far slower. Of 19,731 cases under the IT Act's obscenity sections before Indian courts in 2024, 601 ended in conviction and 94.7% were still pending at year end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In all of India that year, police registered just 293 cases of cyber defamation or morphing against women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB counts police cases, not complaints, and online sexual abuse is heavily under-reported.

The two-hour rule is the fastest tool India has given people whose images are abused. Use it first, word it precisely, keep the time-stamps, and treat the slower road to a conviction as a separate choice.
two-hour-takedown-rule-explained.hg:
2021 se, leak hui intimate images pe India ka rule 24-ghante ki ghadi pe chalta tha. Phir 10 February 2026 ke ek notification mein government ne "twenty-four hours" kaat ke "two hours" likh diya. 20 February 2026 se platforms ko kisi ki nude, sexual ya morphed images us insaan ki complaint ke 2 ghante ke andar hatani hoti hain [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Intimate image jitni der ghoomti hai, utna nuksaan karti hai. Yahan samjho ki rule kya cover karta hai, platforms se kya karwata hai, aur kahan kamzor pad jaata hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Rule 3(2)(b) kya cover karta hai, simple words mein

IT Rules, 2021 ka Rule 3(2)(b) aise content pe laagu hota hai jo pehli nazar mein kisi ka private area expose kare, kisi ko poora ya aadha nude ya sexual act mein dikhaye, ya kisi ka impersonation kare, artificially morphed images samet [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]]. AI ke zamane mein yeh aakhri clause bahut important hai. Tumhare chehre ki photo se bana fake nude bhi isme aata hai, chahe tumhari body ki kabhi photo li hi na gayi ho.

Teen cheezein is rule ko alag banati hain. Complaint content mein dikh raha insaan khud kar sakta hai ya uski taraf se koi bhi, yaani dost, parent ya lawyer bhi file kar sakte hain. Na FIR chahiye, na court order, na police ki chitthi. Aur platform ko content hatane ya uska access band karne ke liye "all reasonable and practicable measures" lene hote hain, aur ghadi complaint milte hi chalu ho jaati hai [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]].

## 24 ghante se 2: 20 February 2026 ko kya badla

IT Amendment Rules, 2026 ne ek saath teen ghadiyan tez kar di [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]:

| Kaam | Pehle | 20 February 2026 se |
|---|---|---|
| Kisi insaan ki complaint pe uski intimate images hatana | 24 ghante | 2 ghante |
| Court order ya authorised government notice pe action | 36 ghante | 3 ghante |
| Baaki user grievances resolve karna | 15 din | 7 din |

Teeno mein 2-ghante wali ghadi sabse tez hai, aur ise tum khud shuru kar sakte ho, bina court ya officer ke. Isliye wording matter karti hai. Jis complaint mein yeh na likha ho ki content mein kya hai, use ordinary grievance maan ke 7-din wale track pe daala ja sakta hai. Chaar cheezein likho: ki image mein tum ho (ya tum us insaan ki taraf se file kar rahe ho), exact links, content mein kya dikh raha hai, aur "Rule 3(2)(b) of the IT Rules, two hours". Leak ke baad ke pehle ghante pe hamari guide mein ready-to-paste version hai.

Isi amendment ke hisaab se jo platforms AI tools dete hain, unhe users ko synthetic child sexual abuse material ya bina consent wali synthetic intimate images banane se rokna hoga, aur baaki synthetic content pe prominently label lagana hoga [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

## Hash-matching aur I4C ka hash bank

Takedown se wahi copy hatti hai jo tumhe mili. Agli copy alag problem hai. 11 November 2025 ko Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY) ne non-consensual intimate imagery pe ek Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) jaari kiya, jo Madras High Court ke directions pe bana tha. Usne saare platforms ko flagged content 24 ghante mein hatane ko kaha, bade platforms ko re-uploads rokne ke liye hash-matching aur crawlers use karne ko kaha, aur Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) ko aisi complaints ka central collector aur ek secure hash bank ka keeper banaya [[pib-meity-ncii-sop-2025]]. Uski 24-ghante wali window ab 2-ghante wale rule se peeche chhoot chuki hai.

February 2026 ke amendment ne ek alag duty ko bhi sakht kiya. 2021 se bade platforms ko bas aise automated tools lagane ki "endeavour", yaani koshish, karni thi jo rape aur child sexual abuse content aur pehle hataye gaye content ki copies pakdein; ab unhe "deploy appropriate technical measures" karna hi hoga [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Simple words mein, agar kisi bade platform ne tumhari image ek baar hata di, toh usse ummeed hai ki image wapas aane pe woh use khud pakde. Chhote platforms pe Rule 4(4) ki aisi koi duty nahi hai; wahan removal abhi bhi complaint ya order se hi shuru hota hai. StopNCII aur Take It Down pe hamari guide batati hai ki tum khud hash kaise bana sakte ho.

## Jab platform ghadi ko ignore kare: grievance officers aur escalation

Shuruaat platform ke apne grievance channel se karo, jo rules ke hisaab se use chalana hi hai: February 2026 se ordinary grievances use 7 din mein resolve karni hoti hain [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Tumhari complaint ordinary nahi hai. Apna record bhejo: links, complaint ka time, aur yeh ki 2 ghante beet chuke hain. Har reply sambhaal ke rakho; agle step ke liye yahi evidence hai.

Phir government ka channel use karo. 1930 pe call karo ya cybercrime.gov.in pe file karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]; SOP ke under I4C hi in complaints ka hub hai [[pib-meity-ncii-sop-2025]]. Ek limit bhi jaan lo: tumhara local police station apne dum pe 3-ghante wali ghadi shuru nahi kar sakta, kyunki 2026 amendment ke hisaab se platforms ko police notice kam se kam Deputy Inspector General (DIG) rank ke officer se aana chahiye [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Jahan system peeche raha, wahan courts aage aaye hain. Mrs X v. Union of India (26 April 2023) mein Delhi High Court ne direct kiya ki cybercrime.gov.in pe intimate-image complaints ka status tracker ho, aisi complaints ke liye 24 ghante chalne wali helpline bane, aur search engines digital identifiers use karein taaki de-index ki gayi images wapas na aayein [[delhihc-mrs-x-2023]].

## Rule abhi bhi kya nahi kar sakta

Yeh complaint ka wait karta hai. Bade platforms ki proactive duty ko chhod do, toh jab tak koi content dhoondh ke report na kare, kuch nahi hota. Private encrypted chats mein ise laagu karna sabse mushkil hai, kyunki wahan kya forward ho raha hai, platform dekh hi nahi sakta. Hash tools bhi sirf jude hue platforms tak pahunchte hain: StopNCII ke fingerprints sirf uske partner platforms ko jaate hain [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]], aur Take It Down sirf un public ya unencrypted platforms pe kaam karta hai jo isse jude hain [[ncmec-take-it-down]].

Aur yeh kisi ko saza nahi deta. Image hat jaana insaaf nahi hai, aur criminal track bahut slow hai. 2024 mein IT Act ke obscenity sections ke 19,731 cases Indian courts ke saamne the; inme se 601 mein conviction hua aur saal ke end tak 94.7% pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi saal poore India mein police ne women ke khilaf cyber defamation ya morphing ke sirf 293 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB police cases ginta hai, complaints nahi, aur online sexual abuse bahut kam report hota hai.

2-ghante wala rule un logon ke liye India ka sabse tez tool hai jinki images ka misuse hua hai. Ise sabse pehle use karo, sahi words mein complaint karo, har time note karke rakho, aur conviction tak ki lambi road ko ek alag decision samjho.

unsolicited-nudes-cyberflashing-law-indi.en:
Imagine a 21-year-old in Indore who sells handmade earrings through Instagram. Close to midnight a message request arrives from an account with no posts: an explicit photograph of a stranger's body, and a question asking whether she likes it. The next morning a friend laughs and says it happens to everyone: just block him.

That it happens to so many people is the problem, not the excuse. The word for it is cyberflashing: sending sexual images to someone who did not ask for them. Indian law has no offence by that name, and does not need one. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Is sending an unsolicited nude actually a crime?

Yes. Section 67 of the Information Technology Act punishes transmitting obscene material in electronic form with up to three years in prison and a fine of up to Rs 5 lakh on first conviction. Section 67A covers sexually explicit material and goes up to five years and Rs 10 lakh [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Which one fits depends on what the image or clip shows.

Two features matter. The sections are gender-neutral: a man sent an explicit image, by a man or a woman, is covered exactly as a woman is. And they are obscenity law: they ask what the material is, not whether you wanted it. Your complaint will sit under "obscene material", a heading that says nothing about what was done to you.

When a man sends such an image to a woman, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) may also be relevant: Section 75 punishes sexual harassment of a woman by a man with up to three years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Whether it fits is for police and the court to decide.

If the receiver is under 18, the law sees a child: POCSO defines a child as anyone under 18 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Tell an adult you trust, or call the Child Helpline on 1098.

## What should I do the moment it arrives?

1. **Do not reply.** Not with anger, not with a joke. A reaction is often what the sender is after.
2. **Capture who and when.** Screenshot the sender's profile, username or phone number, and the message with its date and time. An account can be renamed or deleted in minutes.
3. **Report inside the app, then block.** A report made from inside the chat carries the message with it. Block or delete first, and there may be nothing left to attach.
4. **Report outside the app.** Call the cyber crime helpline 1930, or file on cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

Keep the evidence; do not circulate it. Forwarding the image to a group, or posting it to shame the sender, can itself count as transmitting the same material, which is what Section 67 punishes [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

## It came from a colleague or my boss: what changes?

You get one more door, and a deadline.

"Showing pornography" has been part of the definition of sexual harassment at work since the Supreme Court's Vishaka guidelines of 1997 [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, the POSH Act, turned those guidelines into statute [[pib-law-posh-act-gazette-2013]]. Employers must set up an Internal Complaints Committee; workplaces with fewer than ten workers, and complaints against the employer himself, go to the district's Local Committee. The complaint must be in writing, within three months of the incident, and the inquiry must finish within 90 days [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. The government's SHe-Box portal takes these complaints online [[shebox]].

Do not rule it out because the image came to your personal phone at night. The Act's idea of a workplace already goes beyond the office building, to places visited in the course of work and employer-provided transport [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. A sender who decides your appraisal does not become a stranger after office hours. File the complaint and let the committee rule; the police route stays open alongside.

The limit: the POSH Act protects women [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. A man sent explicit images by a colleague has the IT Act and his employer's conduct rules, not this committee.

## Will reporting it go anywhere?

Each door gives something different.

**The platform is the fastest.** A reported account can be restricted or removed, and under the IT Amendment Rules, 2026, platforms must resolve a user's grievance within seven days, down from 15. The two-hour takedown rule covers intimate images of the person complaining, not of the sender [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

**The police station is where a case starts.** A complaint on the portal is a record, not an FIR. Any station must record a cognizable offence wherever it happened, and a woman's complaint of sexual harassment must be recorded by a woman officer. Because Section 67 carries three years, police may, with a Deputy Superintendent's permission, hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days before registering it [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

**The courts are slow.** Police registered 2,914 cases under Section 67 and 2,197 under Section 67A in all of India in 2024. Unsolicited nudes are an uncounted slice of those totals, because no section is called cyberflashing. Of 19,731 cases under the IT Act's obscenity sections before the courts in 2024, 601 ended in conviction and 94.7% were still pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

A criminal case is possible, and strongest when the sender is identifiable: a classmate, a neighbour, a colleague.

## Why it matters to call it what it is

The slang for these images is built to sound like a joke. It files the act under bad manners and hands the work to the receiver: laugh, block, be a good sport. Change the setting and nobody laughs at a man who exposes himself to a stranger at a bus stop.

> The phone removes the bus stop. It does not remove the act.

Courts have changed the words before. In 2023 the Supreme Court's handbook on gender stereotypes told judges to replace "eve teasing" with "street sexual harassment" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. The old phrase made an offence sound like a pastime.

An unsolicited explicit image is sexual harassment carried out with a camera and a send button. Said that way, "block and move on" becomes one choice among several. Blocking is a legitimate choice. So is a complaint.

And if you have ever sent one unasked, the fix costs nothing. Ask first, and treat no answer as a no.
unsolicited-nudes-cyberflashing-law-indi.hg:
Socho, Indore ki ek 21 saal ki ladki Instagram pe handmade earrings bechti hai. Aadhi raat ke kareeb ek aise account se message request aati hai jis pe ek bhi post nahi hai: kisi anjaan aadmi ke body ki explicit photo, aur saath mein sawaal ki use pasand aayi ya nahi. Agli subah uski dost hans deti hai aur kehti hai ki yeh toh sabke saath hota hai, bas block kar de.

Yeh itne logon ke saath hota hai, yahi toh problem hai, yeh koi bahana nahi hai. Iska ek naam hai, cyberflashing: kisi ko sexual images bhejna jisne maangi hi nahi. Indian law mein is naam ka koi offence nahi hai, aur zaroorat bhi nahi hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Kya bina maange nude bhejna sach mein crime hai?

Haan. Information Technology Act ka Section 67 electronic form mein obscene material bhejne pe first conviction mein teen saal tak ki jail aur Rs 5 lakh tak ka fine lagata hai. Section 67A sexually explicit material ke liye hai aur paanch saal aur Rs 10 lakh tak jaata hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Dono mein se kaun sa lagega, yeh is pe depend karta hai ki image ya clip mein kya dikh raha hai.

Do baatein kaam ki hain. Yeh sections gender-neutral hain: agar kisi aadmi ko explicit image bheji jaaye, chahe aadmi ne bheji ho ya aurat ne, toh woh utna hi covered hai jitni koi aurat. Aur yeh obscenity law hain: yeh poochte hain ki material kya hai, yeh nahi ki tumne maanga tha ya nahi. Tumhari complaint "obscene material" ke heading ke neeche jaayegi, aur woh heading yeh nahi batata ki tumhare saath kya kiya gaya.

Jab koi aadmi aisi image kisi aurat ko bhejta hai, toh Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) bhi relevant ho sakti hai: Section 75 kisi aadmi dwara aurat ke sexual harassment pe teen saal tak ki saza deta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh section lagega ya nahi, yeh police aur court tay karenge.

Agar receiver 18 se kam umar ka hai, toh law use child maanta hai: POCSO ke hisaab se 18 se kam ka har insaan child hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Kisi bharosemand adult ko batao, ya Child Helpline 1098 pe call karo.

## Jis pal yeh aaye, mujhe kya karna chahiye?

1. **Reply mat karo.** Na gusse mein, na mazaak mein. Sender ko aksar bas ek reaction hi chahiye hota hai.
2. **Kaun aur kab, yeh save karo.** Sender ki profile, username ya phone number ka screenshot lo, aur message ka bhi, date aur time ke saath. Account kuch minute mein rename ya delete ho sakta hai.
3. **Pehle app ke andar report karo, phir block.** Chat ke andar se ki gayi report ke saath message bhi platform tak jaata hai. Pehle block ya delete kar diya, toh attach karne ko shayad kuch bache hi nahi.
4. **App ke bahar bhi report karo.** Cyber crime helpline 1930 pe call karo, ya cybercrime.gov.in pe file karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

Evidence apne paas rakho; use ghumao mat. Image ko kisi group mein forward karna, ya sender ko sharminda karne ke liye post karna, khud wahi material aage bhejna maana ja sakta hai, aur Section 67 isi ko punish karta hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

## Yeh colleague ya boss ne bheja hai: ab kya badalta hai?

Ek darwaza aur khul jaata hai, aur ek deadline lag jaati hai.

"Showing pornography" 1997 ke Supreme Court ke Vishaka guidelines se hi workplace pe sexual harassment ki definition ka hissa hai [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, yaani POSH Act, ne un guidelines ko kanoon bana diya [[pib-law-posh-act-gazette-2013]]. Employers ko Internal Complaints Committee banani hoti hai; jin workplaces mein das se kam workers hain, aur jo complaints khud employer ke khilaaf hain, woh district ki Local Committee ke paas jaati hain. Complaint likhit mein honi chahiye, incident ke teen mahine ke andar, aur inquiry 90 din mein khatam honi chahiye [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Sarkar ka SHe-Box portal yeh complaints online leta hai [[shebox]].

Sirf isliye is raaste ko mat chhodo ki image raat ko tumhare personal phone pe aayi thi. Act ke hisaab se workplace office ki building se aage tak jaata hai: kaam ke silsile mein jahan jaana pade woh jagah, aur employer ka diya hua transport bhi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Jo aadmi tumhara appraisal decide karta hai, woh office hours ke baad anjaan nahi ban jaata. Complaint file karo aur faisla committee ko karne do; police ka raasta saath mein khula rehta hai.

Limit yeh hai: POSH Act sirf women ko protect karta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Jis aadmi ko colleague ne explicit images bheji hain, uske paas IT Act aur employer ke conduct rules hain, yeh committee nahi.

## Kya report karne se kuch hoga?

Har darwaze se alag cheez milti hai.

**Platform sabse tez hai.** Report hua account restrict ya remove ho sakta hai, aur IT Amendment Rules, 2026 ke under platforms ko user ki grievance saat din mein resolve karni hoti hai, pehle 15 din the. Do ghante wala takedown rule complaint karne wale ki apni intimate images ke liye hai, sender ki image ke liye nahi [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

**Case police station se shuru hota hai.** Portal pe ki gayi complaint ek record hai, FIR nahi. Koi bhi station cognizable offence ko record karega, chahe woh kahin bhi hua ho, aur aurat ki sexual harassment ki complaint woman officer hi record karegi. Section 67 mein teen saal ki saza hai, isliye police Deputy Superintendent ki permission lekar register karne se pehle 14 din tak ki preliminary enquiry kar sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

**Courts dheere chalte hain.** 2024 mein poore India mein police ne Section 67 ke under 2,914 aur Section 67A ke under 2,197 cases register kiye. Bina maange bheje gaye nudes in totals ka ek aisa hissa hain jo gina hi nahi jaata, kyunki kisi section ka naam cyberflashing nahi hai. 2024 mein IT Act ke obscenity sections ke 19,731 cases courts ke saamne the; unme se 601 mein conviction hui aur 94.7% saal ke end tak pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Criminal case ho sakta hai, aur sabse mazboot tab hota hai jab sender pehchana ja sake: classmate, padosi, colleague.

## Ise sahi naam se bulana kyun zaroori hai

In images ke liye jo slang chalta hai, woh mazaak jaisa sunne ke liye hi bana hai. Woh is harkat ko badtameezi ke khaate mein daal deta hai aur saara kaam receiver pe chhod deta hai: hans do, block karo, itna serious mat lo. Jagah badal do toh koi nahi hansta us aadmi pe jo bus stop pe kisi anjaan ke saamne khud ko expose karta hai.

> Phone bus stop ko hata deta hai. Harkat ko nahi hatata.

Courts pehle bhi shabd badal chuke hain. 2023 mein Supreme Court ki gender stereotypes wali handbook ne judges se kaha ki "eve teasing" ki jagah "street sexual harassment" likhein [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Purana phrase ek offence ko timepass jaisa bana deta tha.

Bina maange bheji gayi explicit image sexual harassment hai, jo camera aur send button se kiya gaya hai. Aise kaho, toh "block karo aur aage badho" kai options mein se ek ban jaata hai. Block karna ek sahi choice hai. Complaint karna bhi.

Aur agar tumne kabhi kisi ko bina pooche aisi image bheji hai, toh sudhaar free hai. Pehle poocho, aur jawab na aaye toh use na hi samjho.

video-call-sextortion-scam-playbook.en:
Consider this situation. A 27-year-old in Nagpur accepts a friend request from a profile full of a young woman's photos. A few messages later, the profile video-calls him. He picks up. For a few seconds the screen shows an explicit clip, and his own face sits in the small window in the corner. The call drops. Minutes later a message arrives with a recording, an amount and a threat: pay, or this goes to everyone on your friends list. Police who have caught these gangs describe the same method: a fake profile posing as a woman, a video call that is recorded, then blackmail [[bhaskar-alwar-sextortion-2021]]. It runs on one thing above all: silence. A senior Maharashtra Cyber police officer estimated in 2022 that fewer than 0.5% of sextortion cases in India are registered as FIRs [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]].

## Minute one: the call is already being recorded

The trap is set before the phone rings. The profile is fake, and the video call exists for one purpose: to be recorded and used for blackmail [[bhaskar-alwar-sextortion-2021]]. Whatever the screen shows, the gang is capturing the person who answers.

That is the whole trick. In the situation above, he did nothing except pick up. A recording that puts his face next to an explicit clip is enough to build a threat to send the video to his friends and family.

Learn to recognise the first minute: a video call from a profile you have barely spoken to, a call that ends in seconds, a message straight after. Answering a call is not a crime. Blackmail is, and so is spreading sexual material. Under the IT Act, capturing or sharing images of a person's private parts without consent carries up to three years in jail or a fine of up to Rs 2 lakh. Publishing or sending sexually explicit material carries up to five years and a fine of up to Rs 10 lakh on first conviction, and up to seven years on a repeat [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. The law points at whoever records, threatens or spreads, not at the person on the screen.

## The second wave: the fake 'police' call

Paying does not buy an ending. Nobody can prove that a recording has been deleted, and a payment shows the gang that you can pay. In research cited by WeProtect Global Alliance, 70% of victims who ignored payment demands did not have their images distributed [[weprotect-web-of-deceit-2024]]. That is not a guarantee, as our myth-check on sextortion explains, but it points one way.

Then the cast can change. Police who have caught these gangs say the blackmail is sometimes followed by calls from people posing as police [[bhaskar-alwar-sextortion-2021]]. The new caller raises the stakes to a criminal case and names a price for making it disappear.

That price is the giveaway. A real police officer does not settle a case over the phone for a UPI payment.

## Organised gangs, and the minors among them

This is not the work of lone tricksters. In Rajasthan's Alwar district alone, police caught more than 60 sextortion gangs in the year to September 2021, and 13 of those caught were minors aged 14 to 16 [[bhaskar-alwar-sextortion-2021]]. The Maharashtra Cyber officer wrote in 2022 that such rackets operate from small towns in Rajasthan and Haryana [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]].

Two things follow. First, children are among those police have caught. Second, these are gangs documented by police, not the character of any district, caste or community. Most people in those districts have nothing to do with the racket. Turning a crime pattern into a regional stereotype does not stop the next call. Reporting is what puts a gang's numbers and accounts on record.

## Why victims stay silent, and who that silence protects

The same officer estimated that India sees more than 500 sextortion cases a day [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]]. Both his numbers are estimates, not measurements: India has no official sextortion count at all. But he named the reason for the silence plainly. The crime feeds on victims' shame and social stigma [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]].

Think about what the threat is aimed at: a marriage, a job, a parent's trust, your standing in the family WhatsApp group. Going to the police can feel like doing the gang's work for it. So paying quietly, or suffering quietly, can feel like the only choice, and the gang moves on to the next number.

The system does not make speaking up easy either. In 2024, police filed chargesheets in just 31.9% of the cyber crime cases they disposed of, and 90.9% of cyber crime cases before the courts were still pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Silence and slow justice protect the same people: the gangs, for whom every unreported call is a free rehearsal for the next one.

## What to do the moment the threat arrives

This is general information, not legal advice.

- End the call and do not call back. Do not reply to the demand, do not negotiate and do not pay.
- Before you block anyone, save the evidence: screenshots of the profile and chat, the call log, every number that called, and any UPI ID or bank details, including those of any later "officer".
- Call the national cyber crime helpline, 1930, or file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. Report the profile on the app as well.
- If someone claiming to be from the police calls about the video or asks for money, hang up. Then look up your local police station's number yourself and call it.
- If the recording appears online, report it to the platform. Since 20 February 2026, platforms must remove nude, sexual or morphed images of a person within two hours of that person's complaint, down from 24 hours [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Then tell one person you trust. The racket depends on you being alone with the threat; the moment someone else knows, it loses much of its power. If the fear feels like too much, call Tele-MANAS on 14416, the Health Ministry's free helpline that answers round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].
video-call-sextortion-scam-playbook.hg:
Ek situation socho. Nagpur ka ek 27 saal ka ladka ek friend request accept karta hai. Profile pe ek young ladki ki bahut saari photos hain. Do-chaar messages ke baad usi profile se video call aati hai. Woh utha leta hai. Kuch second tak screen pe ek explicit clip chalti hai, aur kone ki chhoti window mein uska apna chehra dikh raha hai. Call kat jaati hai. Kuch hi minute mein message aata hai: call ki recording, ek amount, aur ek dhamki. Paise bhejo, warna yeh video tumhari friend list mein sabke paas jayega. Aisi gangs pakadne wali police yahi tareeka batati hai: ladki ban ke chalayi gayi fake profile, video call jo record ho jaati hai, aur phir blackmail [[bhaskar-alwar-sextortion-2021]]. Yeh poora khel sabse zyada ek cheez pe chalta hai: chuppi. Maharashtra Cyber police ke ek senior officer ne 2022 mein andaaza lagaya tha ki India mein sextortion ke 0.5% se bhi kam cases mein FIR register hoti hai [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]].

## Pehla minute: call uthate hi recording shuru

Jaal phone bajne se pehle hi bichh chuka hota hai. Profile fake hoti hai, aur video call ka ek hi maksad hota hai: use record karke blackmail ke liye istemaal karna [[bhaskar-alwar-sextortion-2021]]. Screen pe jo bhi dikhe, gang call uthane wale ko record kar rahi hoti hai.

Bas itni si trick hai. Upar wali situation mein us ladke ne call uthane ke alawa kuch nahi kiya. Ek explicit clip ke bagal mein uska chehra, bas itni si recording kaafi hai yeh dhamki dene ke liye ki video uske doston aur ghar walon ko bhej diya jayega.

Pehla minute pehchaanna seekho: aisi profile se video call jisse theek se baat bhi nahi hui, call jo kuch second mein kat jaaye, aur uske turant baad message. Yaad rakho, call uthana crime nahi hai. Blackmail crime hai, aur sexual content failana bhi. IT Act ke under, kisi ke private parts ki images bina consent ke kheenchna ya share karna teen saal tak ki jail ya 2 lakh rupaye tak ke fine wala crime hai. Sexually explicit content publish karne ya bhejne pe pehli baar mein paanch saal tak ki jail aur 10 lakh rupaye tak ka fine hai, aur dobara karne pe saat saal tak ki jail [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Kanoon ki ungli us pe uthti hai jo record karta hai, dhamki deta hai ya video failata hai, us pe nahi jo screen pe dikh raha hai.

## Doosra round: nakli 'police' ka phone

Pay karne se kahani khatam nahi hoti. Koi saabit nahi kar sakta ki recording delete ho gayi, aur payment se gang ko pata chal jaata hai ki tum pay kar sakte ho. WeProtect Global Alliance ki batayi ek research mein, jin victims ne paison ki demand ko ignore kiya, unmein se 70% ki images aage distribute nahi hui [[weprotect-web-of-deceit-2024]]. Yeh guarantee nahi hai, jaisa humne sextortion myths wale article mein samjhaya hai, lekin ishara ek hi taraf hai.

Phir characters badal sakte hain. Aisi gangs pakadne wali police batati hai ki kai baar blackmail ke baad police wale ban ke phone aate hain [[bhaskar-alwar-sextortion-2021]]. Naya caller darr ko criminal case tak le jaata hai, aur problem "gayab" karne ki ek price bata deta hai.

Wahi price uski pol kholti hai. Asli police phone pe UPI payment le ke case band nahi karti.

## Organised gangs, aur unmein pakde gaye minors

Yeh akele-dukele thugon ka kaam nahi hai. Sirf Rajasthan ke Alwar district mein police ne September 2021 tak ke ek saal mein 60 se zyada sextortion gangs pakdi, aur pakde gaye logon mein 13 minors the, jinki umar 14 se 16 saal thi [[bhaskar-alwar-sextortion-2021]]. Maharashtra Cyber ke usi officer ne 2022 mein likha ki aise rackets Rajasthan aur Haryana ke chhote towns se chalte hain [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]].

Isse do baatein saaf hoti hain. Pehli, police ne jinhe pakda, unmein bachche bhi hain. Doosri, yeh police ki pakdi hui gangs hain, kisi district, caste ya community ki pehchaan nahi. Un districts ke zyadatar logon ka is racket se koi lena-dena nahi. Kisi area ko stereotype karne se agli call nahi rukti. Report karne se hi gang ke numbers aur accounts record pe aate hain.

## Victims chup kyun rehte hain, aur is chuppi ka fayda kise

Usi officer ka andaaza hai ki India mein roz sextortion ke 500 se zyada cases hote hain [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]]. Unke dono numbers andaaze hain, measurement nahi; India mein sextortion ka koi official count hai hi nahi. Lekin chuppi ki wajah unhone saaf batayi: yeh crime victims ki sharm aur social stigma pe palta hai [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]].

Socho, dhamki kis cheez pe vaar karti hai: shaadi, naukri, maa-baap ka bharosa, family WhatsApp group mein tumhari izzat. Police ke paas jaana aisa lagta hai jaise gang ka kaam khud kar rahe ho. Isliye chupchaap pay karna, ya chupchaap sehna, hi akela raasta lagta hai, aur gang agle number pe chali jaati hai.

System bhi bolna aasaan nahi banata. 2024 mein police ne jin cyber crime cases ko niptaya, unmein se sirf 31.9% mein chargesheet file hui, aur courts mein pahunche cyber crime ke 90.9% cases saal ke end tak pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Chuppi aur dheema insaaf, dono ka fayda ek ko hi milta hai: gang ko. Uske liye har unreported call agli call ki free rehearsal hai.

## Dhamki aate hi kya karein

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

- Call kaato aur wapas call mat karo. Demand ka reply mat karo, bargain mat karo, aur pay mat karo.
- Kisi ko block karne se pehle saboot save karo: profile aur chat ke screenshots, call log, call karne wala har number, aur koi bhi UPI ID ya bank details, baad mein phone karne wale kisi "officer" ki bhi.
- National cyber crime helpline 1930 pe call karo, ya cybercrime.gov.in pe complaint file karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. App pe bhi profile report karo.
- Agar koi khud ko police bata ke video ke baare mein phone kare ya paise maange, toh phone kaat do. Phir apne local police station ka number khud dhoondo aur wahan call karo.
- Agar recording online aa jaaye, toh platform pe report karo. 20 February 2026 se platforms ko kisi insaan ki nude, sexual ya morphed images uski complaint ke do ghante ke andar hatani hoti hain; pehle yeh time 24 ghante tha [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Phir ek bharosemand insaan ko batao. Yeh poora racket is baat pe tika hai ki tum dhamki ke saath akele raho; jaise hi kisi aur ko pata chalta hai, dhamki ki bahut si taakat khatam ho jaati hai. Agar darr bardasht se bahar lage, toh Tele-MANAS ko 14416 pe call karo. Yeh Health Ministry ki free helpline hai jo din-raat chalti hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

where-online-sexual-crimes-are-registere.en:
In 2024, police in Uttar Pradesh registered 633 cyber crimes in which they recorded sexual exploitation as the motive, more than any other state. Maharashtra came next with 544. Together the two held 37% of India's 3,190 such cases, and Rajasthan (280) and Kerala (225) followed [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Shade those states dark on a map and the obvious reading is that online sexual crime is worst there. The numbers cannot carry that reading, and the National Crime Records Bureau, which publishes them, says so itself. A state table counts FIRs. It shows where victims managed to report and where police wrote it down, as much as where crime happened.

## The states that register the most

The 3,190 cases are a small slice of India's cyber crime record. Police registered 1,01,928 cyber crimes in 2024. Fraud was the motive in 73,987 of them (72.6%), sexual exploitation in 3.1% and extortion in 2,536 [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]].

"Motive" is the label a police officer writes at registration. A video-call sextortion case can be recorded as extortion or fraud instead of sexual exploitation, so the 3,190 misses an unknown number of sexual crimes filed under other motives [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]].

Size matters too. Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra are among India's most populous states, so their high counts partly reflect how many people live there. Kerala, with a far smaller population, still made the top four.

## Rate against count: Telangana's 71.1

Rates divide by population, and they redraw the map. Telangana registered 27,230 cyber crimes in 2024, the highest rate of any state at 71.1 per lakh people [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The national rate was 7.3 [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. So Telangana recorded nearly ten times the national rate, and more than a quarter of all of India's cyber crime FIRs.

Yet Telangana is not among the four states with the most sexual-exploitation cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Almost all of its cyber crime falls under other motives. The same state had the second-highest rate of registered crimes against women in 2024, 128.6 per lakh women, behind only Delhi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

A state that leads tables for very different crimes may simply have more crime. It may also have police stations and online systems that turn more complaints into FIRs. The table cannot tell you which.

## NCRB's own warning about this map

The 2024 edition of *Crime in India* carries a "word of caution" for anyone who reads it [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]:

> "'Rise in crime' and 'increase in registration of crime by police' are clearly two different things."

The same note says a rise in a state's figures may come from "citizen centric police initiatives, like launching of e-FIR facility or women Helpdesks". It says more crime registered in a city "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe" than a city with less, and that comparing states on these figures alone "will be too simplistic and is best avoided" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

For online crime the warning matters even more. Reporting depends on knowing that 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in exist, on having the confidence to use them, and on reaching a police station that will register an online complaint. Each of those can differ from one state to the next, and the table records the result.

## The victim's state, the caller's state

Online crime also splits the place where a case is registered from the place where the offender sits. Police in Rajasthan's Alwar district caught more than 60 sextortion gangs in the year to September 2021, and 13 of those caught were minors aged 14 to 16 [[bhaskar-alwar-sextortion-2021]]. A senior Maharashtra Cyber police officer wrote in 2022 that such rackets operate from places such as Mewat, Bharatpur and Alwar in Rajasthan and Haryana [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]].

So a student in Pune or a shopkeeper in Patna may be reporting a caller several states away. Their FIR, if there is one, is counted where it was registered. These gangs are documented by police. They are not the character of any district or community, and most people in those places have nothing to do with them.

The law no longer lets distance become an excuse. Under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), anyone can report a cognizable offence at any police station "irrespective of the area where the offence is committed", known as a Zero FIR, or by electronic communication, an e-FIR that must be signed within three days. The victim must get a copy of the FIR free of cost [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## What your state's number may hide

A complaint is not an FIR. Complaints on the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal reached 22.68 lakh in 2024 [[ls-uq432-2025]], while police registered 1,01,928 cyber crime FIRs [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Most portal complaints concern financial fraud, and not every complaint describes a crime, but the gap shows how much never enters NCRB's tables.

The law also allows a pause. The IT Act's offences involving sexual images carry maximum sentences of three to five years on a first conviction [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. For offences in that range, Section 173(3) BNSS lets police, with a Deputy Superintendent's permission, hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days before registering [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A complaint that stops at that stage never enters the state's count.

And many victims never come forward. The same Maharashtra officer estimated in 2022 that fewer than 0.5% of sextortion cases in India are registered as FIRs. It is an estimate, not a measurement [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]].

So a low number for your state may mean less crime. It may also mean victims who did not know where to go, complaints that never became FIRs, or cases filed under another motive. A high number may partly reflect police who write things down. The better question is not "which state is worst?" but "where can a victim get heard?" Anyone who needs to report can call 1930 or use cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]], and walk into the nearest police station, wherever the caller is. This is general information, not legal advice.
where-online-sexual-crimes-are-registere.hg:
2024 mein Uttar Pradesh ki police ne 633 aise cyber crimes register kiye jinmein motive sexual exploitation likha gaya, kisi bhi aur state se zyada. Maharashtra 544 ke saath doosre number pe tha. Dono milke India ke aise 3,190 cases ka 37% the, aur unke baad Rajasthan (280) aur Kerala (225) aaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Map pe in states ko gehre rang se bhar do, toh seedhi si baat yeh lagegi ki online sexual crime sabse zyada yahin hai. Yeh numbers us baat ka bojh nahi utha sakte, aur inhe chhaapne wala National Crime Records Bureau khud yeh kehta hai. State table FIRs ginti hai. Woh utna hi yeh dikhati hai ki victims kahan report kar paaye aur police ne kahan likha, jitna yeh ki crime kahan hua.

## Sabse zyada register karne wale states

Yeh 3,190 cases India ke cyber crime record ka chhota sa hissa hain. 2024 mein police ne 1,01,928 cyber crimes register kiye. Inmein se 73,987 (72.6%) mein motive fraud tha, 3.1% mein sexual exploitation, aur 2,536 mein extortion [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]].

"Motive" woh label hai jo police officer registration ke waqt likhta hai. Video-call sextortion ka case sexual exploitation ki jagah extortion ya fraud mein bhi darj ho sakta hai, isliye 3,190 ki ginti mein woh sexual crimes chhoot jaate hain jo doosre motives mein file hue, aur unki ginti kisi ko nahi pata [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]].

Size ka bhi farq padta hai. Uttar Pradesh aur Maharashtra India ke sabse zyada aabaadi wale states mein se hain, toh unke bade numbers ka kuch hissa sirf wahan rehne wale logon ki ginti se aata hai. Kerala ki aabaadi kahin kam hai, phir bhi woh top four mein aaya.

## Count banaam rate: Telangana ka 71.1

Rate numbers ko aabaadi se divide karta hai, aur isse map badal jaata hai. 2024 mein Telangana ne 27,230 cyber crimes register kiye, aur 71.1 per lakh logon ke saath uska rate kisi bhi state se zyada tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. National rate 7.3 tha [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Yaani Telangana ka rate national rate ka lagbhag das guna tha, aur India ki saari cyber crime FIRs ka ek-chauthai se zyada hissa isi ek state se aaya.

Phir bhi Telangana un chaar states mein nahi hai jahan sexual exploitation ke sabse zyada cases hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Uska lagbhag saara cyber crime doosre motives mein aata hai. Isi state mein 2024 mein auraton ke khilaaf registered crime ka rate desh mein doosre number pe tha, 128.6 per lakh auratein, sirf Delhi se peeche [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Jo state bilkul alag-alag crimes ki tables mein upar ho, wahan sach mein zyada crime ho sakta hai. Ya wahan ke police stations aur online systems zyada complaints ko FIR mein badalte ho sakte hain. Table yeh nahi bata sakti ki in dono mein se kya sach hai.

## Is map pe NCRB ki apni chetaavni

*Crime in India* ke 2024 edition mein har padhne wale ke liye ek "word of caution" hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]:

> "'Rise in crime' and 'increase in registration of crime by police' are clearly two different things."

Yaani crime ka badhna aur police ka zyada crime register karna, do alag baatein hain. Usi note mein likha hai ki kisi state ke numbers ka badhna "citizen centric police initiatives, like launching of e-FIR facility or women Helpdesks" se bhi ho sakta hai. Note kehta hai ki kisi city mein zyada registered crime "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe", yaani kam crime wali city se woh zyada unsafe hai, iska saboot nahi. Aur sirf in figures pe states ki tulna karna "will be too simplistic and is best avoided" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

Online crime ke liye yeh chetaavni aur bhi zaroori hai. Reporting is pe tiki hai ki logon ko 1930 aur cybercrime.gov.in ke baare mein pata ho, unhe use karne ki himmat ho, aur woh aise police station tak pahunch paayein jo online complaint register kare. Yeh sab ek state se doosre state mein alag ho sakta hai, aur table bas uska nateeja darj karti hai.

## Victim ka state, caller ka state

Online crime mein woh jagah jahan case register hota hai, aur woh jagah jahan offender baitha hai, alag ho jaati hain. Rajasthan ke Alwar district ki police ne September 2021 tak ke ek saal mein 60 se zyada sextortion gangs pakdi, aur pakde gaye logon mein 13 minors the, jinki umar 14 se 16 saal thi [[bhaskar-alwar-sextortion-2021]]. Maharashtra Cyber police ke ek senior officer ne 2022 mein likha ki aise rackets Rajasthan aur Haryana mein Mewat, Bharatpur aur Alwar jaisi jagahon se chalte hain [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]].

Toh Pune ka koi student ya Patna ka koi dukaandaar kai states door baithe caller ki report kar raha ho sakta hai. Uski FIR, agar hui, toh wahin gini jaati hai jahan register hui. Yeh gangs police ke records mein darj hain. Yeh kisi district ya community ki pehchaan nahi hain, aur un jagahon ke zyadatar logon ka inse koi lena-dena nahi.

Kanoon ab doori ko bahaana nahi banne deta. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 173 ke tahat koi bhi cognizable offence ki report kisi bhi police station pe kar sakta hai, "irrespective of the area where the offence is committed", yaani crime kahin bhi hua ho. Ise Zero FIR kehte hain. Report electronic tareeke se bhi ho sakti hai, yaani e-FIR, jis pe teen din ke andar sign karna hota hai. Victim ko FIR ki copy free mein milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Tumhare state ka number kya chhupa sakta hai

Complaint aur FIR ek cheez nahi hain. 2024 mein National Cybercrime Reporting Portal pe complaints 22.68 lakh tak pahunchi [[ls-uq432-2025]], jabki police ne 1,01,928 cyber crime FIRs register ki [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Portal ki zyadatar complaints financial fraud ki hoti hain, aur har complaint crime nahi hoti, lekin yeh gap dikhata hai ki kitna kuch NCRB ke tables tak pahunchta hi nahi.

Kanoon khud ek rukaawat ki ijaazat deta hai. Sexual images se jude IT Act ke offences mein pehli baar ki saza teen se paanch saal tak hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Is range ke offences ke liye BNSS ka Section 173(3) police ko, Deputy Superintendent ki permission se, FIR register karne se pehle 14 din tak preliminary enquiry karne deta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo complaint is stage pe ruk jaaye, woh state ki ginti mein kabhi aati hi nahi.

Aur bahut se victims kabhi saamne aate hi nahi. Maharashtra ke usi officer ne 2022 mein andaaza lagaya tha ki India mein sextortion ke 0.5% se bhi kam cases mein FIR register hoti hai. Yeh ek andaaza hai, naapa hua number nahi [[toi-yadav-sextortion-oped-2022]].

Toh agar tumhare state ka number kam hai, toh iska matlab kam crime ho sakta hai. Iska matlab yeh bhi ho sakta hai ki victims ko pata nahi tha kahan jaayein, complaints FIR nahi bani, ya cases kisi aur motive mein file hue. Zyada number ka kuch hissa aisi police se bhi aa sakta hai jo cheezein likhti hai. Behtar sawaal yeh nahi ki "sabse bura state kaunsa hai?" balki yeh ki "victim ki sunwaai kahan ho sakti hai?" Jise report karna ho, woh 1930 pe call kar sakta hai ya cybercrime.gov.in use kar sakta hai [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]], aur sabse paas ke police station mein ja sakta hai, caller chahe kahin bhi ho. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.
